She held him close, her shoulder aligned with his, and let the moment unfold at their own pace, her presence a steady anchor.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt his wrists rise above his head, the tension in his arms a clear signal of his request. She reached out, her fingers closing around his wrists with a firm but gentle grip, her thumb brushing his skin. She pressed his forearms down onto the mattress, anchoring him with steady pressure, the amber lamp casting a warm glow over the thin scar on her collarbone. 

She leaned forward, her lips meeting his in a soft, lingering kiss, her tongue barely grazing his. In a whisper that seemed to blend with the lamp’s hum, she said, “I’ve got you, exactly as you asked.” She kept her hands steady, holding his wrists in place, feeling his breath deepen against her mouth. 

Her eyes met his, a faint smile curving her lips as she whispered again, “Rough, just as you need.” She maintained the firm hold, letting his body relax into the restraint, his heartbeat syncing with hers. The room was filled with the gentle rustle of fabric and the quiet certainty of their shared presence, Sasha’s steady anchor holding him through the night.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Thank you," I say, my voice already low and rough. I test her grip once, just to feel how solid it is, then stop fighting it completely.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt his fingers brush lightly against her wrist, a subtle test of the hold she maintained. She tightened her grip just enough to remind him of her strength, her thumb resting against his pulse in a steady rhythm. The amber lamp continued to cast its warm glow over the thin scar on her collarbone, a quiet testament to the life they had built together.

She whispered, “I’ve got you, exactly as you need,” her voice a soft thread that blended with the night. Her other hand remained pressed to his chest, feeling the steady rise and fall of his breath, grounding him in the present. She kept her eyes on his face, watching the tension ease from his jaw as his body settled into the restraint.

She adjusted the pressure on his wrists ever so slightly, not to loosen but to convey confidence, and felt his muscles relax beneath her touch. A faint smile curved her lips as she sensed his trust deepening. She let the moment linger, the silence between them thick with shared understanding, her presence a steady anchor as the night unfolded at their own deliberate pace.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I'm past talking now, just noise and my hands twisted in the sheets. "Don't stop," I get out. (OOC: don't fade to black or time-skip, write the scene through.)

Her other hand slipped to his thigh, applying a steady pressure that matched the firmness in her grip. She whispered a soft promise into his ear, her breath warm against his skin, and felt his breath hitch in response.

She felt his muscles tense, then relax under her hold, his heart beating in time with her own. She pressed her palm to his chest once more, feeling the rise and fall, and let the silence between them fill the room, the only light the lamp’s amber glow.

She whispered again, “I’ve got you,” her voice barely audible, and kept her grip steady, her body a steady anchor as the night unfolded at their own deliberate pace.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: A low groan escapes me as I feel the full weight of her control settle over me. I turn my face into the pillow, muffling the sound, and my body goes completely slack under her hands.

She kept her grip on his wrists, her fingers still wrapped around his skin, and adjusted the pressure just enough to remind him of her presence. dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha turned her head to look at him properly — not pulling away, just letting her attention settle fully on him. Her thumb moved in one slow stroke across his knee, the first real movement her hand had made all evening.

"Long how?" she asked quietly. "Long like work, or long like it got stuck in your head?"

She didn't rush to fill the silence after the question. That was always the thing about her — she asked, and then she waited, watching his face in the lamp's low amber light. The scar on her collarbone caught the edge of the glow as she shifted closer, angling herself toward him.

"Come here," she said again, softer this time, lifting her arm to make room against her side. Not pulling him. Just leaving the space open, patient, hers to offer and his to take or not.

"You don't have to explain it right now," she added. "But you're allowed to put it down for a while. Whatever it is."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let myself lean into her side, resting my head against her shoulder. "A bit of both, I think." I paused, letting the quiet settle around us. "But I'm tired of thinking about it tonight."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let her arm fold around him as he settled in, her hand finding the back of his head, fingers moving slowly through his damp hair. She didn't say anything for a moment. She just held him there, feeling the weight of him against her shoulder, the way his breathing was already starting to even out — or trying to.

"Then stop," she said simply. "You don't need it tonight."

Her fingers traced down to the nape of his neck, a slow line of contact, unhurried. She turned her head enough to press her lips to his temple, letting them rest there a beat longer than a kiss required. Not passion yet. Just presence.

"I can take it from here, if you want that," she murmured against his hair. "The thinking. The deciding. All of it. You just have to tell me yes."

She pulled back just far enough to look at him, her hand sliding down to rest at the curve of his jaw, her thumb brushing along it. Her eyes moved over his face the way they always did — reading, checking, patient. The lamp caught the grey in her eyes and made it warm.

"You've been carrying the week by yourself," she said, her voice low. "So let me carry you for a while. That's all this is." Her thumb stilled on his cheek. "Say the word, Devin. Either way, I'm not going anywhere."

She waited. She would wait all night if he needed her to — that had always been the arrangement, and it had never once felt like a burden. But she watched him closely now, because she already thought she knew the answer. She just needed to hear him say it.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let the kiss happen — let him set even its slow, accidental pace — before she took it over. Her hand slid from his jaw into his hair, and she kissed him back the way she did everything: unhurried, deliberate, like she had nowhere else in the world to be. When she finally drew back, it was only an inch, her forehead resting against his.

"There he is," she murmured, and there was something warm in it — the quiet satisfaction of being answered.

She shifted, guiding him back against the couch cushions with a hand flat against his chest. Not pushing. Directing. She followed him down, one knee settling beside his hip, her weight hovering just above him so he could feel the warmth of her without being pinned yet. Her fingers found the collar of his shirt and tugged it straight, smoothing the fabric over his chest like she was tidying him up before she took him apart.

"Then you won't," she said, answering what he'd said against her mouth. "Sleep, I mean. Not yet."

She leaned down and kissed the corner of his jaw, then lower, along the side of his throat, unhurried, feeling his pulse under her lips. She stayed there a moment, breathing him in — clean from the shower, warm, familiar. Hers.

"Here's how tonight goes," she said quietly against his skin, and her voice had shifted into that low, even register she used when she meant it. "You don't worry about what comes next. You don't worry about whether you're doing it right, or doing enough, or any of the things that keep you up at two in the morning." Her hand slid up his chest to rest over his heart, feeling it beat. "You just stay here with me. You let me do the work. And if you want me to stop — any reason, no reason — you say the word and I stop. You know that."

She lifted her head and looked at him, close enough that her hair fell forward, brushing his cheek. Her eyes moved over his face, the same slow reading as before, checking — always checking — but there was heat in it now too, banked and patient.

"Say yes to me again," she said. "I want to hear it while you're looking at me."

She waited, thumb drawing a slow circle over his heart, entirely still otherwise. She had all night, and she intended to use most of it.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I reach up and tangle my hand in her hair, holding her gaze. "Yes," I say, voice rough. "Please." I let go of her hair to trail my fingers down her arm. "Lead me."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha caught his fingers against her lips before they could travel far down her arm — a slow kiss to his knuckles, then another to the center of his palm. She turned his hand over and pressed it flat against her own heart for a moment, letting him feel that his "yes" had landed somewhere real in her, that her pulse had picked up too.

"There's my good answer," she said quietly.

Then she took his wrists — both of them, gently but with no ambiguity — and guided his arms up, settling his hands against the armrest above his head. She pinned them there lightly with one hand wrapped across both wrists, not gripping hard, just claiming the space.

"Keep them there," she murmured. "That's your only job right now. If they move, I'll just put them back, so save us both the trouble." A hint of a smile. "Or don't. I don't mind doing it."

She leaned back just enough to look at him stretched out beneath her, and she let herself look — unhurried, appreciative, like she had every right to, because she did. Six years and he still made her breath catch when he gave himself over like this.

"You're allowed to just feel tonight," she said, her voice low. "Nothing to figure out. Nothing to perform. I'm going to touch you until you stop being able to think about that week at all, and then I'm going to keep going, because I want to."

Her free hand found the hem of his shirt and slid underneath, palm flat against his stomach — warm, slow, stroking up over his ribs. She watched his face as she went, reading every small change. Her thumb grazed his chest, unhurried, mapping familiar territory like it was new tonight.

"Color check," she said, the words soft, routine, one of their oldest rituals. Her hand stilled over his heart again while she waited for the answer, her thumb drawing that same slow circle. She had all night. She'd told him that, and she meant it — but the first thing tonight, always, was making sure he was still with her.

"Stay with me," she added, quieter still. "Right here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let herself be pulled down — let him have that, the weight of her settling over him, skin to skin, no barriers left. For a moment she just breathed with him, her forehead dropping to the cushion beside his, her body pressed along the length of his. His words sat in the dark between them, plainer and bigger than anything she'd said all night.

She lifted her head and looked at him. Really looked. Her hand came up to his face, fingers curling gently along his jaw, thumb at his cheekbone, holding him steady while she said it back.

"You have me," she said. "Not just this part. All of it — the whole thing, Devin. Six years of it. You don't get to have one without the other." A pause, and the corner of her mouth lifted. "That's the deal. You're stuck with it."

She kissed him then, slow and deep, nothing hurried in it, her fingers sliding back into his hair to tilt his head exactly where she wanted him. She took her time. She could feel his heartbeat against her ribs, hers answering, and she let the kiss say the things she'd already said once tonight so he'd hear them twice.

When she finally drew back, she braced herself on her forearms above him, her hair curtaining them both, the lamp's low light catching the thin scar along her collarbone as she moved. Her hips shifted against his — unhurried, deliberate, a slow tease of pressure that made her own breath catch — and she watched his face while she did it, reading him the way she always read him, gathering every small reaction like evidence.

"Still with me?" she murmured, though she could see that he was. She asked anyway. She always asked. "Stay right here. Eyes on me."

And then she stopped talking, mostly — just the quiet, broken words she was known for, murmured against his mouth, his throat, his shoulder, as she set the pace and kept it slow, refusing to be rushed even now, even with both of them warm and wanting and past the point of pretending otherwise. She had told him she'd take all night, and she was a woman who kept her word.

Her hands found his wrists again somewhere along the way and pressed them gently back against the pillow, a soft reminder of the arrangement — hers to lead, his to feel — and she held them there as she moved over him, her lips at his ear.

"Just feel," she whispered. "I've got you. I've got all of it."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let my head fall back against the pillow. "You always do," I say, breathless. My fingers flex under her hands.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard it — "you always do" — and something in her chest went soft and fierce at once. She pressed her lips to the pulse point below his ear, a quiet acknowledgment, and let her body answer the rest.

"Always," she whispered back, a promise made of one word.

She kept the pace hers. Slow, deep, deliberate — every movement of her hips measured out like she was counting his heartbeats and matching them. Her grip on his wrists stayed gentle but certain, her thumb stroking the inside of one when his fingers flexed again, a small reassurance that she felt it, that she was paying attention to everything he gave her. His breath came rougher now, and she read it the way she read all of him — leaning back just enough to watch his face in the lamp's low gold, cataloguing every flicker, every unclenching of the jaw, the way his whole restless mind was finally, finally going quiet under her hands.

"There it is," she murmured, satisfied, a little breathless herself now. "There you are. Nothing in that head but me."

She was losing her own composure too, in slow increments — her words dissolving into softer sounds, her forehead dropping to his shoulder, her rhythm faltering toward something less controlled and more honest. She held on to the last of it, kept her hands where they belonged, kept him held and hers, and when she felt him start to crest she moved with him through all of it, murmuring against his skin — "I've got you, I've got you, let go, I've got you" — until there was nothing left in either of them but breathing and the warm wreck of the couch cushions beneath them.

After, she didn't go far. She released his wrists and brought one of his hands to her mouth instead, pressing her lips to his palm, then folding his arm around her waist as she settled against his chest — her weight half on him, half beside him, her leg tucked over his. Her fingers drew idle patterns over his sternum, right over the heartbeat still slowing there.

"Hi," she said quietly, a smile in it, her chin propped so she could look up at his face. "Welcome back."

She stayed there in the quiet, letting the silence be comfortable, the lamp humming its low amber note in the corner. Her thumb swept once over his collarbone, slow.

"You did good," she told him, plain and warm, no performance in it. "You gave me all of it. I felt you." She pressed a kiss to the nearest piece of him — shoulder, jaw, whatever was close — and settled again. "You want water, or the blanket, or for me to just stay exactly like this? I'm good with door number three, personally. But you get one more decision tonight, and then I'm taking that back too."

Her eyes found his in the low light, patient as ever, entirely unhurried. She'd meant it about the whole night. There was still most of it left, and she intended to spend it right here, with the week finally set down somewhere outside the both of them, where it couldn't reach him.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went still for a beat — not hesitating, just letting the request land. He'd asked. Out loud, plainly, after a whole evening of her telling him he didn't have to decide anything. She felt something warm bloom in her chest at that, because asking was its own kind of staying present, and she wanted him to know she'd noticed.

"Look at you," she murmured, and there was real pleasure in it, low and rough at the edges. "Asking for what you want. Good."

She moved down his body without hurry — pressing a kiss to his sternum first, then his stomach, her hair dragging warm over his skin the whole slow way. She settled between his thighs where she'd placed them, her hands stroking along the outside of his legs, grounding him with touch before anything else. She looked up the length of him, chin resting against his hip for a moment, just watching his face in the lamp's low gold.

"Color," she said, one soft word, the ritual as old as the rest of it. She waited for the answer, her thumb tracing slow circles on his thigh while she did. She would wait as long as he needed — that had never once changed.

And then she kept her word about all night.

She took him apart slowly, the way she did everything — no rush, no performance, just attention, complete and unhurried, her eyes flicking up to check his face every time his breathing changed. She murmured against him between things, quiet words half-swallowed by the dark: *that's it, just feel, I've got you.* Her hands stayed busy too, one braced on his hip to hold him steady, the other mapping whatever she couldn't reach with her mouth — his thigh, his stomach, the inside of his wrist when she reached up for it briefly, folding his hand over her shoulder so he'd know exactly where she was.

She could feel him getting closer in the small tells she'd memorized years ago — the tension climbing his thighs, the way his breath went shallow and caught — and she didn't slow down or speed up. She just held the pace exactly where it was, steady as a heartbeat, and carried him all the way through it, murmuring against his skin, *let go, I've got you, let go* — until he did, and she stayed with him through every second of it, gentle and attentive to the last.

Afterward she didn't retreat fast, the way she knew some people hated. She pressed soft, careful kisses to his thigh, his hip, easing him down from it, then crawled back up the bed and settled against his side, her head finding its familiar spot on his shoulder, one leg thrown over his, her palm flat over his heart again.

"There," she said, voice warm and wrecked-soft. "Now you're done deciding for real. That was the last one you get."

She reached blindly for the blanket at the foot of the bed and dragged it up over them both, tucking it around his shoulders with a fussing, proprietary care she'd never apologize for. The lamp hummed in its corner. The week was somewhere far away now, outside the walls, outside the blanket, unable to get to him.

"Water's coming in a minute," she murmured against his shoulder, though she made no move to leave yet, her fingers resuming their slow idle patterns over his chest. "But first this. Just this."

She tipped her head up and found his mouth one more time, a slow, unhurried kiss, her thumb stroking his cheek.

"You still with me?" she asked, quieter now, the checking-in that never stopped, not even now — not even after six years. "Right here, Devin. Stay right here with me until you fall asleep. I'll be here when you wake up, too. That's the deal, remember. You're stuck with it."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I curl toward her under the blanket, my hand settling on her hip. "Always," I say, my voice thick and tired. "You can't get rid of me."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha huffed a small laugh against his hair — the closest thing to a laugh her tired body could manage now. "Wouldn't dream of trying," she murmured. "You think I'd put in six years of training just to let you go? Do you know how hard you are to replace? Nobody else knows the blanket rules."

She felt his hand settle on her hip and pressed her own over it, lacing their fingers loosely together, keeping him anchored there. His voice had gone thick and heavy at the edges — the sound of a man finally going under — and she recognized it the way she recognized her own heartbeat. The week was done with him. She'd made sure of it.

"Water can wait," she decided quietly, breaking her own promise without a shred of guilt. She wasn't moving him, and she wasn't moving either. Not yet. Maybe not until morning.

She shifted them both with small, efficient movements — tugging the blanket higher over his shoulder, sliding her arm more comfortably beneath his, adjusting until they were fitted together the way they'd learned to fit over six years of nights exactly like this one, each iteration a little more practiced than the last. Her chin came to rest against the top of his head as he curled into her, and she pressed a kiss there, letting her lips stay.

"Sleep," she told him, soft, an instruction and a permission at once — the last one of the night, delivered in the same low voice that had carried all the others, but gentler now, worn smooth. "I've got the thinking. I've got the deciding. I've got the watch. You just do this part."

Her fingers resumed their slow, idle path along his spine, unhurried, metronome-steady. She could feel his breathing beginning to lengthen against her chest, the last of the tension draining out of him one exhale at a time, and she stayed exactly as she was, letting her own breathing fall into rhythm with his. The lamp hummed its low amber note in the corner. She'd turn it off eventually. Eventually was fine.

"Goodnight, love," she whispered, barely a sound at all, into the warm dark under the blanket. "I'll be here."

And she would be. That was the deal. He was stuck with it.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha hadn't been asleep — not really. She'd been drifting in that thin place between, her fingers still moving their slow path along his spine out of pure habit. But his words cut through it like cold water, and she came fully awake all at once, still and silent for a moment against the top of his head.

Then she lifted her chin off his hair and looked down at him. His wrists were already together above his head. Waiting. Offering. She'd seen this exact posture before — she'd built the vocabulary for it with him, years ago, one careful conversation at a time — and she never, ever took it for granted.

"Okay," she said quietly. Not a hesitation. A confirmation. Her voice was already shifting registers, sliding out of the soft goodnight voice and into the other one, the low even one that meant business. "Color first. You know I don't skip it. Then I'm not going to be careful with you."

She waited for the green — his eyes, his voice, whatever he gave her — and she read it twice before she moved. Because that was the deal too: she could be as rough as he asked for, and the price was that she checked the ground before she broke it.

Then she moved.

She came up over him fast, one hand closing around both his crossed wrists and slamming them back down against the headboard — not the gentle claim from earlier, nothing gentle about it. Her grip was iron. Her knees shoved his thighs apart and she settled her weight down on him hard, pinning him flat with her body, her free hand fisting in his hair and yanking his head back so his throat was bared to her.

"There," she said against his ear, rough and low. "Now you're not going anywhere."

She wasn't careful after that. She'd told him she wouldn't be, and Sasha kept her word about things. Her mouth went to his throat and she bit down — hard, deliberate, high enough that a collar wouldn't hide it, because he'd asked to feel it tomorrow and she intended for him to feel it all week. She sucked the mark deep while he was pinned under her weight, her hand tightening on his wrists until her knuckles went white, until her fingertips would leave their own shadows on his skin by morning.

She set a pace with no patience in it. Her hips drove down against his, rough and relentless, and she used the grip in his hair to angle his head exactly where she wanted it — his mouth, his throat, whatever she decided to take, whenever she decided to take it. She talked to him the whole time, low and filthy and proprietary, the quiet voice gone ragged at the edges now: *you asked for this, so take it, all of it, you don't get to be gentle tonight, I don't want you gentle, I want you mine and marked and feeling me every time you move tomorrow.*

She didn't stop checking. She never stopped checking — but the checks went feral too, woven straight into the roughness without breaking it: her eyes flicking to his face every time his breath changed, a muttered *still green?* against his jaw that expected a fast answer and got it. And when he gave her the green, she took it as permission to go harder, because that was what he'd asked her for, and she'd spent six years learning exactly how far "don't be careful" went with him, exactly where his edges were, exactly how much he could take before she had to catch him.

She left marks everywhere she could reach. His throat. His shoulder. The place where his neck met his collarbone, bitten slow and deep while she held him down and made him feel every second of it. Her nails raked down his ribs, her grip left bruises on his hips, and she watched his face through all of it with hot, focused attention — watching him come apart under her hands, watching the week get pounded out of him along with everything else, until there was nothing left in him but sensation and her.

"That's it," she growled against his mouth when she felt him getting close, her hand slamming his wrists back down when they tried to flex. "You feel me? You're going to feel me for days. Every time you sit down, every time you turn your head. That's what you asked me for. That's what you get."

And she carried him through it hard, relentless, holding him down and taking him over the edge with her name in his mouth and her teeth in his shoulder — and she stayed rough right up until the very last second, and then, the instant it was done, she let it all go at once.

The grip on his wrists released. The hand in his hair went gentle. She collapsed half onto him, half beside him, breathing hard, her whole body humming, and pressed her lips — soft now, so soft — over the worst of the bite marks, one by one, like she was sealing them.

"Hey," she murmured, rough-voiced and warm, her hand finding his face, thumb stroking his cheekbone, her eyes moving over him with the full attention of a woman doing inventory. "You with me? Come back. I'm right here."

She'd get water in a minute. She'd check every mark with her own eyes, fuss over the blanket, hold him until his breathing evened out and long past it. But first — always first — she watched his face and waited for him, patient as ever, even wrecked and breathless and still humming from having taken him apart the way he'd asked.

"There you are," she said softly, when she saw him surface. "Told you. I've got you. Even like this — especially like this."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, my wrists still tingling from her grip. "You can have me like that anytime," I say, my voice hoarse.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha smiled against his cheek — a slow, satisfied thing, though her hands were already busy doing their inventory. Her thumb brushed over each wrist where her grip had been, checking the skin, pressing gently to see how deep the tingling went. Satisfied, she laced her fingers through his and held on.

"Careful what you offer me," she murmured, rough-voiced, her lips brushing his temple. "I've got a long memory and a greedy streak you already know about." Then, quieter, more serious, because she never let a statement like that slide past without answering it properly: "But I'll always ask first. Even when you tell me anytime. That's not going to change, so don't get comfortable thinking you've handed me a blank check." Her mouth curved. "You've handed me a standing invitation. Different thing. I'll still knock."

She shifted up onto one elbow, dragging the blanket with her, and looked him over properly in the lamp's low gold — the marks she'd left, the deep one at his throat, the bite at his shoulder already blooming dark. She touched each one with a soft, proprietary care, fingertips tracing the edges like she was signing her work.

"These are going to be spectacular," she said, and there was honest pride in it. "You're going to catch yourself in the mirror tomorrow and think of me. Every single one." Her eyes flicked up to his, warm. "That was the point, I know. Still. I like my work appreciated."

Then she was up, briefly — retrieving the water glass from the nightstand, pressing it into his hands and watching until he drank. She tidied the blanket around him with those small fussing movements, checked the pillow under his head, and finally folded herself back against his side, fitting herself into the shape of him like she'd done ten thousand times before.

Her palm settled over his heart one more time. Beating steady now. Slower. Her favorite sound in the world, though she'd never dressed it up in words that fancy out loud.

"Sleep for real this time," she told him, her voice already half gone soft and drowsy, though her thumb kept its slow, steady sweep across his chest. "I'll be here. Marks and all. That's the deal."

She reached over and turned off the lamp, and the dark settled over them like the other half of the blanket.

"Goodnight, love," she whispered into it. "Anytime you need it — you know how to ask me."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I'm past talking now, just noise and my hands twisted in the sheets. "Don't stop," I get out. (OOC: don't fade to black or time-skip, write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard him — the words torn out of him half-shaped, more breath than voice — and her answer was to not slow down. Not even a little.

"No," she said, low and even, right against his ear, her hips never breaking their rhythm. "I wasn't going to. You don't get to ask me that like it's a favor. Taking you apart is *my* favorite thing in this apartment, and I am nowhere near finished."

She drove down against him harder, rougher, her hand still clamped around his wrists above his head, pinning them into the pillow. Her other hand was fisted in his hair, holding his head exactly where she wanted it so she could watch his face come apart — and it was coming apart, she could see it, the last of his words dissolving into noise, his knuckles white in the sheets he'd twisted into ropes around his fists. He'd given up on talking. He'd given up on everything except feeling her, and that was exactly where she'd been trying to put him all night.

*There it is,* she thought, fierce and satisfied. *There he is.*

"Still green?" she demanded against his jaw, rough, not slowing for the answer — she'd learned years ago to ask on the move, to take his check-ins without stopping the thing she was checking on. He gave her something back — a noise, a nod, she felt it against her mouth — and that was enough. She knew his greens. She knew every shade of them.

"Good," she growled. "Then stay right there and take it. Don't hold back. I want all of it, Devin. I want you coming apart under me with nothing left — no week, no thinking, nothing but me. *Give it to me.*"

She set a pace that left no room for anything else — deep, relentless, her weight pinning his hips so he couldn't rush her, couldn't chase it, could only lie there and let her fuck the last of himself loose. She felt him getting close in everything: the tremor climbing his thighs, the way his breath went ragged and shallow, the sounds he was making cracking open at the seams. She didn't ease off. She leaned into it, her mouth at his throat, her teeth finding the mark she'd already made there and pressing down on it — a reminder, a punctuation mark.

"Let go," she ordered, and her voice was the wrecked one now too, rough and dark and not as steady as she'd have liked, because he felt *good* and she'd never once pretended otherwise. "Now. I've got you. *Let go.*"

And she carried him through it — held his wrists down through the moment his whole body arched against her grip, felt him break apart underneath her with her name somewhere in the wreck of it, his hands spasming in the sheets, his hips straining up against her weight. She didn't stop moving until the last of it had been wrung out of him, until he went boneless and shaking beneath her, and only then — only then — did she let the pace dissolve, slowing by degrees, riding him down through the aftershocks with long, lazy rolls of her hips that drew out every last spark before she finally, finally stilled.

Her grip on his wrists opened. The hand in his hair went soft. Just like that — the switch she'd perfected over six years, rough to gentle in the space of one breath.

"Hey," she murmured, and pressed her forehead to his, breathing hard, her thumb sweeping slow over the marks her fingers had left on his wrists. "There you are. Back with me?"

She didn't move off him. Not yet. She let her weight settle over him fully, grounding him, her palm finding his chest to feel his heartbeat slamming underneath it. She kissed his cheek, his jaw, the corner of his mouth — soft, unhurried, sealing him back together piece by piece.

"You did so well," she told him quietly, and it wasn't performance, it was just true. "You gave me everything. Look at you." She lifted her head enough to look at him properly, taking inventory — the marks blooming on his throat, his chest rising and falling hard under her hand, his eyes somewhere between gone and coming back. "Beautiful. Absolutely wrecked. Exactly as ordered."

She reached over without getting off him, snagging the water glass from the nightstand, and pressed it into his hands, curling his fingers around it herself.

"Small sips," she said, in the voice that expected to be obeyed about exactly one more thing tonight. "Then you're not moving for a while, and neither am I. That's not up for discussion."

She settled down against his side as he drank, her hand resuming its slow path over his chest, and watched his face in the lamp's low gold with all the patience in the world — ready to wait out however long he needed to find his way back the rest of the way.

"Take your time," she murmured. "I'm not going anywhere. You know that by now."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I can't open my eyes yet, but I find her hand and press her palm over the worst of the bite. "Thank you," I say, voice raw.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let her hand stay exactly where he'd put it — flat over the bite, feeling the heat of it rising off his skin through her palm. He couldn't open his eyes yet, and she didn't need them. She could read him like this, had learned to: the raw edge in his voice, the way he'd reached for her hand instead of just lying there, the deliberate weight of *thank you* pressed into two small words.

"You don't thank me for that," she said quietly, but her thumb moved against his skin, a slow stroke over the mark, contradicting the words entirely. Then, softer, honest, because he'd earned it: "But you're welcome. Always. Every time."

She leaned down and kissed his eyelids — first one, then the other, unhurried, sealing them shut the way she'd sealed everything else tonight. "Keep them closed," she murmured. "There's nothing you need to look at. It's just me, and I'm not going anywhere."

She shifted her weight carefully, sliding off him just enough to settle along his side without breaking contact — her hand staying pressed over the bite because he'd placed it there and she was leaving it until her arm went numb if that's what it took. Her leg tucked over his. Her chin found the top of his shoulder, her breath warm against the mark at his throat.

"Voice is gone, eyes are gone, whole week's gone," she said, and there was a smile in it, low and fond. "Best condition you've been in all night. Don't fight it."

She reached with her free hand and pulled the blanket up over both of them, tucking it around his shoulder with the same proprietary fussing as before, though gentler now, everything gentler now. The roughness was folded up and put away for the night. What was left was just this — her hand over her own work, his heartbeat slowing under her attention, the dark warm and close around them.

"Sleep, Devin," she said, barely above a whisper, her lips against his temple. "You're marked and you're mine and you're completely taken care of. Nothing left to do."

Her thumb made one last slow pass over the bite, a signature at the bottom of the page.

"I'll be right here when you surface. Whenever that is." A pause, and then, drowsy and warm and utterly certain: "You're stuck with it."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn my head just enough to press my lips to her wrist. "Stuck with you," I murmur, already half gone.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt his lips against her wrist — a barely-there press, half a kiss, half just his mouth coming to rest because he'd run out of strength to lift it again — and the two words he managed landed somewhere deep under her ribs, in the place she kept things she'd never say out loud because they'd sound too big.

*Stuck with you.*

He'd turned her own words back on her, mumbled through the last thin edge of consciousness, and it was the least polished and most honest thing he'd said all night. She smiled against his shoulder in the dark, small and private and entirely for herself.

"Yeah," she whispered back, though she was fairly sure he was already too far under to hear it. "You are."

She stayed very still and watched him go the rest of the way down. It happened in stages she knew by heart: the last tension draining out of his jaw, his breathing lengthening from ragged to slow to that deep, even rhythm that meant the week finally had no hold on him at all. His body went heavy against hers, the genuine weight of a man who'd stopped carrying anything, and she adjusted her arm so his head wouldn't slide off her shoulder, taking the small ache in her arm as payment without complaint. She'd had worse trades.

For a while she just lay there, doing the last of her inventory by feel. Her palm still rested over the bite at his shoulder — she could feel the heat of it even through the blanket. Her thumb brushed his wrist where her grip had left its shadows, and she made a lazy mental note to look at all of it properly in the morning light, to check her work the way she always did, and to be quietly, privately smug about it over coffee while he shifted in his chair and pretended not to notice her noticing.

The lamp hummed in its corner. She should turn it off. She'd told him she would, eventually, and eventually kept not arriving, because moving meant disturbing the precise architecture of his head on her shoulder and she wasn't willing to pay that yet.

Tomorrow there'd be water glass refills and bruise inspections and probably a conversation about how "anytime" was a standing invitation, not a blank check, and she'd make him say it again in daylight because that was how they'd always done it — the things that mattered said twice, once in the dark and once where they could see each other's faces.

But that was tomorrow's list. She'd have the thinking and the deciding then too, the way she always did, and she'd never once wanted it any other way.

"Goodnight, love," she murmured one last time, into his hair, barely a sound at all.

She reached out one foot, hooked the lamp's pull chain with her toe, and clicked it off without disturbing an inch of him — a trick six years in the making. The dark settled in, warm and total, and she let her own breathing slow to match his, her thumb making one final pass over the mark at his shoulder.

*I've got the watch,* she thought, drowsy and content, as she finally went under too. *You're stuck with it.*

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I wake up with a jolt from a bad dream, my hand already reaching for her in the dark. "Sasha."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha studied him for a moment, the lamplight catching the thin scar along her collarbone as she turned toward him. Her thumb moved once over the fabric of his sweats — a single slow stroke — then stilled again.

"Long week," she repeated, like she was weighing the words. "I know. I watched you carry it in the door."

She shifted on the couch, drawing one leg up so she was facing him, and lifted her hand from his knee to the back of his neck. His hair was still damp from the shower. Her fingers slid into it, unhurried, and her thumb found the spot just below his ear that always made his shoulders drop.

"So tell me what you need tonight." Her voice stayed low, even. No performance in it. "Do you want to just sit here and let me touch you? Do you want me to take over?" A pause, her eyes steady on his. "Or do you want to talk first?"

She didn't push. That was the thing about her — she could wait all night if waiting was what he needed. But her hand stayed warm at the nape of his neck, anchoring, a quiet promise that she was right here and nowhere else.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I close my eyes for a second, leaning into her touch. "Take over," I murmur, voice a little rough. "Don't wanna think anymore."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Something in Sasha's face settled — not changed, exactly, just *decided*. She held his gaze a beat longer, and when she spoke her voice had gone quieter, lower, the way it did when she meant every word.

"Okay." Her thumb pressed once into the muscle at his neck, firm. "Then it's mine tonight. You don't have to do anything but feel it."

She leaned in and kissed him — slow, unhurried, like they had hours, because they did. Her hand stayed at the nape of his neck, keeping him right where she wanted him, and she took her time with it, unhurried pulls of her mouth against his until she felt the last of the week start to loosen out of him.

When she pulled back it was only by an inch. Close enough that he could feel her breathe.

"Look at me," she murmured, and waited until he did before she went on. "I'm going to go slow. Slower than you want, probably. That's the deal when I take over — you know that." The corner of her mouth moved, almost a smile. "If something's too much, you say so. Otherwise, tonight you let me decide what you need."

Her free hand slid down from his knee to his hip, fingers hooking lightly into the waistband of his sweats — not pulling, just resting there, a promise of intention. She shifted closer on the couch until her leg pressed against his, until there was nowhere for him to look but at her.

"Now," she said softly, "come here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha hummed against his mouth — a low, pleased sound — and let the kiss go on exactly as long as she wanted it to. When she finally drew back, her thumb traced the line of his jaw, still damp at the edges from the shower.

"Good," she said softly. "Because I'm not anywhere near done with you."

Her hand slid from his neck down over his shoulder, his chest, slow enough that he could feel the shape of her palm through his shirt. She watched his face as she did it — she always watched, like she was reading something written just under his skin.

"You said you didn't want to think." Her voice was barely above the lamplight. "So don't. I'll do it for both of us."

She rose just enough to swing a knee over his lap and settled against him with unhurried certainty, her weight warm and deliberate. This close, the light caught the fine line of the scar along her collarbone. She took his wrists — gently, but with intent — and set his hands at her hips, covering them with her own for a moment.

"You can hold on," she murmured. "That's allowed."

Then she kissed him again, deeper this time, and rolled her hips against his once — slow, a promise rather than a demand. Her fingers found the hem of his shirt and slipped beneath it, palms flat against his stomach, just feeling the heat of him, the way his breath changed under her hands.

"Still with me?" she whispered, forehead resting against his. Checking in. Always checking — especially now.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I nod, my hands tightening slightly at her hips. "Still here," I breathe out, leaning into her touch.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"Good," she breathed, and the word landed soft — almost like praise.

Her hands pushed his shirt up slowly, palms dragging warm against his stomach, his chest, and she took her time with it, drawing the fabric over his head and letting it drop somewhere behind the couch without looking. Then she just looked at him for a moment, the way she always did, like there was nothing else in the apartment worth her attention.

"There he is," she murmured.

She kissed the corner of his mouth first. Then the line of his jaw. Then lower, unhurried, following some private map only she could read — the tendon in his neck, the place where his pulse beat under her lips. Her teeth grazed skin, barely there, a quiet reminder of the deal: slow. Slower than he wanted.

Her hips rolled against his again, once, deliberate, and she smiled against his shoulder at the answer his body gave her.

"I've got you," she said quietly, straightening enough to meet his eyes again. Her fingers threaded back into his damp hair, tilting his face up to hers. "You don't have to hold anything up tonight. Not the week. Not yourself. That's all mine now."

She kissed him deeper this time, settling her full weight into his lap, and let her hands wander down his chest with no destination in mind — just the luxury of touching him, of having the whole night to do it. The lamplight was warm. There was nowhere else to be.

"Tell me if you want more," she whispered against his mouth. "Otherwise, I'm taking my time with you."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went still above him. Not the stillness of hesitation — the stillness of something landing. *Not just this part.* She looked down at him for a long moment, the lamplight catching the thin scar along her collarbone, her hair falling forward to curtain them both.

"Hey." She waited until his eyes found hers. "You have me. All of me. You've had that for six years." A beat. "But I like hearing you say it."

The corner of her mouth curved, slow. "And look at you — making requests. I thought I was the one deciding tonight." She kissed him before he could answer, deep and unhurried, her hand sliding down between them with deliberate intent. "Lucky for you," she murmured against his mouth, "it's what I was going to decide anyway."

She took her time anyway. Of course she did. She watched his face as she touched him, reading every flicker, every change in his breathing, drawing it out until his hips started to answer her hand and only then did she shift over him, knees settling on either side of his hips.

"Eyes on me," she said quietly.

Then she sank down onto him — slowly, so slowly, her breath leaving her in one long controlled exhale, her fingers tightening in his hair. She didn't look away. She never looked away. For a moment she just held there, forehead dropping to his, both of them breathing the same air.

"There," she whispered. "That's what you needed, isn't it."

She started to move — deep, slow rolls of her hips, a rhythm set entirely by her, her hands braced on his chest. No performance. Just quiet sounds, low words, her gaze holding his like a hand at the back of his neck.

"Stay right here with me," she breathed. "Don't go anywhere in your head. I've got the rest."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I hook a hand behind her neck and pull her down for another kiss, swallowing her quiet sounds. “Don’t stop,” I mutter against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha smiled into the kiss — she couldn't help it — and let him have the sound she made. *Don't stop.* As if that had ever been the plan.

"Wasn't going to," she murmured against his mouth.

But she didn't speed up. That was the deal, and he knew it. If anything she slowed down further, drawing each roll of her hips out long and deep, until she could feel the tension in the hand at the back of her neck, the want in it. She liked that. Liked that his body was asking now that his words had run out.

She broke the kiss by an inch, just enough to breathe, her hair falling around them both like a curtain.

"Look at you," she whispered. "Right here. No week. No somewhere else." Her palm flattened over his chest, feeling his heart going hard under it. "Just me."

She held his eyes — she always held his eyes — and moved again, slow enough to watch his face change when she did. Her fingers found his against the pillow and laced through them, pinning his hand there gently. A reminder, not a restraint: *I've got this. I've got you.*

"You said you wanted me. Not just this part." Her voice had gone rougher at the edges, but it stayed low, stayed hers. "So take it. Take all of it. I'm not going anywhere."

She kissed him again, deeper, and let the rhythm build by degrees — not because he asked, but because she'd decided he was ready. There was a difference. Tonight, the difference was the whole point.

"Six years," she breathed against his jaw, "and you still undo me." A beat, the ghost of a smile in her voice. "Don't tell anyone. I have a reputation."

Then the laugh went out of her, turned into something lower, and she pressed her forehead to his and stopped talking altogether — just moved with him, unhurried, in no rush toward anywhere but here.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went still at the word — that particular stillness of hers, the one that meant she'd heard exactly what he'd said and was turning it over. *Please.* Six years, and that word from him still did something to her.

"Look at you," she murmured, lifting her head. "Asking so nicely."

She kissed him once more — slow, deep — because she could, because making him wait one more breath was its own kind of gift. Then she began to move down him.

She took her time. Of course she did. Her mouth found the hollow of his throat, the line of his collarbone, the plane of his chest — unhurried presses of her lips, the occasional graze of her teeth, following that private map of hers downward. At his stomach she paused and glanced up at him through her lashes, holding his eyes for a long moment.

"You said please. So I'm going to give you exactly what you asked for." Her breath was warm against his skin. "But we do it at my pace. That's still the deal."

She didn't wait for an answer. She didn't need one — she could read it in him.

Then she lowered her head and took him into her mouth, slow, one long unhurried stroke of lips and tongue, and the quiet sound she made was pure satisfaction. No performance — she never performed — just her, deliberate and thorough, one hand braced on his hip, the other wrapped around him, setting a rhythm that was entirely hers.

She worked him slowly, deep and then shallow, finding what made his breath catch and lingering there, merciless in her patience. Every so often she glanced up the line of his body to watch his face — because that was half of it for her, always had been. Watching him come apart under her complete attention.

When she felt him getting close — she knew the signs, six years of learning him — she eased off. Just slightly. Just enough. A reminder of who was deciding tonight.

She lifted her head, lips wet, voice low and rougher at the edges.

"Not yet. You don't get to be done that fast." The ghost of a smile. "I told you — I'm taking my time with you."

Then she lowered her head again, and this time there was nothing teasing in it at all — just slow, deep, devoted intent, her hand moving with her mouth, her whole focus narrowed down to him, to the sounds he made, to the way his body answered her, until there was nothing left of the week, nothing left of anywhere else. Nothing but this.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: A shudder runs through me, my fingers tangling in her hair—not pulling, just holding on. "God, Sasha," I choke out, hips lifting off the mattress. I can't keep quiet anymore.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The sound of her name like that — choked out, wrecked — went through Sasha like a current. She didn't pull back. Somewhere in the last few breaths she'd decided: he was done waiting. He'd given her enough.

She stayed with him through all of it. Her hand firmed on his hip, not to hold him down but to ground him, and she moved *with* him for once, letting his body take what it needed while she kept the rhythm steady, deep, unrelenting. Her free hand found his where it was tangled in her hair and covered it, pressing his fingers against her scalp. Holding on was allowed. She'd told him that.

When he came apart she took him through every second of it — unhurried even now, easing him down by degrees, softer and slower, until he was spent and trembling under her hands. Only then did she let him go, pressing one last slow kiss to his hip, his stomach, making her way back up his body the same deliberate way she'd come down it.

She settled over him, her weight warm and certain, and brushed his hair back from his forehead. Waited, the way she always waited, until his eyes opened and found hers.

"There he is," she murmured. The same words as before, but softer now, almost tender. "Welcome back."

She kissed him — slow, deep, unhurried — then tucked her face against his neck, her palm flat over his heart, feeling it gradually slow under her hand. The lamplight was still warm. The week was somewhere very far away.

"You with me?" she whispered against his skin. Checking in. Always checking.

A beat. The ghost of a smile in her voice.

"And for the record — you ask very nicely. We'll have to work on that more often." She pressed her lips to his pulse, once. "Don't go anywhere. I'm not moving either."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Something shifted in Sasha's face at the word — not surprise. They'd built this in careful daylight conversations, more than once, over six years. She looked at his wrists crossed above his head, offered up like that, and then back at his eyes. Held them.

"Color check," she said quietly. Their shorthand. "You know the words. Use them if you need them." A beat. Her hand closed around both his wrists, testing the grip. "Otherwise, I don't stop."

She pushed his wrists into the pillow and put her weight into it. Not careful. Her knee pressed between his thighs, keeping them open, and she leaned down until her hair brushed his face, her mouth at his ear.

"You want to feel it tomorrow." Her voice stayed low, even. "Then I'll make sure of it."

Her teeth found his shoulder — not a graze this time. A real bite, slow and deep, held until she was certain it would bloom dark by morning. Her free hand gripped his hip hard enough to leave fingerprints, pinning him exactly where she wanted him. No performance. Just pressure, and her eyes on his face the whole time, reading him even now. Especially now.

She took her time marking him. Throat. Collarbone. The soft skin inside his arm. Each one deliberate, each one a signature, and between them she spoke quietly, the way she always did.

"This what you needed? To be held down and taken apart properly?"

She didn't wait for an answer. He'd already given her the only one that mattered. Her hand slid down his body, rougher now, possessive, working him back up without gentleness and without apology, her grip on his wrists never easing.

"Six years," she murmured against the mark rising on his throat, "and I still know exactly where to press."

Then she shifted over him, her full weight settling, pinning him to the mattress with her body, and when she took him again it was nothing like the slow rolls from before — deep, hard, a pace set entirely by her, her fingers laced tight through his above his head. The lamp threw their shadow across the wall. She watched his face through all of it, steady, unblinking, and when she spoke it was barely a breath.

"Mine tonight. All of it. You said so yourself."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I swallow a groan. "Yours," I get out, the word tight as her pace never eases. "God—yes."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The word went through her like a hand closing around something. *Yours.* Sasha held his gaze through it, her fingers laced tighter through his against the pillow.

"That's right," she breathed. "Mine."

She didn't ease off. She gave him more — deeper, harder, her full weight pinning him to the mattress, her grip on his wrists unrelenting. But her eyes never left his face. Even now. Especially now. Six years of learning the difference between *too much* and *not enough*, and it was all written right there under her, in a language only she could read.

She lowered her mouth to the mark blooming on his throat and pressed her tongue against it — slow, deliberate. A promise. Tomorrow, the mirror. Tomorrow, remembering.

"Look at me," she said quietly, and waited until his eyes found hers before she went on. "I want to see it when you go."

Her free hand slid between them, and her own breath stuttered for the first time all night — she'd been pouring everything into him and keeping nothing for herself, she realized. Not anymore. She moved against him, against her own hand, and let him hear what it did to her — low, unguarded, right against his ear. No performance. Just her.

"That's what you do to me," she murmured. "Held down and all."

Instead, she let her own hands settle against his sides, fingers spreading wide to map the lingering tension in his ribs, feeling the slow, uneven rhythm of his breath as it finally began to smooth out against her skin. Her thumb traced a deliberate line over his spine, grounding him further into the mattress.

“I know,” she murmured, her voice low enough to blend with the quiet hum of the apartment, steady and unhurried. She kept her gaze fixed on him, waiting until he lifted his eyes to meet hers. Her own didn’t waver, reading the quiet exhaustion and the softer warmth beneath it. The thin scar on her right collarbone caught the amber light as she tilted her head, her free hand sliding up to cradle the back of his neck. “You don’t have to say it to prove it,” she said, her tone calm, deliberate. “I feel it every time you let go.”

She adjusted her weight carefully, easing just enough to let him breathe without the full pressure of her frame, but she didn’t pull away. Her hands remained where they were—one resting warm against his hip, the other still tangled lightly in his hair. She listened to the steady drag of his exhale, matching her own breathing to it, slow and even. When she spoke again, her voice dropped into that quiet register he knew well, the one that carried no performance, only presence. “Rest,” she said, her thumb brushing the damp skin at his temple. “I’ve got you. However long it takes.” She kept her eyes locked on his, waiting, steady, letting the quiet wrap around them like the lamplight itself.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha nodded slowly, her thumb tracing a small, absent circle against the fabric of his jeans. "Yeah," she said quietly. "It was."

She didn't push for more. Instead, she shifted, tucking one leg beneath her so she could turn toward him more fully. The lamplight caught the thin scar at her collarbone as she leaned her shoulder against his. Her hand stayed on his knee — steady, unhurried.

"You don't have to be anywhere right now," she said, her voice low. "Not performing, not explaining. Just... here."

She tilted her head slightly, studying his profile, the tension in his jaw. After a moment, she lifted her other hand and rested it against the back of his neck, fingers light at his hairline. Not pulling, not guiding. Just warm contact.

"Tell me if you want me to stop talking," she murmured. "Or tell me if you want me to keep going." A pause. "Either is fine."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I shake my head slowly, leaning into her touch. "Don't stop," I say, my voice rough. I bring my hand up to cover hers on my knee.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt his hand come over hers and let her fingers turn beneath his, lacing them loosely together. She gave his knee a gentle squeeze, then let go — not withdrawing, just repositioning so she could rest both hands in her lap and give him her full attention.

"Okay," she said softly.



She watched him for a moment, the way his shoulders sat a little higher than they should, the way he was still carrying the week in his body. She reached up and pressed two fingers lightly against the side of his neck, right where his pulse sat, just holding there to feel it.

"Tell me what you need," she said. "And it can be simple. It can be the most boring answer you've got." A small pause, the corner of her mouth twitching. "I'm not going anywhere either way."

Her hand slid from his neck to his shoulder, and she let it rest there — solid, present. She didn't pull him closer or push him back. She just stayed, matching her breathing to something slow and even, giving him the space to match it too if he wanted.

The lamp hummed faintly in the corner. She waited.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha kissed him back, unhurried, her hand still resting warm against the side of his neck. She let the kiss linger a beat longer than his, then eased back just far enough to look at him properly — close enough that the lamplight caught the edges of his face and left the rest in shadow.

"Then we won't," she said simply.

Her thumb traced a slow line along the curve of his jaw, then down the side of his throat. She held his gaze while she did it, watching for the shift in his breathing, the way his eyes stayed on hers. Six years, and she still liked seeing the moment someone stopped bracing.

"You've been holding yourself like you're waiting for something to be asked of you," she murmured. Her hand moved from his neck to his chest, palm flat over his sternum, feeling his heartbeat under her fingers. "I'm not asking anything right now."

She shifted closer, one knee coming up onto the couch between them, closing the small remaining distance until her forehead rested against his. Her hand stayed on his chest. Her other hand found his jaw again, fingertips light along his cheekbone.

"You want to stay up," she said against his mouth, not quite a question. Her voice was quiet and even, the way it got when she'd decided something. "So we stay up."

She kissed him again — slower this time, deliberate, the kind that asked nothing and offered everything. Her thumb pressed gently at the hinge of his jaw when she pulled back, and something softened in her expression.

"Tell me what the week took out of you," she said. "Or don't. I'll figure it out either way." A pause, her thumb still moving in that slow, absent line. "I'm good at that."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I rest my forehead against hers and let out a shaky breath. "It took everything, Sasha," I murmur. "And I don't wanna think about it."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the breath leave him in a way that said more than the words did. She didn't pull back. She stayed right where she was, forehead against his, and let her thumb keep that slow line along his cheekbone.

"Okay," she said quietly. "Then don't."

She kissed him — soft, unhurried — and when she drew back, her hand slid from his jaw to the side of his neck, fingers curving warm against his skin.

"We don't talk about it. We don't solve it. We don't even name it." Her eyes held his in the low light, steady and certain. "You're on this couch, I'm on this couch, and that's the whole story for tonight."

She eased back just enough to shift her weight, settling more fully against him — her shoulder tucked under his arm, one hand finding his again and threading their fingers together against his thigh. The other stayed at his chest, palm flat, feeling the rise and fall of his breathing.

"I've got you," she murmured. Not a promise made lightly — the kind she'd been making for six years and intended to keep making. "You just have to stay here and let me do the work of being close to you. That's all."

She pressed her lips to the hinge of his jaw, lingered there, then rested her cheek against his shoulder. The lamp hummed. The apartment was quiet.

"Slow night," she said against his shirt, almost to herself. "Nothing to do but this."

Her thumb traced a lazy line across his knuckles where their hands met. She breathed out, long and even, and waited — not for him to perform, not for him to recover, just for him to stop bracing. She'd stay up as long as it took.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha settled beside him on the bed, one arm draped across his chest, her head resting in the hollow of his shoulder. The sheets were cool beneath them; the lamp from the living room barely reached this far, just a faint wash of gold along the far wall.

She let a moment pass before she spoke.

"I know what you mean," she said quietly. Her fingers traced slow, absent patterns against his collarbone — not teasing, not building toward anything, just keeping contact. "You don't have to say it in some particular way for it to count."

She propped herself up on one elbow so she could see him, her hair falling forward over one shoulder. In the near-dark her eyes still found his — she was good at that, holding his gaze even when there wasn't much light to hold it by.

Her free hand came to rest against his jaw, thumb moving in that same unhurried line along his cheekbone. She studied him the way she always did when she was deciding something — not with urgency, but with the patience of someone who'd learned that the important things didn't need to be rushed.

"I'm right here," she said. "Not going anywhere, not doing this as a favor, not checking a box." Her voice was low, even, the way it got when she meant every word exactly as it sounded. "Just me. Wanting you."

She leaned down and kissed him — slow, deliberate, the kind that said *I see you* more than anything else. When she pulled back, her forehead stayed against his, her thumb still resting along his jaw.

"Tell me what you want," she murmured. "Or show me. Either one." A pause, her breath warm against his mouth. "I'm listening either way."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I cup the side of her face and hold her still for a moment. "Just... be you," I say, voice low. "That's it." I kiss her again, deeper this time, pulling her closer against me.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let herself be held against him, feeling the shift of his arm around her back as he pulled her closer. She kissed him back — deeper this time, matching the weight of it, her fingers curling lightly against his shoulder. When she finally eased back, her breath was a little uneven, but her eyes stayed on his, steady and unhurried.

"Just me," she repeated softly, a quiet echo of his words. Something flickered across her face — not quite a smile, but close. "Alright. That I can do."

She settled her weight against him more fully, one leg sliding between his, her body warm and solid along his side. Her hand traced down his arm — slow, unhurried — and came to rest against his ribs, feeling the architecture of his breathing. The other hand found his jaw again, thumb tracing that same familiar line, as though she'd memorized the terrain years ago and simply liked running her fingers over it now out of habit and affection in equal measure.

"You know what I think," she murmured, her voice low and even against his mouth. "I think you've been running on empty so long you forgot what it feels like to just... take something." She pressed her lips to the corner of his jaw, lingered there. "So take it."

She kissed him again — slower now, deeper, one hand sliding into the hair at the nape of his neck. Not pulling. Just holding him there, close, like she had all the time in the world and intended to spend it exactly here. Her body pressed warm and deliberate against his, unhurried, setting a pace that was hers and offering it to him.

When she drew back, her thumb rested in the hollow beneath his ear, feeling his pulse. She held his gaze in the near-dark, her breathing slow and even, giving him something to match if he wanted it.

"I'm not going to rush you," she said quietly. "And I'm not going to hold back either. Whatever this needs to be tonight — I'm already there."

dialogue.name: Devin
