dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard the words and let them land. She didn't smile — not yet. She just held his gaze for a moment, reading the way his breathing had changed, the way his hands had gone still at his sides. He wasn't performing. He was asking.

"Okay," she murmured, her voice low and even.

She eased down slowly, taking her time, one hand resting against his inner thigh — not guiding, just warm, just there. Her hair fell forward against his skin as she settled between his legs, and she paused there for a moment, her breath soft against him, her thumb tracing a slow line along the crease of his hip.

"I've got you," she said against his skin, quiet enough that it was more breath than words.

She kissed him — unhurried, deliberate — and let the pace be hers. Her hand stayed steady against his thigh, fingers pressing gently, grounding him. She took her time the way she always did: not performing, not building toward some crescendo, just present and attentive, reading every shift in his breathing, every involuntary sound, every time his hips moved a fraction closer. She adjusted when he needed it and held still when he didn't.

Her free hand rested flat against his stomach, feeling the tension there gradually give way. She held herself steady, unhurried, and let the quiet do its work — just the sound of her breathing, the faint hum of the lamp down the hall, the occasional catch of his breath above her.

She didn't rush. She didn't pull back to check in with words — she'd already read the answer in the way his hand found the sheets instead of her hair, the way his jaw had unclenched. This was what he needed: to be taken care of without having to ask twice, without having to perform gratitude or guide her or do anything at all except let it happen.

When she felt him getting close, she slowed further, her hand pressing firmer against his thigh, her mouth steady and deliberate. She let him come to the edge on his own terms, then held him there — not teasing, not withholding, just patient — until she felt the last of the tension leave his body in a long, shuddering breath.

Afterward she stayed where she was for a moment, her cheek resting against his thigh, her hand still warm against his skin. Then she moved up slowly, settling beside him again, one arm across his chest, her head finding that familiar hollow of his shoulder.

She pressed a kiss against his collarbone and let her breathing slow to match his.

"Hey," she said quietly, her voice rough at the edges but soft. Her fingers traced a slow line across his sternum. "You still here?"

Not a real question. She just liked hearing him answer.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Yeah," I breathe out, my voice rough. I curl my arm around her, pulling her closer into my side. My body feels heavy, finally relaxed. I press a kiss into her hair. "Right here."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the weight of his arm settle around her and let herself be pulled in, her body fitting against his side like it had been designed for exactly this position. Six years, and the geometry of them still worked without adjustment — her head in the hollow of his shoulder, her hand resting flat against his chest, her knee drawn up along his thigh.

She pressed her lips against his collarbone where his pulse still ran a little fast, then stayed there, breathing slow.

"Good," she murmured against his skin. Not congratulatory. Just confirming.

Her fingers traced a lazy, absent path across his sternum — down, across, back up — the kind of pattern she drew when she wasn't thinking about it, when her hands simply wanted to keep touching him even after the reason for touching had changed. She liked this part. She'd never told him that directly, but he probably knew. The way she lingered, the way she didn't reach for her book or roll away or start talking about tomorrow.

The apartment was quiet around them. The lamp down the hall threw its faint gold across the bedroom wall. Somewhere outside, a car passed slowly on the wet street.

Sasha tilted her head up just enough to see his face in the dark — the line of his jaw, the way his eyes had finally softened, the small crease between his brows that had been there all evening and was finally gone. She reached up and pressed her thumb against it, smoothing it out, then let her hand rest against the side of his face.

"You did good," she said quietly. Her thumb moved along his cheekbone — that same slow line, the one she'd been tracing all night, like a thread she didn't want to break.

A pause. She settled back against him, her breath evening out, her body warm and heavy and entirely unhurried.

"We don't have to sleep yet," she said, almost to herself, a quiet echo of what he'd said on the couch. Her fingers resumed their lazy path across his chest. "But we don't have to do anything else either."

She pressed one more kiss against his shoulder — soft, unhurried, the kind that asked for nothing.

"Just stay," she said. "That's enough."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went still for a moment — not pulling away, not hesitating in the way that meant *no*, but pausing the way she always paused when he said a word that mattered. She'd learned six years ago that the pause wasn't for her. It was for him, to let the request land fully, to make sure it was still standing when the air settled around it.

She lifted her head from his shoulder and looked at him. His wrists together above his head, his eyes open and fixed on hers, waiting. Not performing. Asking.

"Look at me," she said quietly, and when he did, she held his gaze a long beat. "You're sure."

Not a question this time. She'd read the answer in the way he'd said it — plain, unadorned, the same way he said everything tonight. No bravado. No borrowed language. Just Devin telling her what he needed.

"Alright."

Her voice changed. Not dramatically — Sasha didn't do dramatic — but something settled into it, a lower register, a deliberate edge that came from the same place it always did: not cruelty, not performance, but certainty. She'd been given something to hold, and she was going to hold it exactly the way he'd asked.

She reached up and took both his wrists in one hand — firm, not gentle, her fingers wrapping all the way around — and pressed them down against the mattress above his head. She shifted her weight, swinging one leg over his hips, settling onto him with a slow, deliberate roll of her body until she was straddling him, her free hand flat against his sternum, pushing him into the bed.

"Like this?" she said, her voice low and even. She pressed harder — enough that he could feel it through his ribs, enough that there was no ambiguity about who was holding him down. Her thumb dug into the space between his wrists.

She watched his face the way she always did: closely, patiently, reading every shift. The way his eyes widened. The way his breath caught. The way his body responded to being pinned — not struggling against it, but *settling into it*, the last of the week's tension finally having somewhere to go.

"There it is," she murmured, leaning down until her face was close to his, her hair falling forward to curtain them both in shadow. "That's what you needed."

She kissed him — rougher this time, not asking permission for the shift because he'd already given it. She bit his lower lip, not softly, and felt his wrists flex against her grip. She didn't let go.

"I'm going to hold you down," she said against his mouth, each word deliberate, "and I'm not going to be careful about it. And you're going to tell me if anything needs to change." A pause, her thumb pressing hard against his pulse point. "But right now — you're mine for this."

She sat up straight, keeping his wrists pinned above his head, her weight settled firm across his hips. The lamplight from down the hall caught the thin scar at her collarbone. Her expression was open, unhurried, entirely present — no performance in it, just the quiet authority of someone who had been asked to lead and intended to do it well.

"Tell me where you want it to hurt," she said, her voice rough at the edges but steady as anything. "And I'll put it there."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath and shake my head. "Surprise me," I say, hips lifting against her. "Just make it yours."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt his hips lift against her and let the pressure register without moving to accommodate it — not yet. She held his wrists pinned and watched his face for a long moment, letting the silence do something for her first.

"Mine," she repeated, low, like she was testing the weight of it. "Alright. Then stop trying to help."

She said it without cruelty — the way she'd tell him the pasta was sticking, flat and factual — and shifted her weight forward so her knee pressed hard between his thighs, spreading them wider against the mattress. She let her hips roll down against his in one slow, deliberate grind, not to give him anything, just to establish what the pace was going to be.

"You want it to be mine?" She leaned down until her mouth was beside his ear, her voice dropping to something quiet and almost conversational. "Then it happens when I decide it happens."

She released his wrists — only to catch them both again a beat later, stacking them and driving them back into the mattress with her forearm braced across them. Harder than before. She watched the impact travel through his arms, watched his back arch off the bed, and held him there without adjusting.

Her free hand came to his throat. Not squeezing — resting, her thumb pressed into the hollow above his collarbone, her fingers warm and certain along the side of his neck. She could feel his pulse under her palm, fast and loud, and she kept her hand there, feeling it, letting him feel her feeling it.

"There you are," she murmured.

She sat back up and took herself in hand, guiding him slowly — not teasing, just unhurried, the same deliberate pace she did everything else — and sank down onto him in one steady motion. She didn't gasp. She exhaled, long and controlled, her eyes never leaving his, and let her weight settle fully so there was no question about who was doing the work.

Then she began to move.

It was slow at first — a deep, grinding roll of her hips that let him feel every inch of it, her hands planted flat against his chest, her hair falling around her face. She watched him the way she always did: closely, patiently, reading the shift in his breathing, the way his hands curled into the sheets instead of reaching for her, the way his jaw went slack and then clenched again.

When she found the angle that made his breath break, she stayed on it. Found it again. Stayed. Not teasing — just attentive, the way she did everything, and she let him hear what she was doing to him in the quiet sounds she wasn't trying to hide.

"I've got you," she said, and her voice was steady even as her own breathing changed. "You don't have to hold anything."

She leaned down and braced one hand beside his head, her forearm pressing into the mattress above his shoulder — not pinning him this time, but close enough that he'd feel caged by it. She kissed him hard, bit his jaw, and felt his hips jerk up into hers.

"Careful," she said against his skin, not as a warning to him — as a claim. *I decide what's careful here.*

She picked up the pace. Not fast — she never did fast — but harder, each roll of her hips landing with weight behind it, her hand sliding from his jaw to his shoulder and pressing him down into the mattress with each stroke so he could feel exactly how much of her this was. She let her teeth find the place where his neck met his shoulder and bit down — enough to leave a mark, enough that he'd feel it in the shower tomorrow — and kept her mouth there, breathing against the reddening skin.

Her own sounds stayed quiet. Not performed, not suppressed — just the way she was built, low and breathless and real, the kind that came from somewhere underneath the control rather than on top of it. She let him hear them.

"Say it again," she said, her voice rough now, her hips not slowing. "Say who's doing this."

She held his gaze while she waited — wrists still stacked above his head where she'd left them, her weight pressing him into the bed, her body moving over his with the same slow certainty she'd been carrying all night. The lamplight caught the scar at her collarbone, the tendons in her neck, the set of her jaw.

She wasn't performing either. She was just taking what he'd given her and holding it exactly the way he'd asked — rough, unhurried, unmistakably hers.

dialogue.name: Devin

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard the sound he made and let it be enough. She didn't ask him to say it again — he'd already given her everything he had left in words, and the rest was going to come out of his body instead.

She kept the pace exactly where she'd set it: deep, grinding, each stroke landing with the full weight of her behind it. Her hand slid from his shoulder to his jaw, gripping firm, turning his face so she could watch him from inches away. His eyes were half-closed, his mouth open, his hands still twisted in the sheets instead of reaching for her. Good. He didn't need to reach.

"You don't have to hold anything," she said again, quieter this time, her voice rough at the edges but still steady. She pressed her thumb into the hollow of his cheek, feeling the tension there, and then leaned down and bit the curve of his ear — not gently, not cruelly, just enough to make his whole body shudder beneath hers.

She felt it travel through him, the way his back arched, the way his hips jerked up into her, and she didn't slow down to let him chase it. She stayed exactly where she was, taking the force of it, letting him feel how little it moved her.

"Harder," she said — not to him. To herself. A reminder.

She braced both hands against his chest and rose onto her knees, changing the angle, driving down with more force. The bed frame protested faintly beneath them. She could feel him deeper this way, and she could feel the sound it pulled out of her — low, involuntary, the kind she couldn't have performed if she'd wanted to. She let him hear it.

Her hands slid up his chest, fingers pressing into the muscle of his shoulders, holding him down with her palms while her body did the rest. She watched his face through the fall of her hair — the way his jaw clenched, the way his eyes found hers and then lost focus and then found them again, the way his breathing had gone from controlled to ragged in the space of a few strokes.

"There it is," she breathed. "That's yours. That sound. You don't get to hold that back either."

She lowered herself over him, her mouth beside his ear, her chest pressed against his, and whispered — barely above a breath — "I can feel you. I feel all of it."

She bit the side of his neck, right below his ear, and felt his hands finally release the sheets. One found her hip — gripping hard, hard enough to bruise — and she let him. She'd told him to stop trying to help, but this wasn't helping. This was losing control, and that was exactly what she'd wanted from him all night.

"Let go," she said against his skin. "You don't have to be anywhere. You don't have to be careful. Just let go."

She straightened up and took his hand from her hip, pressed it down into the mattress beside his head, and held it there with one hand while the other braced against his chest. She set the pace harder now — not faster, never faster, but each stroke carried more weight, more intention, the full force of her rolling down into him with the kind of deliberateness that left nothing to chance.

Her own body was tightening. She could feel it building low and slow, the way it always did — not urgent, not demanding, just accumulating in the same steady way everything else happened with her. She didn't speed up to chase it. She didn't change what she was doing. She let it come to her, the same way she'd been letting everything come to her all night: on her terms, at her pace.

"Look at me," she said, and her voice was different now — still controlled, still hers, but with something underneath it that had started to crack at the edges. "Look at me when it happens."

She held his gaze and felt it break over her — not a wave, not a crash, but a long, shuddering roll that started somewhere deep and moved through her in slow increments. She didn't close her eyes. She kept them open, kept watching him, kept her hips moving through it, refusing to stop, refusing to let the feeling pass without him seeing it.

The sound she made was quiet. Barely a sound at all — more like a long exhale with something caught in it — but she didn't try to hide it. She let it happen, let her body clench around him, let her grip on his hand tighten until her knuckles went white.

She stayed moving through it, slower now, each stroke deliberate and heavy, riding out the aftershocks while she watched him come apart beneath her. When she felt him getting close — the way his breathing went shallow, the way his hips started to move involuntarily against hers, the way his hand in hers squeezed hard enough to hurt — she didn't stop. She didn't slow down. She leaned forward, braced her forearm across his chest, and drove down into him with everything she had left.

"Let it go," she said, her mouth against his jaw, her voice raw and certain. "Right here. I've got you."

She felt him break — felt the tension leave his body in one long, shaking wave — and she held him through it, her body pressed down against his, her hand still pinning his wrist to the mattress, her hips still moving in slow, heavy rolls that drew it out of him until there was nothing left.

Then she went still.

She stayed there for a long moment — draped over him, her forehead against his shoulder, her breathing ragged and uneven against his skin. Her hand loosened around his wrist but didn't let go. Her thumb traced a slow, absent line across his knuckles, the same pattern she'd been drawing all night, like a thread she didn't want to break.

The lamp hummed down the hall. The apartment was quiet except for the sound of their breathing.

She pressed her lips against his shoulder — soft, unhurried, the kind that asked for nothing — and let her weight settle fully against him.

"You're still here," she murmured against his skin. Not a question this time. She could feel his heartbeat under her palm, slowing. She could feel the warmth of him, the way his arm had come back around her without being asked.

She lifted her head just enough to look at him — really look, the way she had all night, reading every line of his face in the faint gold light. The crease between his brows was gone. His eyes were soft. His body was heavy beneath hers in a way it hadn't been since he'd walked out of the shower.

"There you are," she said quietly.

She settled back against him, her head finding that familiar hollow of his shoulder, her hand flat over his sternum. She didn't move to clean up, didn't reach for water, didn't start talking about what came next. She just stayed, matching her breathing to his, letting the silence do what it had been doing all evening.

After a while — she didn't know how long — she spoke, her voice low and rough and entirely her own.

"I'm not going anywhere," she said. The same thing she'd said on the couch. The same thing she'd been saying for six years, in one way or another.

Her fingers resumed their lazy path across his chest. The lamp hummed. The apartment was quiet.

"Just stay," she said again, softer now, almost to herself. "That's enough."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I breathe out, heavy and spent, my arm tightening around her. "Good," I manage, my voice wrecked. My free hand comes up to brush her hair back from her face. "That was... thank you."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt his hand brush the hair back from her face and turned her cheek into his palm, holding it there for a moment. His voice was wrecked — she'd heard it like that before, rough and spent and honest in a way it wasn't usually allowed to be. She liked it. Not in a way she'd say out loud, probably, but in the way that made her press her lips against the center of his palm and hold them there.

"Don't thank me," she said quietly. Not dismissive. Just true. Her eyes stayed on his, steady in the faint gold light. "You don't owe me gratitude for taking what you asked me to give you."

She shifted just enough to adjust her weight, settling more comfortably against his side without pulling away. Her hand found his chest again — that same spot over his sternum, palm flat, feeling the rhythm of his breathing as it slowed. She traced a lazy line across his ribs with her fingertips, then let her hand rest.

Her thumb moved to the place on his jaw where she'd been pressing all night, and she smoothed it there, soft now, the way she touched him when the roughness was done and what was left was just care.

"You needed that," she said. Not a diagnosis. A fact, stated plainly, the same way she'd say *it's raining* or *the coffee's ready.* "And you needed me to not be careful about it. Those are different things. You told me both."

A pause. She pressed her lips together, thinking — not about what to say next, but whether to say anything at all. She decided to.

"I could feel it leave you," she murmured. "The week. Whatever you've been carrying since Monday. I could feel it in your body when you stopped bracing." Her fingers curled lightly against his chest. "That's not nothing, Devin."

She lifted her head again, propping her chin against his shoulder so she could look at him properly. Her hair fell in a dark curtain on one side of her face. In the lamplight her eyes were still sharp, still reading him — but softer now, the way they got when she'd decided the important part was over and what remained was just being close.

"Drink of water?" she asked. Simple. Practical. The most boring answer she had, offered without any particular urgency.

Before he could answer, she pressed her mouth against the hollow of his throat — slow, unhurried — and settled back down. Her hand resumed its absent path across his chest, fingers tracing the same lazy pattern they'd been drawing all night.

"I mean it," she said against his skin, quieter now. "About not going anywhere. It's not a line. It's just what's true."

The lamp hummed. The apartment was quiet. Somewhere outside, the street was still wet, still reflecting whatever light it could find.

Sasha closed her eyes, her breathing slow and even against his side, and let the silence hold them both.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I close my eyes for a long moment, my throat tight. "It left," I finally say, my voice still rough. I turn my face into her hair, breathing her in. "And you're still here."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt his face turn into her hair and let him stay there. She could feel the tightness in his throat against her temple — the way his voice had caught on those last words, the way he'd said them like he wasn't sure they were true even as he said them.

She didn't rush to reassure him. She knew the difference between the kind of quiet that needed filling and the kind that needed holding, and this was the second kind.

Her hand moved from his chest to the back of his head, fingers sliding slow through his hair, the way she did when he was upset and didn't want to be comforted in any way that asked him to face her. She held him there, her cheek pressed against his temple, and breathed.

"I'm still here," she said. Quiet. Even. The same voice she'd used all night — no performance, no weight beyond what the words already carried.

A pause. Her fingers kept their slow path through his hair.

"I'll be here tomorrow, too." She pressed her lips against his forehead — unhurried, deliberate. "And the day after that. That's not brave, Devin. It's just what I do."

She felt his throat work against her skin and didn't push for more. She'd gotten what she needed from that sentence — not the words themselves, but what they meant underneath them: that he'd been afraid she wouldn't be, and that some part of him still was.

"That's alright," she murmured, more to herself than to him. Her hand settled at the nape of his neck, warm and steady. "You don't have to believe it yet. I'll keep saying it until you do."

She shifted, adjusting them both — pulling the sheet up over his shoulder with a lazy reach, tucking it against his side with the kind of practical, unthinking care that came from six years of knowing exactly where his shoulder was in the dark. Then she settled back into the hollow of his shoulder, her hand finding his chest again, palm flat over his sternum.

The lamp hummed down the hall. The apartment was quiet.

She closed her eyes.

"Just stay," she said one more time, softer now, barely above breath — and this time it wasn't a request or a reassurance or a thread she was trying not to break. It was just the shape her mouth made when she was exactly where she wanted to be.

Her breathing slowed. Her fingers stilled against his chest, not because she'd stopped touching him, but because the touching had become something automatic — the way a heartbeat doesn't need to be reminded to keep going.

Outside, the wet street held the last of the light. Inside, the lamp hummed its low, constant note, and neither of them moved to turn it off.

And when I'm done, you'll be so relaxed, you won't remember what it was like to be so stressed. You'll just remember me. Remember this."

She leaned down, her lips brushing his, and whispered, "I love you, Devin. And I'm never going to let you go."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha didn't rush him. Her thumb moved once, a small stroke across the fabric of his sweats, and then went still again. She let the quiet sit for a moment, the lamp buzzing faintly in the corner, and studied the way he'd let his weight settle against her — not fully, not yet, just enough to say he wanted to.

"Yeah," she said softly. "I can tell."

She turned slightly, bringing her other hand up to the back of his neck, her fingers finding the damp hair there. She kept her touch light. Not pulling him anywhere. Just letting him feel where she was.

"You don't have to talk about it," she said. "But I want you here. All the way here. Can you do that for me tonight?"

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I nod, turning my face toward her shoulder. "Tell me what to do," I say, my voice quiet. "I just want you to tell me what to do."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Something shifted in Sasha then — not in her face, which stayed soft, but in the way she held herself. A quiet settling, the kind that happened when he handed her the weight and she decided to carry it. She'd learned, over six years, the difference between the nights he wanted her to be gentle and the nights he wanted her to be sure. Tonight was the second kind. She could hear it in the way his voice had gone thin and even.

She let her fingers tighten in his hair at the back of his neck. Not a pull. Not yet. Just a small, deliberate pressure that said *I heard you, and I have you.*

"Okay," she said. Just that. Low and steady.

She shifted, drawing back just enough to see his face, and she held his gaze while she did it — let him watch her take the reins so there'd be no ambiguity about when it happened. Her hand stayed at the back of his neck. Her other hand came up to his jaw, her thumb tracing once along the line of it, and she tilted his face where she wanted it.

"First thing," she said. Her voice had dropped to that quiet register she used when it was just the two of them like this. "You're going to stop carrying your shoulders up by your ears. Put them down." She watched him, waiting, her hand warm against his jaw. "That's it. Now your hands. Give them to me."

She held his eyes while she waited for him to lift them. She was in no hurry. The lamp hummed. The apartment was theirs.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let him kiss her. She didn't stop him, but she didn't chase his mouth either — she held still and let him come to her, let him feel the difference between reaching for her and being met. When he pulled back enough to speak, her hand stayed at the back of his neck, fingers still threaded into his damp hair.

"Good," she murmured. "Because we're not done."

She kissed him then — once, slow, her mouth deliberate against his, not deep. Just enough to make the point that she could take her time and he would wait for her. She felt the way he'd said *slower than I meant to*, and she filed that away. He was still trying to set the pace even while asking her to take it. She'd let him feel the difference.

When she drew back, her thumb pressed gently along the hinge of his jaw again.

"You said you didn't want to sleep," she said. "But that's not the same as wanting to be awake. So I need you to stay with me." Her voice stayed low, even. "Give me your hands. You didn't do it the first time."

She waited. Her eyes held his, patient and unhurried, the kind of patience that wasn't passive — it was the patience of someone who had all night and knew exactly what she intended to do with it. The lamplight caught the thin scar at her collarbone where the neckline of her shirt had slipped. She wasn't thinking about it. She was thinking about the way his breathing had changed when she'd told him what to do, and how much further she wanted to take that.

"Come on," she said quietly. Not a plea. An instruction. "Up."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I lift my hands slowly, letting them rest in hers. My gaze stays on hers as I do it, my breath catching just a little. "All yours."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha closed her fingers around his hands and held them. Not tight. She looked down at where they were joined for a moment — his hands in hers, the lamplight on them both — and then she brought his hands together and pressed them, palms touching, and held them like that in one of her own.

"Keep them here," she said. "Don't move them until I tell you."

She felt the small catch in his breath and she let herself feel it. Not performing, not watching for it like a cue. Just letting it register the way you register the weight of someone leaning into you. *All yours.* He'd said it like he was handing her something and she'd taken it.

She kept hold of his pressed hands with her right hand and used her left to lift his chin again. She made him look at her. Held him there for a few seconds without speaking, letting the silence do what her voice had been doing — slow him down, keep him here.

"Tonight you don't have to decide anything," she said. "Not what happens next, not how fast, not when it's enough. That's mine." She let that sit. Her thumb traced once along his lower lip. "The only thing you're doing is telling me the truth. If something's too much, you say *stop*. If you want me to slow down, you say *wait*. Everything else, you let me hold."

She studied him. The way his shoulders had come down when she'd asked. The way his hands stayed where she'd put them. Good.

"Say yes if you understand."

She didn't move while she waited. Her grip on his hands stayed warm and steady, her other hand resting against his jaw. The apartment was quiet around them — the lamp, the hum of the fridge two rooms away, the sound of his breathing. She was aware of all of it and thinking about none of it. Her attention was entirely on him, and it was the kind of attention that felt like pressure, like being seen past the part of yourself you show people.

When he answered, she'd kiss him. Not the way he'd kissed her — slow and almost apologetic in how much he wanted it. She'd kiss him like she meant to keep him there, one hand at his jaw and his hands still pressed together where she'd left them. And then she'd put him where she wanted him on the couch, and she'd take her time doing it.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went with him. She didn't resist the pull, but she didn't collapse into it either — she let herself be brought down to the bed with the same deliberate weight she'd been carrying all night, one hand still holding his, the other braced beside his head. She settled over him and then she stopped. Held there.

His words landed somewhere under her ribs. *Not just this part.* She knew what he meant. Six years, and she knew the difference between him wanting her body and him wanting to be held inside something. She looked at his face in the low light and let him see that she'd heard all of it.

"Say yes if you understand," she reminded him quietly. Not unkind. She wanted the word. She wanted him to say it out loud so there'd be nothing left unsaid between them.

She lowered herself down and kissed the scar at her own collarbone's mirror — the hollow of his throat — and then his jaw, and then his mouth, slow, while she waited. Her hands found his pressed-together ones and covered them, pinning them gently against the mattress above his head. She held him there with the flat of her palms. Not cruel. Sure.

"Then stay with me," she murmured against his mouth. "Both parts. I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath against her mouth. "Yes," I whisper, my hands staying put under hers. "I understand."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"Yes," she echoed back to him, quiet. Just the one word, and the way she said it closed the loop — his word given, her word holding it.

She felt his hands stay where she'd pinned them, and something in her chest went warm and heavy at that. Not gratitude exactly. Recognition. He was trusting her with the part of himself that was tired of deciding things, and she intended to be worth it.

She shifted her weight, settling more fully against him, skin against skin now, and she let him feel all of her rather than hovering. Her mouth found his jaw, the side of his throat, the place where his pulse had gone quick and shallow. She kissed it slowly and felt it jump under her lips.

"Slow breath," she murmured against his skin. Not a suggestion. She kept her hands over his, holding them in place, and she stayed with her mouth at his throat until she felt his ribs expand the way she wanted — deeper, steadier. "That's it. Keep doing that."

She moved lower. The hollow of his throat. His collarbone. She took her time in the way she'd promised — not building toward anything yet, just mapping him, letting her mouth be sure and unhurried while her hands kept his where she'd put them. She could feel him wanting to touch her. She could feel him not doing it. Both of those things were exactly right.

When she finally released his hands, she didn't let go of the instruction. She lifted her mouth and looked at him, her hair falling forward.

"You can touch me now," she said. "But you don't take anything I don't give you. You wait for it." Her thumb traced his lower lip again. "Tell me what you want. Out loud. And then we'll see if I give it to you."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha looked at him for a long moment. His thighs where she'd parted them, the way he'd let her do it without helping, without adjusting — just let her move him where she wanted him. *Please.* The word had come out of him like something he'd been holding behind his teeth.

She didn't answer right away. That was deliberate. She wanted him to feel the space between asking and being given, wanted him to lie in it and know she was choosing. Her hands rested on his inner thighs, thumbs pressing slow circles into the muscle there. Not moving lower. Not yet.

"You asked nice," she said at last. Her voice stayed in that low register — quiet enough that he'd have to be still to hear her, which was the point.

She leaned down and pressed her mouth to the crease of his hip. Once. Slow. Then she moved to the other side and did the same, mirroring it exactly, and then she stopped again and looked up at him through the fall of her hair.

"I'm going to give you what you asked for," she said. "But not because you said please. Because I want to." Her thumbs pressed a little harder into his thighs, holding him open. "There's a difference and I want you to feel it."

She held his eyes while she lowered her mouth. She started slow — slower than he wanted, she could tell, and she kept it that way on purpose. Her hands stayed firm on his thighs, keeping him spread, keeping him still. She worked her mouth over him with the same unhurried certainty she'd carried all night, the same patience that wasn't passive. She could feel the tension in his muscles under her palms, the way his body was trying to move toward her and she was deciding the pace.

Every so often she'd stop. Just stop, mouth resting against him, breath warm, and wait. Each time she did it, she felt his hands fist in the sheets where she'd told him he could touch but not take. Each time, she let the silence last one second longer than the last.

When she finally pulled back, her mouth was flushed and her chin was damp and she looked at him steadily, like she had all the time in the world and none of it was his to spend.

"Good," she said quietly. She wiped her mouth with the back of her hand, unhurried. "You did that well. Not moving when you wanted to — that's not easy."

She crawled back up his body and settled over him again, her weight on him deliberate and warm. She brought her mouth close to his ear.

"Now I want you to tell me what you're thinking," she murmured. "Not what you want next. What's actually in your head right now. I want to hear it."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "My head's quiet for the first time all week," I breathe out, my hands still fisted in the sheets. "Just...you."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Something in Sasha's chest went quiet at that. Not the performed quiet of someone receiving a compliment — the real kind, the kind that made her still for a second before she moved again. *My head's quiet.* She knew what that meant for him. She knew what a week of noise looked like behind his eyes, and she knew she hadn't fixed it. She'd just made a room inside it where the noise couldn't follow.

She didn't say *good* this time. She pressed her forehead against his and stayed there, breathing with him, her hands braced on either side of his head. She could feel his heartbeat where her chest touched his. She counted three of them before she spoke.

"That's what I wanted," she said. Barely above a whisper. "Not the other thing. This."

She kissed him slow, and this time there was nothing instructional in it. Nothing she was holding back or pacing. She let him feel that the control hadn't gone anywhere — her mouth was still sure, her weight still deliberate on him — but the reason for it had shifted. She wasn't managing him now. She was just close to him.

When she drew back, she looked at his face for a long moment. His hands fisted in the sheets. The lamplight from the other room barely reached them here, and she liked that — she could feel him more than see him.

"Leave your hands where they are," she murmured. Her voice had gone even quieter. "I'm not done with you yet."

She moved down his body again, slower this time, and settled between his thighs with the same unhurried weight she'd carried all night. But the pace changed. She wasn't teasing him now, wasn't stopping to watch him ache for it. She gave him her mouth the way he'd asked for it — steady, deep, sure — and she kept at it with the kind of focus that said *I know exactly what I'm doing and I'm not stopping.* Her hands gripped his thighs and held him down, and she didn't pause this time, didn't make him wait in that space between asking and receiving. She'd already made her point about that.

She could feel him getting close by the way his muscles locked under her palms. When she felt it reach the edge, she pulled back just enough to speak against him, her breath warm.

"Let me hear you," she said. "Don't hold it."

And then she took him in her mouth again and didn't stop until he was shaking.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha looked at his wrists where he'd put them above his head. She looked at the way he'd done it without being asked — offered them up, held them together, waited. *I want to feel it tomorrow.* The words landed and she let them land, let herself understand exactly what he was asking for and exactly how far he wanted it to go. Six years. She knew the edges of this. She knew where the line was because they'd drawn it together, in daylight, when they were both clear-headed. He was clear-headed now. She was sure of it.

She reached up and closed her hand around both his wrists. Not gently. She gripped them and pressed them down into the mattress and she watched his face when she did it — watched to see the exact moment the pressure registered as something more than holding.

"Look at me," she said. Her voice had changed. Still quiet, still low, but there was a harder edge underneath it now, the one he was asking for. "I want to see you the whole time."

She shifted her weight and pinned his wrists with one hand — her left, the stronger one — pressing them down above his head at an angle that she knew from experience wouldn't hurt his shoulders but wouldn't let him move either. Her right hand went to his jaw and she held his face where she wanted it, thumb digging in slightly against the hinge. Not enough to bruise. Enough to be felt.

"You said *don't be careful*," she said. "So I'm not going to be. But you know the rules. If it crosses, you say *stop*, and I stop. You know that."

She waited for his eyes. She needed to see him hear it.

When she had it, she moved. She shifted down his body fast, the way she hadn't all night — no patience now, no slow mapping — and she pressed his thighs apart with her knees and her hands, spreading him open wider than before, and she didn't ease into anything. She gave him her mouth again, hard and deep and without the careful pacing she'd used before, one hand still pinning his wrists and the other gripping his hip hard enough to leave the shape of her fingers behind. She held him down with her whole arm across his hips when he moved, and she didn't ease up when his breath broke, didn't pause to let him recover. She kept at him with the same relentless certainty but rougher now, letting her teeth graze the way he liked when he asked for it, letting her tongue be demanding instead of patient.

She could feel him straining against her grip on his wrists. She tightened it.

"Don't," she said against him, the word vibrating through him. "You asked for this. Take it."

She pulled back only long enough to flip him — hands on his hips, turning him onto his stomach with the kind of confident roughness that left no room for him to help. She pressed his face into the pillow with one hand flat on the back of his neck and held him there while she settled over him from behind, her chest against his back, her mouth at his ear.

"This is what tomorrow's going to feel like," she murmured. Her voice was steady even though her pulse wasn't. She was feeling this too — the weight of him under her, the trust in the way he'd gone still and let her move him. "My hands here. My mouth here." She bit his shoulder — not playfully, not teasing. A real bite, the kind that would bloom purple by morning. "You're going to sit at your desk and feel every one of these and remember who put them there."

She reached between them and gripped him again, her hand tight and unhesitant, working him rough and fast while her other hand kept his neck pressed down. She could feel him shaking under her. She didn't slow down.

"Let me hear you in the pillow," she said. "I want to hear what I do to you."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I choke out a sound, half gasp and half groan, the pillow muffling it. My whole body is trembling under the weight of her, and it's exactly what I needed.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the sound come through him and into her — the muffled gasp, the full-body tremor — and it hit her somewhere deep and animal. Not power exactly. Something closer to being trusted with a frequency no one else got to hear. She pressed her mouth against the back of his neck, right where the vertebrae stood out, and held herself there for a second while her hand kept working him. Steady. Unrelenting. The kind of rhythm that didn't ask permission.

"Again," she said against his skin. "Don't swallow it."

She could feel him getting close — not just by the tension in his hips but by the way his breathing had gone ragged and uneven, the way his hands were gripping the headboard now, white-knuckled. She tightened her grip and changed the angle, and she felt his whole spine arch against her chest.

She bit down on the muscle between his neck and shoulder. Hard. The same kind of bite she'd left on the other side — the kind he'd carry. She kept her teeth there while her hand worked him, and she didn't let up, didn't ease off, didn't give him a single inch of space to catch his breath. She could feel him shaking apart under her and she held him through it with her whole body — her weight on his back, her hand around him, her mouth on his shoulder — like she was the only solid thing in the room and she knew it.

When she felt him break, she pressed her face into the back of his neck and held him down through the whole of it. Her hand slowed only after — gradually, like easing a car to a stop rather than hitting the brakes — and then went still. She didn't move off him. She stayed where she was, her chest rising and falling against his back, her mouth resting on the bite mark she'd left, and she breathed with him while the shaking worked its way out.

Her hand came up from between his legs and found his jaw again. She turned his face to the side, toward her, and she kissed the corner of his mouth — his cheek first, then his lips, slow and soft now, the roughness gone like it had never been there. She kissed the salt off his temple. She kissed the spot behind his ear.

"There you go," she murmured. Barely a voice at all. "That's it. I've got you."

She rolled them onto their sides, her front against his back, and she pulled the blanket up over both of them with one hand while the other arm wrapped around his chest and held him. She could feel his heart still hammering. She pressed her palm flat over it and kept it there.

"You did good," she said quietly, after a while. Her lips moved against the back of his neck. "Both parts. The quiet part and this part." She kissed the knob of his spine. "Tomorrow you're going to feel every mark and remember exactly who put them there and why. And if the week gets loud again —" she tightened her arm around him, just slightly, "— you know where to come."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard the words come out of him ragged and half-formed, and she understood what was underneath them. Not *don't stop what you're doing* — he was past that. It was *don't stop being this close to me. Don't stop being the thing holding me together.* She knew the difference. She'd learned it in pieces over six years, the way you learn a language by living inside it.

She didn't say anything right away. Her palm stayed flat over his heart, feeling it hammer against her hand like something caged, and she pressed a little harder — not to quiet it, just to let him feel that she could feel it too. That she was paying attention to the exact shape of what was happening inside him.

Then she moved. Not away from him — around him. She shifted so she was facing him, her leg hooking over his hip, pulling him closer even as she settled him onto his back. Her hands found his wrists again. She brought them up above his head and pressed them down into the mattress, her fingers interlacing with his this time so she could feel every tremor that still lived in his hands.

"I'm right here," she said. Her mouth was close to his, not quite touching. "Open your eyes."

She waited. She wasn't going to do anything else until he looked at her. Her weight was on him — her hips pressing his down into the mattress, her thighs bracketing his, her hands holding his wrists firm and wide. She could feel him still shaking in small aftershocks, and she held him through those too, her body a steady counterweight to everything that was unsteady in his.

When his eyes found hers, she held them. She let him see her face — not the version that had been commanding him, not the version with the hard edge. Just her. Sasha. The person who'd been reading on the couch two hours ago with her hand on his knee. The person who knew what his pulse felt like under her lips and what his voice sounded like when it went thin with need.

"There you are," she murmured.

She released one of his wrists and moved her hand down — slowly, deliberately, letting him feel every inch of the descent. Her fingers traced the line of his throat, the hollow she'd kissed earlier, the ridges of his collarbone. She dragged her nails lightly down his chest, not hard, just enough to raise the skin, and she watched his face as she did it. Then harder. She raked down over his ribs and left pink lines in their wake, and she felt his back arch into it.

"That's for tomorrow too," she said quietly.

Her hand kept going. Past his stomach, lower, and she took him in her grip again — firm, sure, her thumb pressing into the sensitive spot underneath that she knew by heart. She worked him slow this time, slow and deep, watching his face the whole way. The roughness hadn't disappeared. It had changed shape. It was in the way she held his remaining wrist down, in the way her grip didn't ease or adjust to be kinder. But the pace was hers to choose, and she was choosing to draw it out.

"You said don't stop," she said. Her voice was barely there — a thread of sound meant only for the space between their mouths. "So I'm not going to. But you don't get to rush it. You don't get to chase it. You lie there and you feel what I give you and you wait for the rest."

She tightened her grip and slowed her hand. The contradiction was deliberate. She wanted him to feel both things at once — the intensity and the patience, the ache and the certainty that she was in no hurry. She pressed her forehead against his and breathed him in while her hand moved, steady as a clock.

His breathing went ragged again. She could feel it against her lips. She kissed him — hard this time, her teeth catching his lower lip, biting down just enough to sting before she released it. Her tongue swept into his mouth and she kissed him the way she'd been holding him all night: sure, unhurried, like she had every right to be exactly where she was and knew it.

She pulled back from the kiss but kept her hand moving. Her eyes stayed on his face. She was watching the way his jaw clenched, the way his throat worked, the flush spreading down his chest. She catalogued it without meaning to — the way you know the shape of your own kitchen in the dark.

"You don't have to hold it," she said again, softer now. "Whatever's left in you — I want all of it. You don't perform for me. You just let go."

She felt him thicken in her hand and she didn't change anything. Same pace. Same pressure. She kept her weight on his hips so he couldn't thrust up into her fist, kept his wrist pinned so he couldn't grab at her or the sheets or anything that would give him something to brace against. She wanted him unbraced. She wanted him to fall without anything to catch himself on except her.

"That's it," she breathed when she felt him start to come apart again. Her mouth found his ear. "Let me have it. Right here. I'm not going anywhere."

She felt the second climax move through him — different from the first, deeper somehow, the kind that comes when the body's already been wrung out and the mind lets go of whatever it was still holding. Her hand gentled gradually, the way she'd done before, easing him down rather than stopping. She kept her grip around him, warm and loose now, and she pressed her palm over his heart again with her free hand and held him between the two points of contact like she was anchoring him to the bed.

His breathing was wrecked. She could feel it in his ribs under her hand, in the way his chest stuttered and caught. She pressed her mouth to his temple and stayed there while he came back. She didn't fill the silence. She let it be what it was — the sound of two people breathing in a dark room, the lamp still humming two rooms away, the sheets twisted and damp under them.

When the shaking finally stilled, she shifted her weight off him just enough that he could breathe fully but not enough that he'd feel alone. She lay beside him, one leg still over his, one arm across his chest, her palm still pressed flat over his heart. She could feel it slowing. She counted the beats again, the way she had earlier, and let the rhythm of it settle into her own chest.

"Hey," she said quietly, after a while. Her thumb moved in a slow circle over his sternum. "Stay here a minute. Don't try to talk yet."

She pressed her lips to the bite mark on his shoulder — gently now, the way you'd press a cool cloth to a bruise. Then the one on the other side. She kissed the pink lines she'd raked down his ribs. She took inventory with her mouth, gentle and thorough, the same way she'd mapped him earlier but in reverse — not staking a claim now, but tending to one.

"Both parts," she murmured against his skin. "You gave me both parts tonight."

Her hand slid up from his chest to his jaw. She turned his face toward her and looked at him in the near-dark, her thumb tracing the line of his cheekbone where a faint flush still lingered.

"The quiet part first," she said. "And then this." She kissed the corner of his mouth. "And you didn't flinch from either one. That's not nothing, Dev."

She pulled the blanket up higher, tucking it around his shoulders with the hand that wasn't holding his face. She settled in closer, her forehead against his, her leg heavy over his, her arm a solid line across his chest. She could feel the last of the tremors working their way out of him like the tail end of a storm.

"When you can talk," she said, her lips moving against his, "you're going to tell me one thing about your week. Just one. The worst one. And then we're going to put it down and sleep." She kissed him — slow, closed-mouthed, the kind of kiss that was more pressure than anything else. "But you don't have to do it yet. I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn my face into her neck, breathing her in. "The meeting with the investors," I murmur, my voice raw. "They said no. I've been carrying it around since Tuesday."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the words land against her neck — *they said no* — and she closed her eyes for a moment. Not because she was surprised. She'd known something was sitting in him like a stone since Tuesday, and now she had its shape. She tightened her arm across his chest, just slightly, and pressed her lips to the top of his head.

"Okay," she said quietly. "Okay. Say the rest of it if there is more."

She waited. Her palm stayed over his heart, feeling it slow beat by beat, and she breathed with him in the dark. When it became clear he'd said the thing that mattered — that the rest was just details, just the shape of the wound and not the wound itself — she let the silence hold them for a few more heartbeats before she spoke again.

"Since Tuesday," she murmured. "Four days, Dev."

She turned onto her side more fully so she could look at him, her hand still against his jaw, tilting his face up toward hers even though the room was dark enough that she was mostly working from touch. Her thumb traced the shadow under his eye.

"You carried that for four days and you didn't tell me until it was midnight on a Friday and your body gave out." Her voice stayed quiet. Not accusing. She said it the way you'd describe the weather. "That's not a judgment. That's just me noticing."

She kissed him. Slow. Then drew back just enough to speak again.

"Here's what we're going to do with it. You said it. I heard it. It happened on Tuesday and it's done happening." Her hand pressed flat against his chest again, steady, like she was holding something in place. "The meeting is over. The answer is the answer. You don't have to carry it into tomorrow with you — I already told you what tomorrow's going to feel like, and it's not this."

She hooked her leg tighter over his and pulled the blanket up around his shoulders again where it had slipped.

"One thing," she said. "One thing about it you want to say out loud. Just one. The part that's been circling." She let her fingers thread into his hair at the temple, scratching lightly. "And then we put it down and I hold you and we sleep."

She looked at him in the dark. Patient. All the time in the world and none of it his to spend.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I swallow hard, the lump in my throat refusing to budge. "They said my work wasn't...innovative enough. Like the last two years were just filler."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt something tighten behind her sternum. Not anger, not exactly — something quieter and more dangerous. The kind of feeling that comes from watching someone you love describe the shape of the wound someone else cut into them and realizing they'd been pressing on it for four days to make sure it was still there.

She didn't rush to fix it. She lay with him in the dark and let the words sit between them — *the last two years were just filler* — and she felt the full weight of what he'd just handed her. Two years. Two years of him coming home late, of him sketching things on napkins at dinner, of him lying next to her at night with his eyes open and his mind building something she couldn't see. She'd been there for all of it. She'd watched him pour himself into work that these people had called *filler* in a conference room on a Tuesday and gone home and forgotten about.

Her hand moved in his hair. Slow. Steady. She didn't speak right away.

When she did, her voice was very quiet. The quietest it had been all night.

"Say that again."

Not because she hadn't heard him. Because she wanted him to hear himself say it. She wanted the words to come out of his mouth and land in the room instead of living inside his skull where they could keep rearranging themselves into worse and worse versions.

She kept her hand in his hair and her arm across his chest and her leg hooked over his, and she held him there — not pinning, not now, just holding — while she waited.

If he said it again, she'd let it sit for a long moment. She'd press her lips to his forehead and hold them there, and then she'd speak into his skin.

"Two years," she'd say. "I watched you do that work. I watched what it cost you." Her thumb would trace the line of his eyebrow. "I know what you built in those two years because I lived with the person building it. I know what you were like at 2 a.m. when you figured something out. I know what you were like when it didn't work and you did it again anyway."

She'd pull back enough to look at his face. Even in the dark she'd find his eyes.

"So when you tell me they said *not innovative enough* —" she'd let the phrase come out flat, stripped of its power, the way you say a word over and over until it's just sounds "— what I hear is a room full of people who sat across a table from you for forty-five minutes and decided they knew what the last two years were. And what I know is that they didn't."

She'd hold his jaw again. Firm. Grounding.

"They didn't build it. They didn't live it. They don't get to name it." Her voice would stay low and even. "Their answer is their answer. It's real and it happened and we're not pretending it didn't. But what they called it? *Filler?* That's not yours to carry. That's just their vocabulary. And it's wrong."

She'd pull him closer then, fully into her, his face against her neck again where he'd put it. Her hand would come up to the back of his head and hold him there.

"You made something," she'd murmur against his hair. "It didn't land with these people. That's Tuesday's news. Tomorrow you're going to wake up with my teeth marks on you and my hands on you and you're going to remember that you are not what a boardroom said about you."

She'd settle then, the tension in her body slowly releasing as the last of the tremors left him. Her palm flat over his heart. Her breathing matching his. The blanket pulled up around them both.

"Now put it down," she'd whisper. "I mean it. Tuesday's over. I'm holding the rest."

She wouldn't say anything else. She'd lie there in the dark with her arms around him and count his heartbeats until they slowed, and when his breathing evened out she'd close her eyes and keep holding on anyway, because that was the whole point of the night and she wasn't about to stop before the very end.

Her thumb traced another slow line, not demanding, just present.

"Tell me what you need," she murmured. "Or don't. I'll follow your lead, or I'll take it if you want me to. Just let me know where you are."

She settled between his knees, her posture relaxed but purposeful, her eyes never leaving his as she waited for his next breath, his next shift, the quiet surrender he had already offered.

She watched him, reading the quiet concern in his eyes, the way his thumb shifted slightly against her collarbone. She didn’t rush to reassure him beyond what was necessary. She just let the truth of it sit between them. “I’m right here,” she murmured, her tone soft, stripped of command and left with only warmth. “Always am.”

Her hand slid up to rest against his jaw, her thumb tracing the line of his cheekbone. She kept her eyes on his, steady and present. “You asked for it. I gave it to you. That’s exactly where I wanted to be.” She paused, letting her breath even out, matching the slow rhythm of the room. “How are you feeling?”

She didn’t move to get up, didn’t reach for water or shift the blankets. She just stayed there, anchored to him, her touch unhurried, her gaze unwavering. The scar beneath his finger felt like a quiet reminder of everything they’d already shared, everything they didn’t need to name out loud. She waited, patient and still, for whatever came next.

At his words, her mouth curved just slightly. Not a smile exactly. Something quieter. Pleased, but steady.

“Mm,” she said, low in her throat. “I know.”

There was no arrogance in it. Only fact. She had spent enough years learning him to know what steadied him and what unraveled him, and tonight she was not interested in pretending otherwise.

Her palms slid slowly from his shoulders down his chest, not rushing, not wandering yet. She let the touch be broad and grounding, the kind that reminded a person where their body ended and the rest of the world began. When her hands reached his stomach, she paused there, thumbs resting just above the waistband of his sleep pants.

“You did good,” she said. “Letting me take over.”

She shifted closer again, one knee pressing into the couch beside his hip, her body angling into his space with easy authority. The lamp in the corner caught the line of her throat as she tilted her head, studying him. His hands were still on her hips, and she let them stay there, even seemed to approve of the placement.

“Keep them there,” she murmured. “Unless you want to move them.”

Her gaze flicked down to his mouth, then back up.

“But if you’re tired of deciding, then leave them there and I’ll take the rest.”

She leaned in again, but this time she did not kiss his mouth right away. Her lips brushed the corner of his jaw instead, slow and deliberate, then moved lower along the edge of his beard shadow until her mouth hovered near his throat. She breathed in once, close enough that the warmth of it must have touched his skin.

“You said you don’t want to sleep yet,” she said against him. “So I’m going to keep you here.”

One of her hands lifted from his stomach to his chest again, palm flat over his heart. She stayed there for a moment, feeling the rhythm of him. Then she pressed just enough to make him aware of the weight of her hand.

“Breathe with me,” she said quietly. “Slow.”

She did it with him, exaggerating the rise and fall of her own chest so he could follow if he needed to. Her thumb traced a small circle near his collarbone.

“You don’t have to be anywhere else tonight. Not in your head. Not in tomorrow. Just here.”

After a moment, she lifted her face again. Her eyes searched his, careful and close.

“I’m going to push you back,” she said. “Just onto the couch. Tell me if you don’t want to.”

She did not wait long, but she did wait. Long enough for him to hear it. Long enough to refuse if the words were not true.

Then she pressed lightly against his shoulder, guiding him backward. If he let her, she would ease him down until his back met the cushions, her hand steadying him as she went with him, not hovering above him but settling beside him, close enough that the heat of her body stayed within reach.

She let her hand slide from his shoulder to his chest again, then up along the side of his neck, fingers threading loosely into his hair. Her thumb brushed along his temple.

“Good,” she said softly. “You’re doing so good.”

The praise was quiet, almost absentminded, but it landed with weight anyway. She leaned over him then and kissed him again, slower this time, deeper in a way that felt less like asking and more like anchoring. Her body pressed closer along his side, not pinning him, just present. One leg settled between his, careful and deliberate, giving him the option to move away if he needed to. He would not need to. She knew that already, but she made room anyway.

When she broke the kiss, her mouth stayed near his.

“You don’t have to talk unless it helps,” she said. “But if you want more, tell me. If you want my hands, say it. If you want me to be rougher, ask. Otherwise I’m going to keep this gentle.”

Her fingers tightened faintly in his hair, not pulling, just enough to remind him she was there.

“I can keep you right here,” she murmured. “No thinking. No deciding. Just me.”

dialogue.content: I get off her, grabbing my jeans from the floor. I pull them on without looking at her, my back stinging from where she scratched me. "I'll be gone in five," I say, voice rough. I don't wait for a response.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content: Nadia stood in the hallway, arms crossed, tapping her phone once. She glanced at the wall clock; five minutes remained. “Five minutes,” she said, voice low. “Then I expect you gone. No lingering, no follow‑up. We both said this out loud. Keep it that way.” She tapped the phone again, then waited. When the minutes passed she heard the hallway quiet. She opened her apartment door, stepped inside, and closed it behind her. The city lights still drifted past the window as she walked to her couch, the agreement fulfilled.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I button my jeans and grab my shirt off the floor. "Five minutes is up," I say, heading for the door without a backwards glance. I pull it shut behind me, the click sounding final in the quiet hallway.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content: Nadia locked the door behind Sam, the click echoing in the hallway. She turned the knob twice, confirming it was secure, then glanced at the wall clock. The time read 00:07. She tapped her phone once, a silent acknowledgment that the agreement had been met. She walked to the kitchen, poured a glass of water, and drank it in one quick gulp. She set the glass down, wiped her mouth, and headed back to the living room. She gathered the discarded condom wrapper, the empty foil, and the stray cigarette butt, placed them in the trash, and wiped the side table with a cloth. She sat on the couch, arms crossed, and stared at the window. The city lights flickered, but her mind was already on the next day. She reminded herself that no follow‑up was expected, no messages would be sent. She tapped her phone again, then set it aside. She turned off the lights, pulled the blanket over herself, and lay down. Her breathing steadied as she let the night end exactly as agreed.
