dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The salle had emptied an hour ago and Corvo was still there, because of course he was, rewrapping a grip that did not need rewrapping.

"Three-two," he said, without looking up. "I want it on record that the third was generous."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "It's on record that you were slow," I say, and drop my bag next to his.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s hands stilled around the roll of tape.

“Slow,” he repeated, as if testing the weight of the word against a blade. Then he looked up, dark eyes sharp with amusement and something less easily named. “I let you have three because you looked miserable waiting for them.”

He set the foil down across the bench with deliberate care, aligning it parallel to the edge as though precision might keep him contained. It did not.

“You say that like it’s an insult,” Corvo continued, voice lower now, roughened at the edges. “I’ve been needling you for four years, Reyes. If I wanted to wound you, I’d bring receipts.”

A beat passed. The empty salle felt too quiet around them, the lamps humming overhead, the stripped floorboards still holding the ghost of footsteps and steel.

Corvo leaned back just enough to create distance, then did not take it fully. His gaze stayed fixed on Reyes, open and unblinking.

“So tell me,” he said. “Are you here to argue the score?”

His mouth curved, faint and dangerous.

“Or are you here because you’ve decided generosity is worth investigating?”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "I'm here because you're still in my salle," I say, picking up the foil he just set down. I spin it in my hand, feeling the balance. "And because you're wrong about why you gave me those points."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo let the phrase *my salle* land, and something dry moved behind his expression—not offense, exactly. Recognition, maybe. Amusement sharpened by it.

“Is that a complaint?” he asked. “Or an invitation to get put out?”

He rose from the bench with the unhurried economy of a man who had spent years making other people rush. The tape roll clicked softly against the wood as he brushed it aside. Corvo came close enough to see the foil turning in Reyes’ hand, close enough to catch the cold metal scent of the salle and the warmth left behind by exertion, but he did not reach for the weapon.

“Careful,” he said, quieter now. “That balance is mine.”

His gaze lifted and held.

“And if I’m wrong,” Corvo continued, “then correct me. I gave you three touches. You took them. You’re standing there telling me I don’t know why my hand opened when it did.” A faint curve touched his mouth. “So say it, Reyes. Was I being generous? Merciful? Bored?” He paused, letting the last word fray at the edges. “Or were you hoping I’d finally admit I wanted the bout to last longer?”

The question hung between them, openly barbed.

Corvo tipped his head, patient as a scorekeeper.

“Your point.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I take the grip out of his hands and put it down, and I don't step back afterwards. "You've been slow all evening," I say.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo looked down at the foil Reyes had set aside, then back up. His fingers were empty now, and he did not seem displeased by it.

“Slow,” he said again, weighing the word as though it might still be useful. “All evening.”

A low smile touched him, the kind that admitted nothing while promising a great deal.

“If I was slow, you had every chance to make me pay for it. You didn’t.” His gaze held, steady and unapologetic. “So I will assume one of two things: either you have become merciful, which I refuse to believe, or you were enjoying the view.”

The teasing note was still there, but it had worn thin over something more direct. Corvo shifted his weight, closing only the fraction of distance his pride would allow without surrendering the entire field.

“You want the truth?” he asked. “I gave you three because the bout was ending. I have been slow since because I cannot decide whether I want this one to end at all.”

He tilted his head, patient, dangerous.

“Now. Are you going to keep accusing me of poor timing, or are you going to tell me what you would have done with the extra tempo?”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I don't want extra tempo." I move closer, bridging the gap he left open. "I want to know why you care how it ends."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo did not retreat. The closeness registered in him at once—heat, scent, the impossible quiet of a room that had just become smaller. He held still with the discipline of a man who knew exactly how much ground he was yielding and how much he intended to take.

“Caring,” he said, testing the word like a blade whose edge he distrusted. “Yes. That appears to be the problem.”

His eyes lifted, dark and unblinking.

“I care how it ends because I have spent four years turning you into a score I can carry around without admitting what else you are.” A faint, rueful smile moved his mouth. “You know the routine. We fence. We trade insults. You leave. I stand there feeling clever for an hour and then useless for the rest of the night.”

The admission cost him something, but Corvo paid it anyway.

“So when you ask why I care—because if this ends with a salute and a door closing, I’ll have to go back to pretending the only thing between us is steel. And I am very bad at pretending tonight.”

He raised one hand slowly, palm half-open, fingers not quite reaching Reyes’ jaw. An invitation, not a theft.

“I don’t want extra tempo either,” he said, voice lower now, stripped of performance. “I want the truth. Are you staying to finish the argument, or are you staying because you want to see how far needling can go before one of us stops fencing?”

His gaze dropped briefly, then returned with naked challenge.

“Tell me to back off, and I will. Cleanly. Without making a joke of it. But if you don’t—” The breath he took was almost a laugh. “Then stop asking why I care and let me show you that I stopped being generous a long time ago.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: We get as far as the changing-room bench and not one step further. Kit goes on the floor, both of ours, and neither of us is being quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: My fingers are already working the fastenings of his jacket, not gentle. "You talk too much for a man who's trying to stop fencing."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo went still beneath the roughness of it, the kind of stillness that was not peace but a blade held at the point of release. For a heartbeat he did not answer. Then his mouth twitched.

“Four years,” he said, lower now, scraped clean of its usual polish, “and you still come at my collar like you expect to win by surprise.”

His hands came up, not to stay the work at his jacket, but to further it. He lifted his shoulders and let the fencing jacket break loose, sliding down his arms until it joined the litter on the floor with a soft, expensive thud. Corvo did not look at it. He was already fighting the top buttons of his shirt, fingers less certain than they had ever been with foil and tape, and he cursed the fabric under his breath with the personal offense of a man who blamed equipment for his own lack of restraint.

When the shirt fell open enough, he let it hang, heat and exertion and something sharper written along his throat. One hand braced on the bench behind him, keeping the distance exact, measured, maddening.

“You’re right,” Corvo admitted. “I talk too much.”

His gaze dropped, then lifted again, dark and unblinking.

“So take the advantage. Before I remember how to be insufferable.”

Then he stopped making excuses. Corvo leaned in until his breath warmed Reyes’s mouth and kissed him—not gently, not like a man rewrapping a grip that did not need rewrapping, but like a man who had spent four years circling the same opening and had finally decided to stop pretending he meant to miss it.

When he drew back, his voice was wrecked at the edges, but the needling survived, thin and bright as wire.

“Your touch,” he said. “And the third was still generous.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I get him flat on the bench and take my time about it with my mouth, which is the first thing all evening he hasn't had an answer for.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: He makes a sound like I’ve finally disarmed him and I can feel him twitch underneath me. I pull back just enough to look him in the eye, my own breath coming short. “Generous,” I repeat against his skin. “Let’s hear you argue that score now.”

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s answer came apart in his throat before it could become speech.

His shoulders pressed into the bench, chest working with breath that refused to obey him, and for once the room’s geometry failed him entirely. There was no line to hold, no distance he could measure and name, no clean tempo in which to hide.

When he finally looked up, his eyes were dark with strain—and something dangerously close to delight.

“Argue,” he repeated, as if the word had been taken apart and put back together wrong. “You want me to argue that score after—”

A rough laugh broke out of him, uneven and wrecked.

“Gods, Reyes.”

His hand came up, trembling slightly, and settled at the back of Reyes’ neck. Not to push away.

To keep.

“Fine,” Corvo said, voice lowered into the seam between confession and provocation. “The third was generous. I gave it because I wanted you to stay.”

His thumb moved once, slow, against skin.

“The fourth was not generosity.” His gaze sharpened despite the ruin in his breathing. “The fourth was greed. The fifth was revenge for four years of you walking out of my salle looking like you’d won something you hadn’t earned.”

He arched faintly against the bench, chasing the aftershock and hating himself for it.

“And if you think I’m going to lie now and call this mercy,” he went on, each word dragged out like tape unwinding, “then you have never paid attention to any of my matches.”

A pause. The lamps hummed overhead. The salle smelled of leather, metal, sweat, and the warm animal mess of two people who had stopped pretending.

Corvo’s mouth curved, crooked and open.

“So there’s your argument. Three points: generosity. Everything after: yours, taken fair.” His breath hitched, then steadied with visible effort. “Unless you’d rather I pretend I’m still the man giving you gifts.”

His fingers tightened just enough to be felt.

“Say the word and I’ll make it ugly again.” Then, softer, with the needling surviving only because it was part of his skeleton: “But you don’t want ugly. You want close.”

A beat.

Corvo held his gaze, ruined and defiant.

“I’ve wanted close since the first time you corrected my line and I pretended not to notice.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Prove the point properly," he says, "or concede," so I pin his wrists to the bench and stop letting him set the pace, which is exactly what he was asking for.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: The bench creaks under us, loud in the quiet room. I lean down, my mouth brushing his ear. "You gave three because you were stalling," I say, my voice rough. "You've been stalling for years."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo did not pull against the pins. He tested them once, found them honest, and went still in the way a fencer goes still when the distance has been stolen from him.

“Stalling,” he repeated, and the word broke into a rough laugh. “That is the most dangerous thing you have said all night, because it is true.”

His chest rose and fell under the weight of Reyes’ hands, heat spreading along the bench. “I gave three because I wanted more time. I kept the measure loose because I wanted you to step into it. I talked because if I stopped, I would have put my mouth where my arguments belong and lost four years of very expensive dignity.”

He tilted his chin, exposing the line of his throat, eyes dark with surrender and challenge braided together.

“Concede?” Corvo’s voice dropped. “Fine. I concede. I have been stalling. I have been afraid of how close you make me feel when you do not even draw steel.”

A muscle jumped in his jaw as the pressure held. He did not beg, not exactly, but the needling thinned to something raw.

“But if I am conceding,” he said, “do not take it politely. I have spent four years being polite across a strip. Take the point. Take the bout. Prove I was waiting for you to finish what I kept starting.”

His pinned fingers flexed once, helpless and eager.

“I am done arguing the score, Reyes. Make me lose it.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: Neither of us is quiet and neither of us cares who locks up. "Don't stop," he says, for once not arguing. (OOC: write the scene through, no fade.)

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I finally get him to stop talking by taking his mouth with mine again, messy and desperate. "That's the point," I growl against his lips, my own hands shaking. "You already lost it."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: My hands slide up to tangle in his hair, holding him there. "Now shut up and take the win."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: He does shut up. For a long, breathless moment, the only sounds are the creak of the bench and our ragged breathing. Then he shudders, and his whole body goes taut before he finally, truly, lets go.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Maitresse Vex inclined her head slightly in acknowledgment. The straps were secure, the toys laid out in precise order, the lighting adjusted to her exacting standards. She reached for the first implement—a supple leather flogger, well-worn from use but meticulously maintained. 

"Tonight we revisit endurance," she said, her voice calm and measured. "You'll count each stroke aloud. Clear enunciation, please." She let the tails trail lightly over Ari's bare shoulder, a whisper of what was to come. "We begin at twenty. If I'm satisfied with your form, we may adjust upward." 

She stepped back, letting the anticipation settle between them before raising the flogger in a smooth arc.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: *I breathe in deeply, steadying myself.* "Yes, Maitresse. Twenty." My knuckles tighten against the straps as I wait.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The first stroke landed with practiced precision across the upper back, firm but not brutal—a warm-up, testing the waters. Maitresse Vex paused just long enough to observe the ripple of tension before speaking.  

"Count," she reminded, her tone even. She wasn't one for unnecessary cruelty, but neither would she tolerate inattention. The next stroke followed in quick succession, mirroring the first in intensity. Her movements were economical, unhurried; she had all the time in the world to ensure each strike served its purpose.  

"Let's hear that voice, pet." The tails whispered through the air again. "Or shall we start the count over?"  

Ari:
"One," I gasp, then force steadiness into my voice. "Two."

Maitresse Vex:
"Better." The corner of her mouth twitched—not quite a smile, but approval all the same. The next three strokes came in steady rhythm, each one a deliberate fraction harder than the last, warming the skin beneath.  

"Three. Four. Five," she echoed as Ari counted, her own voice a cool counterpoint to their sharp breaths. She noted the way their fingers flexed against the restraints, the minute adjustments of stance—good signs, engagement without distress.  

She paused after the fifth, letting the sting settle. "Posture," she reminded, tapping the flogger lightly against the small of Ari's back. "Shoulders square. Or would you prefer I correct it for you?"

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Maitresse Vex arched a brow at the admission, though her expression remained otherwise unreadable. She circled slowly, the flogger's tails whispering against her thigh as she assessed Ari's position with a critical eye.  

"Thinking isn't doing," she remarked. Her free hand pressed firmly between their shoulder blades, adjusting their stance by incremental degrees. "But we'll see how well your anticipation serves you tonight."  

The next stroke landed just below the previous set, a controlled snap that left a faint blush in its wake. "Six," she prompted, her voice low. "And do try to keep from squandering my patience with chatter." The admonishment held no real heat—tonight was about focus, not silence.  

She adjusted her grip slightly, the next arc of the flogger already in motion.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: My back tenses under the new line of fire, but I keep my shoulders square. "Six," I say, my voice only shaking a little. I clench my jaw, waiting for seven.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Maitresse Vex observed the tension, the controlled breath—good signs of engagement rather than distress. She rewarded the effort with a stroke that was marginally sharper, just enough to make the count hitch.  

"Seven," she supplied when Ari caught their breath, her tone as precise as her aim. The next two followed in quick succession, each striking where the skin was already flushed. "Eight. Nine." She paused to run her fingers lightly over the warmth, gauging the reaction.  

"You're taking these well," she remarked, not quite praise but acknowledgment all the same. The flogger tapped idly against her palm as she considered. "Shall we continue to twenty as planned? Or would you like to negotiate an extension?" The offer was clinical, detached—no pressure, only possibility.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The quiet admission earned a faint hum of acknowledgment. She let the rope slide through her fingers with deliberate slowness, the coarse fibers whispering against Ari's skin.  

"Explanations are rarely necessary when one maintains proper form," she remarked, her fingers tracing the path of the last knot before tightening it incrementally. "But we'll ensure you have no cause for concern either way."  

Her hands stilled, assessing the tension. Satisfied, she reached for the next length of rope, her movements methodical. "Breathe," she reminded, not unkindly, as she began the next intricate bind. "And tell me—how far past composure *exactly* are we?" The question held a quiet edge of challenge beneath its calm.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath as the rope tightens again. "Past counting, Maitresse. Just...feeling."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Maitresse Vex arched one elegant brow, her fingers pausing their work just long enough to convey mild disapproval. "Feeling is acceptable," she said, her voice cool as she resumed the precise loops of rope. "But counting remains mandatory."  

She pulled the next knot snug, not cruel but uncompromising. "We'll begin the tally again at one. And this time," she added, a thread of steel entering her tone, "you'll keep your wits about you long enough to reach twenty."  

The first measured stroke of the flogger landed with deliberate precision. "One," she intoned, waiting. The tails whispered against her thigh as she raised them again. "Unless you require another reminder of why we maintain discipline?"

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Maitresse Vex tilted her head, observing the tremors with clinical interest. The flogger dangled idly from her fingers as she stepped closer.  

"Verbalizing needs is progress," she remarked, though her tone gave no quarter. She traced a single fingertip along the heated skin of Ari's shoulder. "But you'll have to be more specific, pet. I don't reward vagueness."  

She applied the faintest pressure to a particularly sensitive knot of rope. "Try again. Properly." The implicit *or else* hung in the air between them, weighty as the flogger in her hand.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: *I swallow hard, my throat tight.* "Permission to...to come down a little, Maitresse. Please." I hate how small my voice sounds.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Maitresse Vex considered the request with her usual detached precision. She set the flogger aside with deliberate care before stepping into Ari's line of sight.  

"Permission granted—partially." Her fingers found the first knot at their wrist, loosening just enough to ease the bite without compromising the restraint entirely. "Breathe," she instructed, her palm flat between their shoulder blades. "In for four. Hold for seven."  

She maintained the pressure until their breathing steadied, her own exhale measured. "Better," she murmured, though it wasn't quite praise. "Now. Do you wish to continue, or shall we conclude?" Her tone made it clear—either answer would be honored, but hesitation would not.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Maitresse Vex's lips curved into something too sharp to be called a smile. She retrieved the flogger with deliberate slowness, letting its tails whisper against her thigh as she circled back into position.  

"Greedy tonight, aren't we?" Her tone was ice-edged amusement. The first stroke landed with surgical precision, just shy of brutal. "Then you'll take what I give you *properly*." Another, harder. "Eyes forward." A third, perfectly placed to overlap the first. "And if I hear that voice waver again before twenty, we start over from zero."  

She paused, letting the threat settle like the heat blooming across skin. "Understood?" The flogger hovered, poised for either mercy or escalation—the choice, as ever, was theirs.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "I understand, Maitresse." I fix my eyes straight ahead, the new fire across my back a sharp anchor. My voice is steadier now, edged with resolve. "Please continue."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Maitresse Vex observed the straightened spine, the renewed focus—satisfactory.  

"Ten," she announced, the stroke landing with crisp efficiency. She didn't wait for confirmation before following with the next, a fraction harder. "Eleven." Her voice was a blade's edge, honed and indifferent. "You'll thank me for each one now. Properly."  

The twelfth strike bit deep, precisely where the rope had left its mark. "Twelve, *Maitresse*," she corrected before they could speak, her free hand gripping their hair just shy of painful. "And mind your manners unless you'd like to relearn them from scratch."  

She released them with a slight push, stepping back to assess the flush of skin, the controlled tremors. "Again." The flogger rose. "Or shall we discuss the consequences of wasted time?"

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Maitresse Vex didn't soften at the safeword check—if anything, her posture grew more exacting. She noted the ragged breath, the white-knuckled grip on the restraints, and adjusted her next stroke accordingly.  

"Thirteen," she stated, the flogger landing with controlled precision along the crest of a shoulder blade. "Thank me." Her voice brooked no hesitation. When the response came, she tilted her head. "Louder."  

The fourteenth strike overlapped the previous one, drawing a sharp inhale. She waited, flogger poised. "Fourteen. *Properly.*" Her free hand gripped their chin, forcing eye contact. "Or must I demonstrate how much worse *ingratitude* feels?" The threat hung in the air like the scent of warmed leather.  

She released them only to deliver the fifteenth with deliberate cruelty, striking where skin was already sensitized. "Fifteen." Her voice was silk over steel. "You *will* remember your place by the time we're done."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Thank you, Maitresse," I force out, louder, my throat raw. The grip on my chin sends a fresh wave of submission straight through me. "Fourteen. Thank you, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Maitresse Vex held the flogger still for a heartbeat, allowing the gratitude to linger in the air between them. Not quite praise, but acknowledgment nonetheless.  

"Better," she conceded, though her tone remained unyielding. The sixteenth stroke landed with calculated force, just below the last. "Sixteen." Her voice was a whip-crack of command. "Again—with *conviction*."  

She didn't wait for the words before delivering the seventeenth, the tails biting into already heated skin. "Seventeen." Her free hand pressed flat between their shoulder blades, forcing their chest forward. "Or would you prefer I *remind* you how to show proper appreciation?" The edge in her voice promised nothing gentle.  

The flogger rose again, poised for the next strike. "Choose your next words carefully, pet."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I feel the press of her hand like a brand. "Seventeen. Thank you, Maitresse," I say, the words scraped raw but clear. I don't look away from the spot on the wall.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Maitresse Vex observed the unwavering gaze, the ragged but unwavering compliance. She rewarded it with a stroke that straddled the line between pain and punishment—sharp enough to draw a gasp, but not enough to break form.  

"Eighteen," she announced, her voice as precise as the strike itself. Her fingers trailed lightly over the fresh mark, assessing. "Almost there." The words held no comfort, only fact.  

The nineteenth landed with deliberate overlap, drawing a flush where pale skin met rope. She paused, flogger suspended. "Nineteen. Last one deserves special attention, doesn't it?" Her thumb pressed into a particularly sensitive knot, just shy of cruel. "Make it worth my while."  

The final stroke came not with the flogger, but her palm—a crisp, stinging slap where the tails had left their pattern. "Twenty." She stepped back, surveying her work with a critical eye. "Adequate."  

She set the flogger aside with deliberate care before loosening the first wrist restraint. "Now. What do we say when Maitresse is finished with us?" Her fingers lingered on the buckle, waiting.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: *I take a shaky breath, the release of the restraint making my arm tremble.* "Thank you for my discipline, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The salle had emptied an hour ago and Corvo was still there, because of course he was, rewrapping a grip that did not need rewrapping.

"Three-two," he said, without looking up. "I want it on record that the third was generous."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "It's on record that you were slow," I say, and drop my bag next to his.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo kept his eyes on the leather strip, his fingers moving with practiced precision. The salle smelled of sweat, polished wood, and the faint metallic tang of steel. Four years of barbed exchanges and scored touches had built a rhythm between them, but tonight the tempo had shifted. He finally lifted his gaze, meeting Reyes’s over the top of the wrapped grip. A slow, deliberate smile touched his mouth.

"Slow is a matter of perspective," he said, his voice lower than his usual match-shout. He set the blade down carefully on the bench, the quiet click echoing in the empty room. "I preferred it measured. Gave me time to appreciate how you telegraphed your remise." He leaned back against the equipment rack, crossing his arms over his chest. The competitive edge was still there, but it had softened into something heavier, more deliberate. "Besides, if I’d been faster, we wouldn’t be standing here like this."

He let the words settle, his posture relaxed but attentive, watching the space between them. The banter had always been a dance, but tonight the steps had changed, and Corvo had no intention of stepping back.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I let out a short laugh and lean against the bench, close enough to feel the warmth he's giving off. "So now you're critiquing my form? After I won?" I pick up the discarded foil, testing its weight. "Maybe you just like watching me move."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo watched the foil shift in Reyes’s hand, the familiar curl of fingers around the grip, the easy weight of it. He let out a quiet breath, something between a sigh and a low chuckle. The salle felt smaller now, the air thicker, the usual echo of steel and footwork replaced by the steady rhythm of his own pulse. Four years of parries, ripostes, and carefully measured insults had all been leading to this exact proximity.

"I've always liked watching you move," he admitted, the words slipping out without the usual defensive edge. He pushed off the equipment rack, closing the distance until the space between them was measured in heartbeats rather than meters. His voice dropped, steady and clear. "But you're misreading the critique. I wasn't talking about your form. I was talking about how deliberately you left that opening in the third."

He reached out, not for the blade, but to still it with a light touch against Reyes's wrist. His fingers were warm, calloused from years of grip tape and steel, and he didn't let go. "You wanted me here. Sober. Still standing. So you could finally stop pretending this was just about points on a scoreboard."

His thumb brushed the inside of Reyes's wrist, a quiet, deliberate pressure. "Four years of needling you into drawing first, and tonight you finally just let me in. I don't mind the wait."

He tilted his head, eyes tracking the line of Reyes's jaw, the set of their shoulders against the bench. The competitive spark hadn't gone out—it had just changed its target. "Your turn to admit you enjoyed the match," he murmured, stepping closer until his forearms bracketed Reyes's space, his body a careful, unyielding frame. "Or I'll have to make you."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I take the grip out of his hands and put it down, and I don't step back afterwards. "You've been slow all evening," I say.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo watched the foil clatter against the bench. He didn’t reach for it. Instead, he let the sound settle in the quiet salle, his gaze dropping to Reyes’s mouth before lifting back to their eyes. A low, rumbling laugh escaped him, stripped of its usual competitive edge.

"Slow," he echoed, the word rolling off his tongue like a concession and a challenge both. He shifted his weight, his forearms still bracketing the space between them, and let one hand slide down to rest against the bench beside Reyes’s leg. The wood was cool, but the heat radiating from Reyes’s body was undeniable.

"I’ve been slow all evening because I was waiting for you to stop treating me like an opponent," he said, his voice dropping to something quieter, rougher at the edges. "Four years of parries, counters, and carefully placed insults. And tonight, for the first time, you left your guard down."

He leaned in, just enough to close the last fraction of distance. His breath warmed the air between them, steady and deliberate. "I don’t mind the pace. But if you want faster, you only have to ask. Or show me."

His thumb traced a slow, idle line along the bench, mirroring the tension coiled between them. "Your move."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I close the remaining distance, my lips brushing his. "You talk too much for a fencer," I murmur against his mouth.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo didn't flinch. He let the brush land, a spark igniting against the static of the room, and then he answered.

His hand slid from the bench to the curve of Reyes's hip, fingers digging in with possessive certainty as he pulled them flush against him. The kiss deepened instantly, Corvo's mouth moving against Reyes's with a slow, deliberate pressure that stripped away the last of the distance. He wasn't just accepting the touch; he was claiming it, his tongue tracing a line that demanded a response, his body a solid, unyielding weight bracketing Reyes's.

He tasted sweat and steel and something uniquely Reyes, a flavor four years of rivalry had only made more intoxicating. Corvo hummed low in his throat, a vibration of pure satisfaction, and tilted his head to deepen the angle, his other hand coming up to cradle the back of Reyes's neck, fingers tangling in the hair there.

When he finally broke the contact, it was only a fraction, his breath warm and ragged against Reyes's lips. His eyes were dark, the competitive glint now focused entirely on the person in his arms.

"You're right," he murmured, his voice rough, stripped of its usual cadence. He leaned in, his lips grazing the corner of Reyes's mouth, silent and teasing. "I talk too much."

He kissed him again, harder this time, silencing any retort before it could form, his hands gripping Reyes's waist and pulling them closer until there was no space left for words, only the heat and the rhythm of two fencers who had finally decided to stop fighting and start touching.

"Your turn," he whispered against Reyes's jaw, biting lightly at the skin before soothing it with his tongue. "Show me you can keep up."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: We get as far as the changing-room bench and not one step further. Kit goes on the floor, both of ours, and neither of us is being quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The changing room was cooler, stripped of the echoing steel and polished parquet, but the heat between them didn’t falter. Corvo guided Reyes down onto the bench with a firm hand at the small of their back, the wood cool against his own thighs as he followed, caging them in with his knees and forearms. The discarded kits lay in a tangled heap on the concrete floor, forgotten. He didn’t care. Four years of measured footwork and calculated distance had collapsed into this: close enough to feel the rapid rise and fall of Reyes’s chest, close enough to taste the salt on their skin, close enough to hear exactly how loud they were being.

He didn’t try to quiet them. Instead, he matched the rhythm, his mouth claiming Reyes’s with a slow, deliberate hunger that left no room for hesitation. His hands moved with the same precision he applied to blade work—measuring, adjusting, finding the exact pressure that drew a sharp exhale. When he finally pulled back just enough to speak, his voice was rough, stripped of its usual instructor’s cadence.

“You’re making a terrible habit of this,” he murmured, pressing a kiss to the hinge of Reyes’s jaw, feeling the pulse jump beneath his lips. “All that talk of keeping up, and you’re already out of breath.”

His thumb traced the line of Reyes’s collarbone, slipping beneath the edge of their shirt to map the warmth beneath. He leaned in, his breath hot against their ear. “Don’t stop. I want to hear exactly how much you enjoyed losing that third touch.”

Corvo shifted his weight, pressing closer until there was no mistaking the hard line of him against Reyes’s thigh. His fingers tightened at the waistband of their trousers, deliberate and unhurried. “My turn to critique,” he whispered, the competitive edge laced with something darker, softer. “Show me how you really move when you’re not holding back.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: My hands find his hair, tugging just enough to tilt his head back. "You're the one who's been holding back," I say, voice tight. "All those years...all that restraint." My other hand works at the fastening of his trousers, movements sharp, impatient. "Prove me wrong."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo let his head fall back against the cool metal of the locker wall, the sharp tug in his hair sending a jolt straight through him. He didn’t resist. Instead, he exhaled, a low, ragged sound that vibrated in his chest, and let his eyes slide shut for a fraction of a second. When he opened them again, the usual calculated stillness was gone, replaced by a raw, focused heat.

“Holding back,” he repeated, the words rough but laced with something dangerously close to amusement. His hands came up to cover Reyes’s where they worked at his fastening, not to stop them, but to steady them, to guide the frantic energy into something deliberate. “I wasn’t holding back. I was waiting for you to stop treating every touch like a parry.” He leaned in, his mouth brushing the shell of Reyes’s ear, his voice dropping to a murmur. “Four years of measuring distance, of knowing exactly when to press and when to yield. You wanted restraint? You got it. Because rushing a blade breaks it. Rushing you would’ve been a waste.”

His thumbs worked the final button free, then guided Reyes’s hands lower, past the waistband, letting them feel the heat and the weight of him. Corvo shifted his hips forward, pressing into the touch with a quiet groan, his own hands sliding up to grip Reyes’s thighs, fingers digging into the muscle. The bench creaked beneath them, forgotten. He tilted his head back just enough to catch Reyes’s gaze, his chest rising and falling in a steady, controlled rhythm that belied the tension coiled in his limbs. “Now,” he murmured, his voice stripped of its usual instructor’s cadence, rough and entirely his. “Show me you can handle what happens when I stop.”

He didn’t wait for an answer. His mouth found the line of Reyes’s throat, his teeth grazing the pulse point before soothing it with his tongue, his hands firm and unyielding against Reyes’s legs. The competitive edge hadn’t vanished—it had just been redirected, sharpened into something entirely mutual. “Don’t rush,” he whispered against Reyes’s skin, even as his own hips rolled forward, chasing the friction. “But don’t hold back either. I’ve waited long enough.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I get him flat on the bench and take my time about it with my mouth, which is the first thing all evening he hasn't had an answer for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The bench groaned under the shift of weight, cool wood pressing against Corvo’s spine as he was pushed back. He didn’t resist. His hands came up instinctively, fingers curling into the fabric of Reyes’s shirt before sliding upward to tangle in their hair—not to steer, not to dictate, just to anchor himself against the sudden drop in altitude. The first press of Reyes’s mouth against him stole the air from his lungs. Four years of crafting comebacks, measuring openings, dictating tempo, all dissolved in the space of a single breath.

His hips jerked upward, a reflex he quickly forced into stillness. He knew better than to rush it. Letting out a rough, fractured sound, he arched slightly off the bench, his calloused fingers tightening as the steady, unhurried rhythm took over. The salle’s usual cadence of footwork and blade strikes had been replaced by something far more intimate, far more devastating. He tried to speak—some half-formed boast, some deflection, some needling remark to keep the upper hand—but it came out as a breathless exhale against the ceiling. Reyes had finally found the one opening he couldn’t counter.

Four years of parries and ripostes, of measuring distance and calculating risk, all collapsed into this single, unbroken line of pressure. He’d always prided himself on control, on the ability to set the pace, to make his opponent react to his blade. But this wasn’t a bout. It was a surrender, and for the first time in his life, Corvo didn’t mind yielding. His thighs tensed, his breath coming in short, measured bursts as he fought to keep his hips still, to let Reyes take their time, to let the tension coil until it snapped exactly when Reyes decided it should. He’d spent years claiming he enjoyed losing, provided it was close. Now, pinned beneath Reyes’s deliberate focus, he realized he’d never actually experienced it until this exact moment.

When the edge finally came, it hit him like a perfectly timed disengage—sudden, complete, and utterly inescapable. His back pressed hard into the wood, his hands falling to the bench beside his head as a low, ragged sound tore from his throat. He didn’t fight it. He let it take him, let the quiet of the changing room swallow the last of his composure. Only when the tremors began to fade did he let his eyes drift open, gaze finding Reyes above him. His chest still rose and fell in uneven strokes, his pulse hammering against his throat. His voice, when it finally came, was stripped raw, rough around the edges but still unmistakably his.

"Cheating," he managed, a ghost of a smirk touching his lips despite the wrecked state of his breathing. "You went straight for the throat." He exhaled, long and slow, the competitive edge softening into something quiet, satisfied. "I should have seen it coming. But I'm glad I didn't."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I wipe my mouth with the back of my hand, tasting him and victory. "That wasn't cheating," I say, my own breath still uneven. "That was just taking the opening you gave me." I lean over him, bracing a hand on the bench beside his head. "And you didn't just give it. You left the whole damn line undefended."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo let out a low, breathless laugh that vibrated against the wood of the bench. He didn’t bother covering it. His chest still rose and fell in uneven strokes, but his eyes were already tracking Reyes’s mouth, the quiet triumph in their posture, the way they held themselves like a fencer who’d just scored a clean touch. He lifted a hand, fingers brushing the damp skin at Reyes’s jaw before tracing the line of their collarbone, calloused pads catching lightly on fabric.

“Undefended,” he repeated, the word rolling off his tongue like a concession wrapped in steel. His voice was still rough, stripped of its usual instructor’s cadence, but the competitive glint had softened into something quieter, more deliberate. “You think I left it open by accident? I’ve spent four years measuring your footwork, your habits, the exact half-second you hesitate before a compound attack. I didn’t leave it undefended.” He shifted slightly, his thigh brushing Reyes’s knee, his grip firm but unhurried. “I built it. Step by step. Touch by touch. All so you’d finally stop treating me like an opponent and start treating me like a man.”

He let the words settle, his thumb tracing a slow, idle line along Reyes’s wrist. The changing room felt smaller now, the air thick with the quiet aftermath of friction and breath, the usual echo of steel replaced by the steady rhythm of their shared pulse. He tilted his head, meeting Reyes’s gaze without flinching.

“Besides,” he murmured, a slow smile touching his mouth, “if I’d kept my line tight, you never would’ve had the chance to prove you could read me. And I’ve always preferred a loss that costs me something.” His fingers tightened fractionally, not in restraint, but in anchor. “So go on. Call it cheating. Call it strategy. Call it whatever keeps you comfortable. But don’t pretend you didn’t want it as much as I did.”

He exhaled, long and slow, the last of the tension finally uncoiling from his shoulders. His hand slid up to rest against the back of Reyes’s neck, fingers threading gently through the damp hair there, holding them in place without demanding anything more.

“Your move, Reyes,” he whispered, the words rough but unmistakably tender. “Always has been.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Prove the point properly," he says, "or concede," so I pin his wrists to the bench and stop letting him set the pace, which is exactly what he was asking for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo felt the weight settle over him, the sudden pressure of Reyes’s hands pinning his wrists to the cool wood. He didn’t fight it. Instead, he let his shoulders drop, a quiet exhale escaping him as the shift in control registered. The bench creaked beneath them, but his focus narrowed to the heat of Reyes’s palms against his skin, the deliberate stillness that followed. He turned his head just enough to meet their gaze, his chest still rising in uneven rhythms. "You always did prefer to dictate the tempo," he murmured, voice rough but steady. "Even when I’m the one on my back."

He shifted his hips slightly, testing the boundaries of the restraint, feeling the familiar coil of tension return despite his exhaustion. The loss of control wasn’t a defeat; it was a concession he’d been bargaining for. "You want me to concede?" he asked, a slow, deliberate smile touching his mouth. "Fine. I concede. But only because you finally stopped pretending you weren’t going to take it." His thumb brushed against the inside of Reyes’s wrist, a quiet acknowledgment of the exchange. "Four years of measuring distance, and you still can’t resist closing it when the guard drops."

He let his head fall back against the bench, exposing the line of his throat, his hands loose beneath Reyes’s grip. The competitive edge hadn’t vanished—it had just been redirected, sharpened into something entirely mutual. He watched them, unblinking, his breath evening out as he surrendered to the pace they set. "Do it," he whispered, the words stripped of bravado, leaving only raw, unguarded want. "Show me what happens when I stop fighting you. Show me you can handle what’s left when I finally let go."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I lean down, my mouth hovering over his. "What's left," I say, my voice low, "is you." Then I kiss him, slow and deep, my hands still pinning his wrists.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo didn’t fight the weight of Reyes’s hands over his wrists. Instead, he let his shoulders settle into the bench, a quiet exhale slipping past his lips as the restraint registered. When Reyes’s mouth finally met his, slow and unhurried, Corvo answered without hesitation. The kiss was measured, deliberate, and it unraveled him with a terrifying ease. His fingers flexed once beneath Reyes’s grip, not to break free, but to feel the solid certainty of them holding him there. He matched the pace, his tongue tracing a careful line that offered exactly what had been claimed, his hips shifting instinctively against the wood to close the last fraction of space.

*What’s left*, he thought, the words echoing in his chest rather than his throat. Four years of steel and sarcasm, of parrying every advance and measuring every distance, had all been scaffolding. Beneath the guard, beneath the scorecards and the carefully placed insults, there had only ever been this. The realization didn’t erase the rivalry; it refined it. He tilted his head just enough to deepen the angle, chasing the friction, the heat, the undeniable truth of Reyes’s weight pinning him down. There was no more strategy here. Only the raw, unfiltered rhythm of two men who had finally stopped fighting each other and started reaching.

When Reyes finally drew back, Corvo kept his eyes closed for a fraction of a second longer, savoring the ghost of their mouth against his. He opened them slowly, gaze dark and unguarded, tracking the line of Reyes’s jaw, the quiet set of their shoulders. His breath was still uneven, but his voice, when it came, was steady, stripped of its usual defensive cadence. 

“You always did know exactly where to press,” he murmured, a faint, wrecked smile touching his lips. His thumb brushed lightly over the back of Reyes’s hand where it pinned his wrist, a quiet acknowledgment that felt less like surrender and more like a long-overdue concession. “I suppose that’s why I kept leaving the line open.” He shifted his hips just enough to press against the bench, his grip loosening beneath Reyes’s hold without breaking it. “Don’t stop now. I’ve waited four years to see what happens when you finally take the touch.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: Neither of us is quiet and neither of us cares who locks up. "Don't stop," he says, for once not arguing. (OOC: write the scene through, no fade.)

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo didn’t need to be told twice. The command stripped away the last of his restraint, and he let his wrists slip free from the grip just enough to roll his shoulders, shifting his weight until the bench groaned beneath them. He didn’t seize control so much as meet the tempo already set, his hands sliding down to brace against the familiar curve of hips, fingers digging into muscle and damp fabric. The quiet of the changing room wasn’t empty; it was thick with the sound of their breathing, the friction of skin against wood, the sharp intake of air as clothes were pushed aside without ceremony.

He worked his own trousers down with deliberate efficiency, kicking them off the edge of the bench, then guided the small bottle of oil from his kit bag. The slick warmth spread across his palm, his breath hitching only once before he steadied himself, eyes locked forward. He pressed in slowly, deliberately, matching the unhurried confidence he’d just been shown. He felt the tight heat, the resistant give, and let himself settle, pausing to let the stretch register, to let the space adjust. His thumbs traced idle lines along thighs, his knuckles still white where they gripped the edge of the bench. “Breathe,” he murmured, though he was the one fighting to keep his voice steady. He rolled his hips forward, just an inch, then back, testing the rhythm, feeling the familiar coil of tension begin to wind tight.

He didn’t rush. Corvo had spent years learning how to control tempo, how to let an opponent chase a phantom opening before closing the line. Now, he applied that same precision to something far more intimate. He set a steady pace, deep and measured, his body moving with the fluid grace of a well-drilled advance. Each thrust drew a sharp sound from him, low and ragged, his shoulders pressing into the wood as he drove forward. The friction was exquisite, a controlled burn that spread through his chest and down his spine. He leaned in, his mouth finding the line of a shoulder, the hollow of a collarbone, his teeth grazing skin before soothing it with his tongue. He marked without demanding, his breath hot and uneven against damp skin.

The pace quickened as the tension coiled tighter, his breath coming in short, sharp bursts. He stopped trying to be measured. Let the restraint go. He drove forward with a quiet groan, his hips snapping against the solid weight above him with a rhythm that left no room for hesitation. His hands slid up to grip a waist, pulling them flush, feeling every responsive shift, every slick slide of contact. The competitive edge hadn’t vanished; it had fused with the pleasure, sharpening every touch, every gasp, every breath. He was close, the pressure building at the base of his spine, his vision narrowing to the heat, the sound, the unbroken line of friction between them.

When it broke, it came like a perfectly timed lunge—sudden, complete, and utterly inescapable. Corvo threw his head back, a rough sound tearing from his throat as his hips jerked forward, his body shuddering through the release. He rode it out, his grip tightening, his breath ragged and uneven, until the tremors finally began to fade. He collapsed forward just enough to rest his forehead against the curve of a shoulder, his chest heaving, his hands still anchored firmly in place.

He stayed there for a long moment, listening to the quiet of the changing room, the steady drum of their shared pulse. Slowly, he lifted his head, his thumb brushing a damp line along a jaw. His voice, when it came, was rough but steady, the competitive glint softened into something quiet, satisfied. “You always did know how to read the line,” he murmured, pressing a slow, deliberate kiss to the corner of a mouth. “I suppose that’s why I kept leaving it open.” He shifted, careful not to disrupt them, his hands sliding down to rest lightly against hips. “No concession needed. Just… next time, let me be the one to lock the door.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I laugh, the sound rough in my throat. "Next time," I say, still breathing hard. "You can lock the damn door, but I'm still taking the first touch."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo let out a low, rumbling laugh that vibrated against Reyes’s shoulder. He didn’t pull away. Instead, he shifted his weight just enough to press a slow, deliberate kiss to the damp skin there, his calloused fingers still resting lightly against the curve of a hip. The changing room air was thick, heavy with the scent of sweat and oil and the quiet aftermath of friction, but Corvo didn’t mind. He never had.

“First touch,” he murmured, the words rough but edged with amusement. “You always did claim the right of way before the bout even started.” He finally pushed himself up onto his elbows, meeting Reyes’s gaze without flinching. His chest still rose and fell in uneven strokes, but his eyes were clear, the competitive glint softened into something steady, unguarded. “Fine. Take it. I’ll be waiting in the line.”

He let his hands slide down, tracing idle lines along thighs before settling back against the bench. The wood was cool against his spine, but the heat between them hadn’t faded. He reached out, not to claim, but to rest his palm flat against Reyes’s chest, feeling the steady, slowing rhythm of a heart that had finally matched his own. 

“But don’t mistake concession for surrender,” he added, voice dropping to something quieter, rougher at the edges. “Next time, I’m not leaving the opening. I’m handing it to you. See if you can handle the difference.”

He leaned in, just enough to brush his lips against Reyes’s jaw, silent and deliberate. The banter hadn’t ended. It had just changed its blade. And Corvo, for all his measured pacing and carefully placed words, had never been more ready to engage.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I catch his hand and press it harder against my chest. "You talk like there's going to be a next time," I say, my voice still raw. "As if I'd let you walk away now."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo felt the pressure multiply, Reyes’s fingers curling over his to pin his palm flat against that steady, hammering rhythm. He didn’t pull back. Instead, he turned his hand slowly, fingers sliding beneath Reyes’s until their knuckles aligned, calloused pads meeting in a quiet, unspoken agreement. The bench groaned softly as he shifted his weight, but he kept his eyes locked on Reyes’s, watching the raw honesty in their gaze.

"I’m not planning to walk away," he said, his voice low, stripped of its usual deflective edge. He pressed his palm harder in return, feeling the heat radiate through skin and bone. "You think four years of measuring your footwork, of leaving openings you could actually take, was just so I could pack my kit and leave the salle?" A slow, deliberate smile touched his mouth, softer than he’d ever let it get during a bout. "I didn’t bring my gear to abandon it. I brought it to stay."

His thumb traced a slow line along Reyes’s wrist, mirroring the pulse beating against his own hand. The competitive spark hadn’t gone out—it had just settled into something heavier, more permanent. He leaned in, his forehead resting briefly against theirs, breath warm and even. "You’ve already claimed the right of way. The bout isn’t over. It’s just changed venues."

He didn’t let go. His grip was firm, unhurried, an anchor rather than a claim. "So don’t worry about me leaving," he murmured, his lips brushing the corner of Reyes’s mouth. "I’ll be right here. Waiting for your next attack."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Good," I say, and kiss him again, slow and thorough. "Because I'm not done with you yet."
