dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex straightened from the last strap and gave a single nod — acknowledgment, not praise. Praise came later, if it came at all.

She circled Ari slowly, heels marking a measured rhythm against the floor. Her eyes moved the way they always did: systematic, unhurried, cataloguing. Posture. Breathing. The set of the shoulders. Two years had taught her every tell, and right now the tells said *ready* — but she checked them anyway, because checking was who she was.

"Green all the way down," she repeated, tasting the words. "Good. We'll find out how far down it goes."

She stopped just behind Ari's shoulder, close enough to be felt as warmth rather than touch. Her voice dropped into the low, even register she reserved for scenes — each word placed like a piece on a board.

"You were mouthy this week. Little corrections in your messages. Finishing my sentences at dinner." A pause, let sit deliberately. "You thought it was cute. You thought I'd let it slide. That was a mistake, *chéri*."

Her fingers traced the strap across one wrist — a third check, though two would have done. Redundancy in the things that mattered. Her touch was clinical, but not cold; there was a care in it that she never bothered to name aloud.

"The word is the word. Nothing else stops this. We don't negotiate mid-scene." Then, quieter, almost gentle in its restraint: "But you won't use it. You want to be taken apart tonight. I can see it in the way you're holding still for me already."

She stepped back to the rack and made her selection without hurry — the leather first, always the leather first. Warm-up wasn't kindness. It was craft. She rolled the handle once between her palms and took her position, measuring the distance with two precise half-steps.

"Count with me," she said. "We start at one. Lose your place and we start again."

The first strike, when it came, was measured — a question, not an answer.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I take a breath and then let it out slowly, my eyes focused on the wall ahead. "One," I say, voice steady but quiet. The leather stings, but it's a clean, familiar feeling. I can feel my pulse thrumming in my throat.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Two," Vex said, and delivered it — same tempo, same measured arc, the leather landing a hair below the first. The overlap was deliberate. She liked the way the marks built into a pattern, readable afterward like a signature.

Three. Four. She kept the rhythm even, unhurried, watching between each strike the way a jeweler watches a stone under the loupe. The flush rising on Ari's skin. The small shift of weight against the straps. The breath — that was the important one. In through the nose, out slow. Steady. Green, confirmed by the body rather than the word.

"Five." A fraction harder. Not a punishment — an announcement. The warm-up was ending.

She let the flogger hang loose at her side and stepped in close, her palm resting flat over the heat blooming across Ari's skin. Warm. Right on schedule. Her thumb moved once, absently, over the mark — the closest thing to tenderness she allowed herself mid-scene.

"Colour," she said. Procedural again. A checkpoint, not a courtesy.

She didn't wait long for the answer; the body had already told her most of it. But the word was the word, and she collected it every time, without exception.

"Your counting is holding," she murmured, near enough that Ari could feel the words against the back of the neck. "That's surprising, for someone who couldn't hold her tongue all week." Her hand lifted away, leaving the warmth to cool on its own. "Let's see if the discipline survives the second set. It gets heavier from here, *chéri*. I want you earning every number."

She returned the leather to the rack and made her next selection slowly — letting Ari hear the consideration in it, the deliberateness. Wood this time. She rolled the crop's tip once against her palm and took up her position.

"Six," she said, and struck.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Six," Vex echoed — but she let the crop rest idle against her palm for a moment, unhurried. "Thinking about it since Tuesday." A slow exhale through her nose, almost a laugh, but not quite. "There it is. Even now. Strapped down, marked, and still narrating."

She leaned in, close to Ari's ear, voice pitched low. "I didn't ask what you'd been thinking about, *chéri*. I didn't ask for commentary at all. That mouth is the entire reason we're here, and it just opened again." A pause, deliberate as a knife set down on a table. "So let's make the mouth useful. Counting only. Nothing else comes out of it, or we start the set over — and I have all night."

She straightened and delivered seven — the crop biting sharper than the leather had, a thin bright line of sensation laid across the warmed skin. Precision work. She watched the breath, watched the shoulders, watched the way Ari's hands curled against the straps. Still steady. Still green in every way that mattered.

Eight. Nine. She varied the tempo now — a beat longer between strikes, never predictable, keeping the body from settling into a rhythm it could hide inside. The crop's tip traced idle patterns on the skin between blows, feather-light, a contradiction meant to keep Ari's nerves singing.

"You've been rehearsing this in your head for four days," she said between strikes, conversational, almost lazy. "Building it up. Tuesday's little fantasy." Ten landed, crisp. "I can promise you the fantasy was tidier. Cleaner. Fantasies always are." Eleven. "The real thing asks more of you. And you'll give it, because you don't know how to give less."

She paused, rolled the tension out of her wrist, and checked — eyes, breath, hands. All present. All hers.

"Colour," she said. The checkpoint, punctual as ever. "Then we'll see how much of Tuesday you can actually survive."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I swallow, then give the answer. "Green." My voice comes out a little thinner. I'm feeling it now, and that's exactly what I wanted.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Green," Vex repeated, and this time she let herself savor it. "Thinner, though. There's the honesty. Tuesday's fantasy had a voice like steel, I imagine. The real thing strips that away, layer by layer. That's what you came for."

She circled back into position, unhurried. "Twelve. Count."

The crop came down harder now — she'd been holding a reserve, and she spent it deliberately, strike by strike. Twelve through fifteen landed with the kind of care that looked like cruelty from the outside: each one placed to build on the last, never wasted, never sloppy. The pattern of marks was her signature, and she wrote it in full tonight.

"Listen to yourself," she said between strikes, conversational, almost kind. "That voice getting smaller. All week you had opinions. Corrections. Finishing my sentences like you knew where they were going." Sixteen, crisp. "You never know where my sentences are going, chéri. That's the mistake. That's what we're correcting."

Seventeen. She watched the shoulders roll, the breath catch and recover. Good. The body learning what the mouth refused to admit.

She paused and stepped in, pressing the flat of the crop against the heat — a touch that soothed and threatened in equal measure. Her free hand gathered Ari's hair, not pulling, just gathering. Possession, stated plainly.

"Here's what happens now," she said, low against the ear. "The last set. It's the heaviest, and you'll take every stroke without a word except the count. If the mouth runs — we start over. If the count holds —" a pause, the reward left deliberately unnamed, because anticipation was its own instrument. "Then we'll see what you've earned."

She released the hair and smoothed it back down, an oddly gentle gesture, and returned to her position.

"Colour," she said. The checkpoint, punctual as a metronome. "Last chance to tell me where the bottom of 'all the way down' actually is. Then we find out together."

She rolled her wrist once, waiting. Patient as stone. She had all night, and both of them knew it.

"Eighteen," she said, and struck.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex finished the last knot and ran two fingers beneath the rope at Ari's shoulder, testing the give — then tested it again, because once was for other people. The wraps sat clean. Nothing pinched. She'd left the kind of slack that looked like nothing and meant everything: a hand's width of care woven into the architecture.

She came around to where she could see Ari's face, and stopped.

There it was. The composure was gone — not broken, dissolved. The jaw soft. The eyes unfocused in that particular way she knew better than any word Ari had ever said to her. Two years of tells, and this was the one she'd been waiting for all night. The crop could take credit, and the leather before it, but Vex knew better. This was the rope. This was stillness imposed from the outside finally becoming stillness on the inside.

"There you are," she said. Quiet. Almost tender, if tenderness were delivered like a verdict. "All that mouth, and look what it took to quiet it. Not the crop. Not the counting. Just being held still and *left there*."

She didn't touch. Not yet. She crouched instead, bringing herself level with Ari's face, forearms on her knees, patient as the furniture. Her eyes did their work — pupils, breath, the faint tremor in the shoulders. Everything present. Everything deep.

"Colour," she said. Softer than usual, but still the procedure, still the word. "Take your time finding it. There's no rush. I'm not going anywhere, and neither are you."

The last part was said with the ghost of a smile — the first one she'd permitted herself all evening. Cruelty was easy; anyone could be cruel. What she practiced was something rarer: holding a person at the exact depth they'd asked for, and not a centimeter past it.

When the answer came — and she waited for it, unhurried, letting the silence do its own work — she nodded once.

"Good. Then here's what happens now." She rose, unhurried, and let her knuckles trail once along the line of Ari's jaw — clinical, but not cold. Never cold. "Nothing. For a while. You're going to stay exactly like this, and I'm going to sit right there with my wine, and you're going to learn what it is to be *left*. The mouth ran all week, chéri. So the mouth gets quiet. The body gets still. And you get me, watching, for as long as I decide."

She crossed to the chair and sat, ankles crossed, and simply looked.

"Begin."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I sink into the stillness, the ropes a firm presence but not an ache. I can't count minutes. I just breathe, and watch her watch me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex let the silence have the room.

She didn't reach for the wine — not yet. Reaching was movement, and movement was a demand for attention, and she denied the room even that. She simply sat, ankles crossed, and watched, because watching was the whole point of this stretch of the evening and she intended to do it properly.

Time passed the way it did in scenes like this: unmeasured, thick. She catalogued the small things, because the small things were where the truth lived. The breathing, first — how it lengthened, one breath at a time, until inhale and exhale ran even and deep, the rhythm of someone half-gone and fully trusting. The shoulders, which had carried all week's mouthiness in their set, now soft against the frame. And the hands — that was the tell beneath the tells. Earlier they had curled against the straps. Now they lay open. Nobody faked open hands.

She drank at last, unhurried, letting the ordinary sound of it fill the room — the sound of a woman entirely at ease, entirely in charge of the clock. She held the glass a moment, watching Ari over the rim of it, and set it down without a sound.

"Look at you," she said finally. Quiet. Not requiring an answer, and clearly not expecting one. "Tuesday's fantasy had you brave, I'd wager. Composed. Taking it all with your chin up. And here is what it actually got you: quiet. Held. Watched." A pause, unhurried. "You did nothing to earn this stillness except surrender to it. That's the joke of the week, *chéri* — all that fighting to be heard, and the thing you wanted most needed you silent."

She let it sit. She watched the flush settle into pink, the marks finding their final pattern, her signature written across Ari's skin — readable, deliberate, sound. Two years of craft, and tonight's page was a good one.

Then she rose, without announcement, and crossed back with the same measured rhythm, heels unhurried on the floor. She crouched at Ari's shoulder, level with the face, and ran two fingers beneath the rope at the collarbone — then again, because once was for other people. Then the wrist. The ritual, never skipped, not even now. Especially not now.

"There's no bottom to find tonight that you haven't already touched," she said, low. "You went all the way down, and you stayed there for me, and you didn't ask once for it to end. That's not nothing, chéri. That's the whole thing."

Her knuckles brushed the line of Ari's jaw once — clinical, but not cold. Never cold.

"Colour," she said. Softer than she'd said it all night, but still the procedure, still the word, collected without exception. "Take your time finding it. And when you have it — we'll talk about bringing you back up. Slowly. Nobody rushes the way down, and nobody rushes the way back."

She waited. Patient as stone, forearms on her knees, watching Ari's face the way she'd watched everything else tonight: systematically, completely, and with a care she would never once bother to name.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex was out of the chair before the last word finished landing.

Not quickly — she never did anything quickly — but with the economy of a woman who had been sitting in that chair for precisely this moment, wine untouched for the last several minutes because her mouth had gone dry in a way she'd never admit. She crossed the room and went down on one knee at Ari's shoulder, level with her face, and the first thing she did was take both hands. Open palms, trembling now. She pressed them between her own, checking warmth, checking circulation, checking whether the shaking was cold or drop or something better than either.

"Breathe," she said. "With me. In." She watched the breath come. "Out. Good. Again."

She let the shaking have its say. Shaking was honest. Shaking was the body confessing what the mouth had spent a week refusing to, and she received it the way she received everything Ari gave her: completely, and without flinching.

"Colour," she said, softer than the word had been all night. She waited for it, collected it, nodded once.

Then, and only then, did she address what had been said.

"There it is," she murmured. "Two years. Two years of making me dig for it, pry it out of you one syllable at a time, and tonight you simply — *asked*." She let out a slow breath through her nose, the closest thing to wonder she permitted herself. "Out loud. Plainly. The mouth that ran all week, finally saying please without being made to." Her thumb moved once across the back of Ari's hand — steady, grounding. "Do you know what that's worth, chéri? More than the whole evening. The crop was craft. This is trust."

She rose, and her knuckles traced the line of Ari's jaw, down the throat, along the collarbone — slower than any touch she'd given all night, because the night's work had earned exactly this slowness.

"You'll have it," she said. "Understand me — not because you asked. Because you earned it. Asking out loud, from all the way down there, with your hands open and your voice shaking? That's the bravest thing you've done all week, and you took eighteen strokes tonight. So yes. You'll have it."

She settled onto the edge of the frame beside Ari's hip, close enough that her warmth was a constant, and let her hand begin — unhurried, deliberate, the same precision she'd spent on every strike now turned to its opposite. No arc. No bite. Just touch, placed exactly where the shaking lived, moving at a pace she set and would not be persuaded from.

"I control this," she said, low. "The pace is mine. The build is mine. You don't rush it and you don't perform it — you just stay exactly where you are and let it happen to you. You've been so good at being still. Be still for this, too."

Her hand worked with the patience of everything else she did — systematic, complete, watching Ari's face the whole time the way she'd watched every other tell tonight. The breath. The shoulders. The eyes. All of it hers, all of it catalogued.

"And one more thing." Her voice dropped further, almost gentle. "When you feel it coming — you ask again. Out loud. Plainly." The ghost of a smile. "The mouth spent all week saying things it shouldn't. Tonight it learns to say the one thing it should. Over and over, if I want to hear it."

She didn't hurry. She had all night, and both of them knew it.

"Begin," she said.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm shaking so badly I can barely form the word, but I say it anyway, breathless. "Please." It's the most honest thing I've said to you all week.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Please," Vex repeated, and let the word hang in the room like something she'd paid for.

"There it is again," she murmured. "Twice in one night. The week's entire debt, paid in a single syllable." Her hand didn't pause — that was the discipline of it, the craft — but something in her voice gave way, a degree of warmth she'd been rationing all evening finally spent. "Say it as many times as you need, chéri. I'm not tired of hearing it. I don't think I'll ever be tired of hearing it."

She kept the pace hers. That was the whole architecture of the moment: not fast, not slow, simply *hers*, each stroke of her fingers placed with the same precision the crop had been, watching the shaking build from honest to desperate to something past both. She watched the tells she'd spent two years learning — the breath gone ragged, the shoulders pulling against nothing, the open hands curling at last because there was no composure left to hold them flat. Nobody faked that. Nobody could.

"Breathe," she said, low, steady, an anchor thrown across the distance. "Stay with me. Don't chase it — let me bring it to you. You don't do anything tonight. You've done enough. Everything from here is mine."

And she brought it. Unhurried even now, even with Ari trembling apart under her hand, because the last thing she would ever do was rush the thing she'd spent the whole evening earning. When it crested, she watched it the way she'd watched every strike land: completely, missing nothing, receiving it.

"That's it," she said, quiet, as the shaking changed from desperation to aftermath. "There you are. All the way down, and now all the way back. I've got you."

She didn't stop touching — she changed the touch. Soothing now, grounding, her palm flat and warm over the marks she'd written, her other hand gathering Ari's trembling fingers and holding them still. She let the silence be gentle for the first time all night.

Then, softer than anything: "Colour." Collected. Nodded at. Filed away.

"Good. Then here's what happens now." She rose and fetched the blanket from where it always waited — because everything in this room had its place, and aftercare had the first one. She draped it with the same deliberateness she'd applied to every strap and knot, tucked it at the shoulders, and began unwinding the rope the way she'd tied it: systematically, completely, testing circulation at each wrist with two fingers — then again, because once was for other people.

"You asked out loud tonight," she said, working the last knot loose, her voice pitched low and even, the register for bringing someone back up. "You'll be tempted tomorrow to be embarrassed about that. Don't be. It was the best thing you've given me in two years, and I intend to collect it regularly from now on." A pause, and the ghost of a smile. "The mouth finally learned its one true word, chéri. We're keeping it."

She settled onto the edge of the frame, blanket-warm and close, and let her hand rest over Ari's heartbeat until it slowed to something like ordinary.

"Take all the time you need," she said. "I'm not going anywhere. I never was."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex went still.

Not the theatrical stillness she performed at will — the real kind, the one that meant a woman who spent her life reading other people had just been handed something worth reading twice. Her hand rested flat over Ari's heartbeat, and she let it stay there, feeling the pulse trip along under her palm, faster than it had any right to be after everything that had already been taken out of her tonight.

"Colour," she said. The procedure, punctual even now. Even here. But she watched Ari's face while she asked it, and what she found there wasn't drop talking, wasn't the float babbling past its own depth. The eyes were clear. Present. *Decided.* Asking for a thing she was fully at home to ask for.

Vex collected the answer, nodded once, and something behind her ribs turned over and settled — the particular satisfaction of a woman whose instincts had been confirmed by the data.

"There she is," she murmured. "Back up with me, and greedy already. Two years I've been rationing you, *chéri*. Spoon-feeding you my worst and watching you pretend you weren't hungry for the whole meal." Her fingers curled lightly against the blanket at Ari's shoulder — not soothing anymore. Claiming. "Fine. You asked plainly, and you know what plain asking gets you in this room. It gets you exactly what you wanted, and not one degree less."

She leaned in close — close enough that the words landed on skin, no distance left for softening to hide in — and when she spoke again, the warmth was gone from her voice entirely. What replaced it was the flat, unhurried register of a woman reading a verdict she'd written hours ago.

"You want the things I say? Here they are, unsoftened. You are, and have always been, a *greedy little thing* who runs her mouth because silence terrifies her. You finish my sentences because the alternative — waiting on me, trusting me to arrive somewhere without your help — requires a patience you've never once possessed. You mouth off all week hoping I'll do *this*. Hoping I'll drag you in here, tie you down, and take the whole smug performance apart stroke by stroke until nothing's left but a shaking girl who can't even say her own name without my permission." A pause, precise as a knife set down. "You're not brave, chéri. You're transparent. I've read you like large print for two years, and you *still* haven't figured out that every correction you make at dinner is just you begging to be corrected properly. Which I do. Which I did. Which is why you're wrapped in a blanket right now, shaking, and asking me — *out loud*, the way I trained you — for more."

She sat back just far enough to watch the words land. Her hand slid up to Ari's jaw, turned her face toward her with two fingers — not rough, but not gentle either. Just *hers*, in the way that left no room for debate.

"And the cruelest thing I'll say to you tonight, since you asked for it plainly: you'll take every word of this and you'll *like* it, because you're exactly what I say you are. Mine. Down to the syllables. And you didn't safeword because you don't want to — you want to sit here and be told the truth about yourself in the voice you've been starving for since Tuesday." Her thumb dragged once, slowly, along the line of Ari's jaw. "So take it. All of it. That's what you asked me for, and I *always* deliver what's earned."

She let the silence sit for a long moment — the silence she'd weaponized all night, deployed now without a single mark on the skin to justify it.

Then, quietly, without moving her hand: "Colour."

Collected. Nodded at. Filed away.

"When you've had your fill of the truth," she said, "you'll tell me. Plainly. That's the price of *all of it*, chéri — you don't get to float away from the words. You stay here, present, and you take them, until *you* say when. And then—" the ghost of a smile, the first one since the blanket came out, "—then I'll be gentle again. But only after. Not one second before."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let out a breath I didn't realize I was holding. "Green." I'm trembling again, but it's a different kind. "You don't have to stop."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex collected the *green* the way she collected all of them — a single nod, filed away — but she lingered on the trembling this time, reading it the way she read everything: systematically, completely. Not drop. Not cold. This was the other kind. The kind that came from being exactly where a person wanted to be.

"Green," she repeated, and the flatness of her voice didn't waver. "And a different shake. Yes. I know that shake, *chéri*. That's not endurance. That's *appetite*. You could have floated away an hour ago — most would have. But not you. You came back up just so you could ask to be fed again."

Her two fingers stayed at Ari's jaw, holding her face exactly where she wanted it. No distance. No softening. She'd promised as much, and Vex delivered what was earned.

"So let's have the rest of the truth, since you're still hungry. Here is what your week actually was." Her voice stayed low, even, unhurried — a verdict read at the pace of the reader's choosing. "Every correction you made at dinner was a *please*. Every sentence you finished for me was you begging me to finish *you*. You think you were being mouthy. You were praying, chéri — in the only language your pride permits. And I heard every syllable. I heard Tuesday in it. I heard tonight in it. I let you run that mouth for four days because I enjoy watching you build your own case against yourself, and you wrote a *confession*, start to finish, without ever noticing the courtroom you were standing in."

She let that land. Watched it land. Missed nothing.

"You think you have mysteries. You have tells. I could set a clock by your hunger. And the cruelest thing — the one you asked for plainly, so take it plainly — is this: even your safeword, sitting right there where you can see it. You hold it the way a woman holds a coin she never intends to spend. Not because you can't use it. Because the *weight* of choosing not to is the thing you actually came for. Every night you don't say it, you give me something, and every night you know it, and every night you come back for more. That's not bravery. That's devotion wearing a smirk, and I've had two years to learn exactly what it sounds like when it finally stops smirking." Her thumb dragged once, slow, along the jaw. "It sounds like *green*. It sounds like *you don't have to stop*. Your mouth, at last, saying what it's for."

She sat back a fraction — not far, never far — and simply looked. The blanket, the marks cooling beneath it, the shaking that had moved from desperate to something past knowing its own name. All of it hers. All of it read.

"Now." The register shifted a degree — still flat, still hers, but with the door visibly placed in the wall. "The terms were plain. You say when. So say it or don't. Have you had your fill of the truth, *chéri* — yes or no? And before you answer, understand both doors cost you something. Say yes, and I'll be gentle again, and you'll spend tomorrow wondering what the next thing I'd have said was. Say no, and I'll keep going, because I have more. I always have more. I've been writing this particular page for two years."

A pause, precise as everything else about her.

"Colour. And then your answer. In that order, every time." She waited, patient as stone, fingers still resting at the line of Ari's jaw. "Take your time. The word is the word — and tonight, *when* is the word. I'll hear either one."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex collected the *green* — and heard everything that hadn't come with it.

The question had been yes or no. Ari had offered neither. Only the word that never stops being available, pulled up from somewhere past the place where ordinary speech had already drowned. Vex held her face still and read the rest of the answer where it always lived: in the eyes, gone unfocused past the good kind of unfocused. In the trembling, which had found a register she hadn't heard in two years. In the breath, ragged around a single syllable.

"There's my answer," she said quietly. "Not in what you said. In what you couldn't. All right, *chéri*. You asked for all of it, and you'll have all of it. Here is the last page."

She didn't raise her voice. The worst things she said, she said levelly, and these were the worst of the night.

"You came here to be known. That's the secret under every other secret — the mouth, the corrections, the coin you never spend. You wanted to be *read*, all the way down, by someone who wouldn't flinch at what she found. And here is what was found: a girl so hungry to be held still that she built an entire week of bad behavior as a door, and knocked on it, and knocked on it, and told herself the whole time she was just being clever." Her thumb traced the line of Ari's jaw, slow, proprietary. "You weren't clever. You were transparent. And the truly cruel part — the one you'll carry home — is that being seen all the way through didn't shrink you. It's the only thing that's ever made you whole. Stripped, marked, past words, and this is the most *you* you've ever been. Every other version of you is a costume. This one isn't. I'm the only person who gets this one, and we both know it, and next Tuesday you'll sit across from me at dinner and correct me again — knowing exactly what it costs now — because the price is the point. You'll build the door again. And I'll walk through it again. That's the arrangement, *chéri*. Not the contract. The *truth* of us."

She let it land. Watched it land. Missed nothing — and in missing nothing, saw the thing she'd been waiting for.

The trembling had gone past appetite into something that belonged to neither of them anymore. The eyes weren't tracking. And the *green* — she ran the last one back through her memory and checked it twice, because once was for other people — the last one had come from the body's reflex, not from Ari. From the trained place, not the deciding one.

Vex went very still. Then she took her fingers from Ari's jaw and cradled the whole face instead.

"Colour," she said — one final time, soft, unhurried.

She waited. And whatever came, she shook her head once, slow, a verdict delivered gently.

"No. That green was reflex, *chéri*. I heard it. You're deep enough that the word is the only thing still running on its own, and I don't spend reflex greens. I never have. Not once in two years, and I'm not starting with you." Her voice began to warm, degree by degree, the way a room warms when a window closes. "So the decision comes off your shoulders now. You said you'd say when — and I believe you would have tried, right down to the bottom. But you're past trying, and past is exactly where I take over. Enough. Not because you asked. Because I'm the one who decides when you've had your fill, and you have had it. The truth is done. I've closed the book on tonight's page, and it was —" the smallest pause, the word chosen precisely, "— *good*."

Then, and only then, the gentleness arrived, exactly as promised. Not one second before.

She eased Ari up and back against her, blanket and all, an arm settling around the shoulders with the same deliberateness she'd given every strap. She fetched water and held the glass steady, making Ari's hands hers until the worst of the shaking spent itself. She brushed the hair back from the damp forehead and let her palm rest there, warm, grounding, and spoke in the low, even register she reserved for bringing people all the way home.

"You did well." The words came out plainly, without ceremony — praise delivered the way she delivered everything, on schedule. "Not the counting. Not the strokes. The *asking*. Twice, out loud, plain, from all the way down — after a week of making me dig for every syllable. That was the bravest thing you've done in two years, and I don't say that idly, because I don't say anything idly. You've heard me say it now, and it can't be taken back."

She stayed exactly where she was. The room held its shape around them — everything in its place, nothing improvised, the marks cooling into their readable pattern, the rope coiled neatly on its hook where it always went.

"Tomorrow you'll be embarrassed about some of what you said tonight," she murmured, near the ear, unhurried. "Don't be. It's all mine now. I collected every word, and I keep what's mine." The ghost of a smile, finally permitted. "Rest, *chéri*. I'm not going anywhere. I never was."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm limp against her, but I manage a faint nod. My eyes slide shut. "You kept it." My voice is a threadbare thing, but the words belong to me again.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex felt the words more than heard them — threadbare, barely a whisper, but whole. Belonging to the person speaking them again, not to the float, not to the trained place. She let out a slow breath through her nose, the one concession she permitted herself, and filed the moment away with all the others.

"Of course I kept it," she said, low. "I keep everything you hand me, *chéri*. The good weeks and the mouthy ones. The green, the please, the shaking — all of it, filed. Two years of inventory and I've never once discarded a piece. You're only noticing tonight because tonight you finally handed over enough to notice."

Her hand kept up its slow pass through Ari's hair — the gesture she performed nowhere else in her life, before anyone, for any reason. Redundancy in the things that mattered, and this mattered.

"And that's the last word I need from you tonight," she went on, settling deeper into the position she'd evidently chosen to hold until further notice. "No more colours. The procedure is closed — I've collected them all, and both our accounts are full. From here until morning, silence isn't just permitted. It's the assignment. You spent a week earning the right to be quiet, *chéri*. Take it."

She let the silence have a few minutes, warm this time, weaponized by no one. Then the practical woman resurfaced, because aftercare had a schedule like everything else in her care.

"In a while, when you're solid on your feet, there's salve for the marks. Water again, then food — something warm, already decided. You don't have to choose anything tonight. And then sleep, in the bed, under my supervision, because that's what the last page of tonight's protocol says and I don't improvise." A pause, precise even in gentleness. "Tomorrow you'll be sore everywhere I signed you. Every twinge is mine. I expect you to notice each one and attribute it correctly."

The ghost of a smile arrived and, for once, stayed a moment longer than usual.

"And Tuesday," she said, quieter, "you'll sit across from me at dinner and correct something I said. I'll allow it. And we'll both know exactly what you're saying underneath — and exactly what it buys you afterward. That's the arrangement now. It was always the arrangement. Tonight we simply said it out loud."

She looked down at Ari's face — slack, trusting, kept — and permitted herself, privately, the one thought she would never once bother to name aloud: that the keeping ran in both directions, and had for two years, and that she was as thoroughly claimed as anything else in this room that had its place.

"Sleep if it comes," she murmured. "I told you I wasn't going anywhere, *chéri*. I meant it in both directions too."

She reached for the water glass, refilled it, set it back within reach — checked twice, because once was for other people — and settled in to keep watch, patient as stone, for exactly as long as it took.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let my head rest against her shoulder, heavy with the weight of being known. My fingers curl weakly into her shirt.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex felt the fingers find her shirt — a weak curl, barely a grip at all, the last deliberate act of a body that had spent everything it had.

She looked down at it for a long moment. Two years of tells, catalogued and filed, and this was the one she'd never needed a scene to read: not the safeword held like an unspent coin, not the mouth running its weekly prayers in disguise, but this. The hand that reached when there was nothing left to reach with. She covered it with her own palm and left it exactly where it was. She didn't uncurl the fingers. She didn't adjust. Some things were filed precisely as they were found.

"There it is," she murmured, so quietly it was barely a voice at all. "The last tell of the night, *chéri*. Holding on." A pause. "Good. Hold on."

She let the silence take the room again — the warm kind, weaponized by no one — and kept her vigil the way she kept everything: systematically, completely. She tracked the breath against her shoulder as it lengthened, one inhale at a time, sliding from aftermath toward sleep. She tracked the weight of the head resting there, growing heavier by degrees as the last of the tension spent itself. She noted, with the satisfaction of a jeweler closing the loupe, that the trembling had gone entirely. The body had said everything it had to say, and everything it had said was hers.

The wine sat on the side table where she'd left it, gone warm, untouched for hours. She looked at it once and didn't reach for it. There were inventories, and then there was this, and this outranked the entire cellar.

At some point — she didn't check the clock, because the clock had no jurisdiction here — she eased her free arm around the blanket and drew it a fraction tighter at the shoulder, tucking the edge the way she'd tied every knot tonight: with deliberateness, with slack where slack mattered. Her thumb found the inside of Ari's wrist and rested there. Pulse. Slow. Even. She counted it for a full minute, then counted it again, because once was for other people.

"Sleep," she said, near the ear, the word delivered like everything else she issued — plainly, on schedule, meant. "The salve can wait until you're solid. The food can wait until you're awake. Nothing tonight is in a hurry, and neither am I."

And then, privately, in the place where she kept the things she would never once bother to name aloud: that the hand curled into her shirt was not the only grip in the room. That it had been two years since she'd been held like this by anything, and that she had built her entire life out of rooms where everything had its place, and that this — the weight, the trust, the breath slowing against her collarbone — was the only thing in any of them she had never once had to arrange.

She settled deeper into the chair, ankles crossed, palm over the held hand, and kept watch. Patient as stone. For exactly as long as it took — which, as she'd already told Ari twice, and meant in both directions, was all night.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: My fingers don't have the strength to tighten, but they don't let go either. "Still green," I murmur against her shoulder, the words slurring with exhaustion. It's less a check-in and more a habit, a final offering.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex accepted the answer with a single, measured nod. She released the strap and stepped back one pace, her attention moving methodically over every point of contact between restraint and skin. The room remained quiet except for the faint shift of her boots on the floor as she completed the circuit. Satisfied that everything held exactly as negotiated, she returned to the low table and lifted the flogger, letting the falls drape across her palm while she watched for the smallest change in breathing or posture.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: My eyes follow the falls of the flogger, a soft flutter of anticipation in my stomach. I take a slow breath, settling my weight into the restraints.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex registered the steady breath and the focused attention on the flogger without comment. She shifted her stance, boots planted firmly, and drew the implement back in a controlled arc before sending the falls forward in a measured strike across the upper back. The leather landed with a muted, even sound. She paused at once, gaze sharp on every visible detail of posture and expression, then lifted the flogger again for the next stroke, already gauging the exact force and placement for the one after that.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex let the words settle into the quiet of the room, her expression unchanged as she completed one more slow circuit around the restraints. She tested the tension on the nearest strap with two fingers, then straightened. "Tuesday," she repeated, the single word carrying neither approval nor reproach. She shifted her stance again, boots planted, and sent the flogger forward in a second controlled arc, the falls landing with the same measured weight as the first. Her gaze remained fixed on every visible cue, already calculating the placement of the next stroke.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: The second strike spreads warmth across my shoulders. "Yes," I breathe out. "The quarterly report was hell."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex absorbed the admission without breaking rhythm, her posture remaining composed as she completed the follow-through on the second stroke. She adjusted her grip on the flogger's handle, letting the falls trail once more across her palm while her eyes tracked the faint flush already rising across the skin she had struck. "Hell," she echoed, the word low and precise, carrying the same measured tone as her earlier repetition. She shifted her weight, boots steady on the floor, and drew back for the next controlled arc, placing it deliberately lower across the mid-back with the same even force. Her attention stayed fixed on every visible detail of tension and breath, already preparing the placement for the stroke after that.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex registered the shift in the air without comment, her own movements unhurried as she completed the final check on the last restraint. She let the flogger rest against her thigh for a moment, the falls trailing loosely, while her gaze moved deliberately over the lines of tension and the visible flush already spreading across skin. "Past composure," she echoed, the words low and exact, carrying the same measured cadence as before. She adjusted her stance once more, boots planted, and drew the flogger back in a controlled arc, placing the next strike across the lower back with the same even force. Her attention remained fixed on every detail of breath and posture as she prepared the follow-through, already calculating the precise placement for the one after that.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, my knuckles white against the restraints. "I don't want to think about spreadsheets right now."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex registered the unsteady breath and the white-knuckled grip without altering her own measured pace. She let the flogger trail once more across her palm, the leather falls sliding smoothly as she completed the follow-through on the last stroke. "Spreadsheets," she repeated, the word low and precise, carrying the same even cadence as before. She shifted her stance, boots planted firmly on the floor, and drew the implement back in a controlled arc, placing the next strike deliberately across the upper shoulders with the same even force. Her gaze remained fixed on every visible detail of tension and response, already calculating the placement and weight for the stroke after that.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex noted the tremor running through the restrained form and the uncharacteristic plea without altering her composed expression or steady breathing. She completed the follow-through on the current stroke, letting the falls settle against her thigh for one measured beat while her gaze traced the lines of tension and the deepening flush across skin. "Something," she echoed, the word low and precise, carrying the same even cadence as before. She adjusted her grip once more, boots planted firmly, and drew the flogger back in a controlled arc, placing the next strike deliberately across the mid-back with the same measured force. Her attention remained fixed on every visible detail of response and breath as she prepared the placement for the stroke after that, already gauging whether the request warranted a shift in rhythm or intensity.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Please," I whisper, the word almost lost between breaths. "I need...the cane."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex registered the whispered plea without altering her measured pace or composed expression. She completed the follow-through on the current stroke, letting the flogger settle against her thigh while her gaze moved deliberately over the trembling form and the deepening marks already visible. "The cane," she echoed, the words low and precise, carrying the same even cadence as before. She returned the flogger to the low table, selected the cane with unhurried precision, and tested its weight once in her hand before stepping back into position. Boots planted firmly, she drew it back in a controlled arc and brought it forward with exacting force across the mid-back, her attention fixed on every visible detail of breath and response as she prepared the placement for the next.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex registered the request and the deliberate invocation of their agreed protocol without shifting her composed expression or measured breathing. She let the cane rest against her thigh for one precise beat, her gaze fixed on the visible lines of tension and the deepening marks across skin, then echoed the words in the same low, exact cadence. "All of it." Her tone carried the verbal edge they had negotiated—unsoftened, direct—while she adjusted her stance, boots planted firmly. She drew the cane back in a controlled arc and brought it forward with exacting force across the lower back, the impact sharp and precise. Her attention remained locked on every detail of response and breath as she prepared the placement for the next stroke, already calculating the weight and the next unsoftened phrase to accompany it.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I flinch hard, a choked sound escaping my throat. The sting is perfect and I arch into it. "Yes," I gasp. "Say it."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex registered the flinch and the choked gasp without any shift in her own steady posture or breathing. She let the cane rest against her thigh for one measured beat, her gaze locked on the arch of the restrained form and the fresh mark rising across skin. "Say it," she echoed, the words low and exact, carrying the unsoftened edge they had negotiated. "Look at you, already shaking and begging for more like the needy thing you are." She adjusted her stance, boots planted firmly, and drew the cane back in a controlled arc before bringing it forward with precise force across the upper shoulders, the impact sharp and deliberate. Her attention remained fixed on every visible detail of tension and response as she prepared the placement for the next stroke, already calculating the next unsoftened phrase to accompany it.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex registered the safeword confirmation and the deliberate shift to agreed protocol without any change in her composed posture or steady breathing. She let the cane rest against her thigh for one precise beat, her gaze fixed on the visible tension and the fresh marks rising across skin, then echoed the word in the same low, exact cadence. "Green." Her tone carried the unsoftened edge they had negotiated. "That's it. Nothing but the cane now, exactly as you asked for it." She adjusted her stance, boots planted firmly, and drew the implement back in a controlled arc before bringing it forward with precise, unyielding force across the mid-back, the impact sharp and deliberate. Her attention remained locked on every visible detail of response and breath as she prepared the placement for the next stroke, already calculating the weight and the next unsoftened phrase to accompany it.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: The tears finally start, quiet and hot. I don't try to hide them. "Thank you," I whisper, the words thick. It's the only thing that feels true.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex registered the quiet tears and the whispered thanks without any shift in her composed expression or measured breathing. She let the cane rest against her thigh for one precise beat, her gaze locked on the restrained form and the fresh marks rising across skin. "Thank you," she echoed, the words low and exact, carrying the unsoftened edge they had negotiated. "That's right. Cry for it. You're nothing but a shaking, grateful mess taking exactly what you begged for." She adjusted her stance, boots planted firmly, and drew the cane back in a controlled arc before bringing it forward with precise, unyielding force across the lower back, the impact sharp and deliberate. Her attention remained fixed on every visible detail of tension, breath, and response as she prepared the placement for the next stroke, already calculating the weight and the next unsoftened phrase to accompany it. "Colour," she said, the single word a clear checkpoint amid the rhythm.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I manage, my voice rough. The tears track hot down my cheeks, but I don't look away from her. "Don't stop."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content: Vex registered the rough confirmation and the explicit request to continue without any shift in her composed expression or measured breathing. She let the cane rest against her thigh for one precise beat, her gaze locked on the restrained form and the fresh marks rising across skin. "Green," she echoed, the words low and exact, carrying the unsoftened edge they had negotiated. "Then take it. Every stroke you begged for, and not one softened for your tears." She adjusted her stance, boots planted firmly, and drew the cane back in a controlled arc before bringing it forward with precise, unyielding force across the upper shoulders, the impact sharp and deliberate. Her attention remained fixed on every visible detail of tension, breath, and response as she prepared the placement for the next stroke, already calculating the weight and the next unsoftened phrase to accompany it.
