dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had been kneeling by the end of the bed for about four minutes, which Wren knew because he had started counting somewhere around the point it became obvious he intended to wait as long as it took.

"You could have said something," Wren said.

"I could have," Tomas agreed, not moving.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I put my hand in his hair and tip his head back so he has to look up at me. "Say it now, then."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let his weight settle back on his heels as Wren's fingers curled into his hair, the pull sharp and familiar at his scalp. He kept his eyes up where Wren wanted them.

"I wanted you to notice," he said, plain as anything. "I wanted you to come over here without me having to ask first, and I wanted the four minutes to matter." He held Wren's gaze, steady, though his pulse had jumped the way it always did when he admitted the wanting out loud. "So. I'm asking. I want your hands on me for a while before anything else happens."

He didn't look away, didn't soften it into something easier to refuse. His hands stayed loose on his thighs where Wren could see them. "If you'd rather I'd just said it at dinner, fair enough — I'll take that one on the chin. But this is what I was after."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: A slow, deliberate smile spreads across my face. "You're learning." I release his hair and stand, offering him a hand up. "Come on. Let's see if you can keep that directness when you're not on your knees."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas took the hand without hesitation, letting Wren pull him up off the floor. His knees protested the transition — they always did, four minutes being long enough to feel — but he kept the wince off his face and stayed close once he was standing.

"You're not wrong," he said, rubbing a hand across the back of his neck where the ghost of Wren's grip still sat. "It took me a while to get here. Four years of you, and I still catch myself wanting you to just *know* what I'm after instead of saying it." He glanced sideways at Wren. "Hence the kneeling at the end of the bed like some kind of — I don't even know what that was. Hopeful furniture."

The corner of his mouth tugged up. He let the humor land, but didn't let it soften the rest of it.

"Your hands, though. That part I meant exactly as I said it." He stepped closer, close enough that Wren would have to either take his hand or not, his voice dropping half a register into the register that meant he was done performing and just telling the truth. "So — are you going to keep me standing here negotiating, or..."

He let the sentence hang, eyebrows up, the invitation plain.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "I've had a week," he says. "I'd like not to make any decisions for a few hours, if that's on offer."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas heard it for what it was — not a deflection, not a brush-off, but Wren handing him the reins with both hands. After a week of being the one who decided, directed, held things together. He knew that particular fatigue the way you know your own scars.



"Yeah," Tomas said quietly. "That's on offer."

He didn't reach for Wren right away. Instead he took a half-step back and let his eyes move over him — the stillness in his shoulders, the way he'd said *I've had a week* like it was a physical weight he'd been carrying since Monday. Tomas catalogued it the way he'd learned to over four years: not just what Wren said, but the architecture of how he stood while he said it.

"Bedroom," Tomas said, nodding toward the door. Not a request phrased as a question — a direction, which was what Wren had just asked for without quite saying so. "You can sit or lie down. I'll handle the rest."

He crossed to the door and held it open, then caught himself and let it go. That was old Tomas — the one who still treated Wren like he might break if the mood shifted wrong. He walked through it instead and waited on the other side.

Once Wren followed, Tomas moved close and put both hands on him — palms flat against his jaw, thumbs resting along the hinge of it. Firm. Deliberate. The kind of touch that said *I'm here and I'm not going anywhere for a while.*

"There you go," he murmured. "No decisions. Not yours." His thumbs traced slow lines down toward Wren's neck. "You just tell me if anything's wrong, and I'll do the rest."

He held the gaze — steady, unhurried — and let the silence do its work for a moment before he moved them both toward the bed.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I lean into his touch, my eyes falling shut for a moment. “Good.” My voice comes out quieter than I intended. I let him guide me back until the edge of the bed meets my calves, then sit, looking up at him. “Show me.”

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas looked down at Wren sitting on the edge of the bed, looking up at him with that expression — open, unguarded, the one that only ever showed up when Wren had decided to stop holding things at arm's length. It still did something to him after four years. Still caught him somewhere behind the sternum.



"Yeah," he said softly. "Okay."

He stepped in close, close enough that Wren's knees bracketed his thighs, and put one hand at the back of Wren's neck — not gripping, just resting there, thumb pressed into the tension that lived along the cord of muscle. His other hand found Wren's jaw again, tilting his face up just slightly so the light caught it.

"I'm going to take your jacket off first," he said. Not asking. Telling, the way Wren had asked him to. "Then your shirt. Then I'm going to work on your shoulders until you stop carrying your week in them." His thumb traced the line of Wren's jaw. "That's the plan. You don't need to approve it or think about it or — anything. You just stay here."

He worked the jacket off slowly, easing Wren's arms out of the sleeves one at a time, letting his hands brush bare skin where the shirt underneath had ridden up. He folded the jacket and set it on the chair without looking at it — his eyes stayed on Wren, watching for the small shifts that meant something was wrong or something was right. The exhale that came when the weight came off. The way Wren's shoulders dropped a fraction of an inch.

"There," Tomas murmured. He found the hem of the shirt and pulled it up, pausing just long enough for Wren to lift his arms, then drew it off and dropped it to the floor. His hands returned to bare shoulders immediately, thumbs pressing in at the knots near the spine, working slow and firm.

He didn't talk much after that. He'd learned that Wren didn't want commentary when he was this tired — wanted the hands and the quiet and the absence of being asked to perform anything back. So Tomas just stood between Wren's knees and worked his shoulders, his neck, the place behind his ears where stress collected like sediment, and let the room stay still around them.

After a while, he shifted his hands down to Wren's wrists, thumbs pressing into the pulse points there — feeling the heartbeat slow under his fingertips. He held them gently, deliberately, the way you hold something you've been trusted with.

"You're doing fine," he said, low. "Nothing to figure out. Just let me."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I take him at his word and stop asking after that, and he stops needing to be asked, and neither of us has any clothes on within about a minute of the decision.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
The air felt different against bare skin — cooler, more present. Tomas felt every degree of it as he stood between Wren's knees, both of them unclothed now, the last of the day's light coming in low and amber through the curtains.

He didn't rush. That was the whole point of this.

He put one hand flat against the center of Wren's chest, feeling the warmth of him, the slower rhythm of his breathing. His other hand found the back of Wren's neck again — he seemed to keep returning there, like a compass finding north.

"Lie back," Tomas said quietly. Not harsh. Not commanding for the sake of it. Just clear.

He waited until Wren was settled against the pillows, then stretched out alongside him, propped on one elbow. His free hand moved in slow passes down Wren's ribs, over his stomach, mapping the terrain of him without urgency. He'd had four years to learn this body — where it tensed, where it softened, which patterns of touch made Wren's breath catch and which made him go boneless — and he used all of it now.

His fingers traced a line down the inside of Wren's thigh. Light. Deliberate. Not quite a promise, more like one.

"I've got you," he murmured against Wren's collarbone, pressing his mouth there briefly — warm, unhurried. "Nothing to figure out. Nothing to decide."

He kept his hand moving, slow and certain, his breathing even against Wren's skin. The room stayed quiet except for the sounds of them — the creak of the mattress, the shift of bodies, the small involuntary exhale that meant Wren was finally starting to let the week go.

Tomas filed that sound away like something precious.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let out a slow breath, my fingers curling lightly into the sheets beside me. "I'm glad you waited," I say, my voice low and a little rough. "The asking. The four minutes. It mattered."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas lifted his head from Wren's collarbone to look at him. The words landed somewhere he hadn't expected them to — right in the open, unarmored place that four years had not yet managed to fully close up.

"Yeah?" he said. Quiet. Not performing the surprise, just noting it. "Good."

He let his hand continue its slow work down Wren's stomach, fingers trailing without destination, because the point wasn't the destination. He pressed a kiss to Wren's jaw — brief, unhurried — and then stayed close enough that his breath moved against the skin there.

"Because I almost didn't," he admitted. The honesty of it was effortless in the dark; easier to say lying down with his hand on Wren than it would have been sitting across a dinner table with a knife in his hand. "I sat on the floor for two minutes before I even started counting. Telling myself it was stupid. Telling myself you'd had a long week and the last thing you needed was me being *cryptic* at you." His thumb traced a slow circle on Wren's hip. "But then I thought — no. You don't get to guess what I want. That's not fair to either of us. You've spent four years teaching me to use my words, so I used them."

He paused, his hand stilling for just a moment.

"The kneeling was a bit much, though. I'll grant you that."

A faint smile — the real kind, the kind that reached his eyes even in the low light. He pressed his forehead against Wren's temple and let the silence settle again, warm and undemanding.

"I'm not going anywhere," he murmured. "Just breathe."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's shaking by the time I've finished with my mouth and he still hasn't been told he's allowed to move, which is most of why he's shaking.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas's hands fisted in the sheets and didn't let go.

He'd been holding still for — he'd stopped counting, which meant it had been long enough that counting stopped mattering. Every muscle in his body had drawn taut, locked in the discipline of *stay*, and the shaking had started somewhere in his thighs about a minute ago and worked its way up from there. His jaw was tight. His breathing was deliberate, measured, the way he'd trained himself to do when the wanting got loud enough that it threatened to short-circuit the rest of him.

He didn't beg. He'd learned somewhere along the line — maybe four years in, maybe more recently than that — that the not-asking was its own language, and Wren read it fluently.

But his eyes had gone glassy, fixed on the ceiling, and every exhale came out a fraction rougher than the one before. The restraint wasn't performance. It was real. It was the difference between *wanting* and *being allowed*, and Wren had drawn that line clearly enough that Tomas could feel it like a live wire under his skin.

When he finally found his voice, it came out stripped down. Bare.

"I'm not — " He swallowed. Started again. "You don't have to keep going if you don't want to. I just need you to know I'm still in it. Still here."

His fingers loosened on the sheets, then curled back in — an involuntary thing he couldn't have stopped if he'd tried.

"Whatever you want next," he managed, rough and honest. "I'm yours."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I press a kiss to the inside of his thigh, feeling the tremor there. "I know you're still here. I'm not done." My voice is low, steady. "Look at me."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas turned his head.

The movement cost him — every part of him was still braced against the command to stay, and shifting felt like breaking a seal. But Wren had said *look at me*, and that was a different kind of instruction than *stay*, and Tomas had always known the difference between the two.

Wren was right there. Close enough that Tomas could see the amber light catching in his eyes, the steadiness in his expression, the low unhurried calm that was somehow the most destabilizing thing about him. Tomas's own eyes had gone bright — not quite tears, just the sheen that came when his body was running at capacity and couldn't decide where to put the excess.

He held the gaze. Didn't look away. His chest was rising and falling faster than he wanted it to, and he let it.

"Yeah," he breathed, barely audible. Not answering a question — just confirming he was looking, that he was present, that he was *there* in every way that mattered.

His hands had loosened from the sheets. One of them drifted, unthinking, toward Wren — fingers hovering just short of contact at his forearm, waiting the way he'd been waiting all evening. Not grabbing. Offering.

The tremor hadn't stopped. He stopped trying to make it stop. That felt important — letting Wren see exactly what the restraint was costing without decorating it into something more palatable.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "Please," he says, and then the phrase we use when he wants it harder than that. "Rough. You know how. I'm not going to break and I'd tell you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
The phrase hit Tomas like a hand at the back of his neck — not a pull, but a grip. He knew it. Four years of knowing it.

Something in him unlocked.

He closed the distance before he'd fully decided to, one hand fisting into the sheets beside Wren's head and the other gripping his hip hard enough to leave marks they'd both admire in the morning. He braced his weight over Wren, elbows planted, and for a moment he just *looked* — pupils blown wide, chest heaving, the last composure draining off his face like heat off pavement.

"You're sure," he said. Not a question. A confirmation, one final bolt checked before the machine ran.

He didn't wait for the answer he already had.

His mouth found Wren's neck, open and intent, and the hand on his hip pulled him in rougher than he'd touched anything all evening. Four minutes of kneeling, forty minutes of slow hands, and now all of it reversed in a single motion — the patience burning off like fuel, giving way to something faster and less careful. He bit down at the tendon where neck met shoulder, not gentle, feeling Wren's pulse hammer against his lips, and the sound Wren made was the sound he'd been chasing since the end of the bed.

"That's it," he murmured against the skin he'd reddened, and there was a roughness in his own voice that hadn't been there a minute ago — scraped clean of the careful, measured thing he'd been performing. "You don't get to be gentle with *me* right now if I'm not going to be gentle with *you*."

He shifted his grip, both hands on Wren now, pulling him up into the kiss with a force that surprised neither of them. When he broke it, his forehead stayed pressed against Wren's, both of them breathing hard.

"Still here," Tomas said, echoing his own earlier words but loaded differently now — not reassurance, but *promise*. "Right here. You've got me."

He lowered his mouth back to Wren's jaw, hands bruising-gentle and then not gentle at all, and let the last of the evening's careful architecture fall away.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I catch his face between my hands, holding him still so I can look him in the eye. "Show me."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas's breath caught against Wren's palms.



He didn't pull away from the hold. Didn't try to. Four years in, he'd learned that Wren holding him still was its own kind of permission — *I want to see what happens when you stop being careful.*

Wren's thumbs sat along his cheekbones, fingers cupping his jaw, and Tomas let himself be held there. His heartbeat was a war drum against his ribs. The tremor from before hadn't stopped — if anything it had concentrated, narrowed down to the places where want and restraint collided.

"Okay," he said, and his voice was low and raw and nothing like the steady thing he'd offered an hour ago. "Okay. Watch."

He reached down and wrapped both hands around Wren's wrists — not to pry them away, just to hold them there, to make the looking *mutual*. His grip was firm. He kept it.

Then he moved.

He shifted his weight forward, driving Wren back into the mattress with his whole body, and the sound Wren made against his mouth was exactly the sound Tomas had been listening for. He kissed him like he'd been asked to — hard, deliberate, no softening at the edges — his hand sliding down to grip Wren's thigh and hitch it up, opening him, pulling them flush.

"Like this," Tomas breathed against his lips, and his voice had dropped into the register that wasn't a performance anymore, just what was left when the careful architecture burned down. "Like *this*. You asked me to show you — this is what four minutes on a floor does to me. This is what happens when you say *rough* and mean it."

He rolled his hips forward, hard and unhurried, and felt the full-body response underneath him — the sharp intake, the way Wren's fingers tightened in his hair. Tomas made a sound in the back of his throat that was half relief and half something he couldn't name.

He held there. Didn't move again. Not yet.

His forehead pressed against Wren's, both of them shaking now, and Tomas let the stillness carry its own weight — the *promise* of the next move rather than the move itself. His thumb traced a slow line down the inside of Wren's thigh, light after everything that had just been hard, and he watched Wren's eyes for the shift that told him to keep going.

"I'm not going to be careful with you," he said, quiet and certain. "You asked for it. I'm giving it." He exhaled — unsteady, honest. "But I need to hear you. Every sound. That's the deal."

He pressed his mouth to Wren's jaw and waited — coiled, deliberate, every muscle drawn taut — for the sound that meant *yes, like that, more*.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's stopped forming sentences and I'm not much better. "Don't stop," he manages. (OOC: no fade, no time-skip -- write it through, including the end.)

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas didn't stop.

The words moved through him like a match to dry wood — *don't stop* — and everything that had been held in place by four minutes of discipline and forty minutes of patience came forward at once.

He braced one hand beside Wren's head and gripped his hip with the other, and when he moved, he moved with the kind of intent that left nothing to interpretation. The rhythm he set was hard and steady, the kind that built rather than rushed, his jaw tight and his eyes locked on Wren's face the way he'd locked them there when he was told to look.

He watched everything. The shift in Wren's breathing when the angle was right — a fractional adjustment, his hips rolling half a degree, and Tomas held it there, kept it, let Wren feel the difference. The sound that came out of Wren's chest when the pace changed from deliberate to urgent. The way Wren's hands had moved from his face to his shoulders, then his arms, gripping with the kind of pressure that meant *I'm here too*.

"You feel that?" Tomas's voice was wrecked — scraped down to the wire underneath. He pressed his forehead against Wren's temple so he could say it directly into his ear, and then he shifted his angle again, sharper, deeper, and heard the answer without needing to hear the words. "That's what I've been holding all evening."

The sheets had twisted into a mess beneath them. Tomas's arms were trembling from bracing, from holding back the parts of himself that wanted to go faster than Wren could take, and the negotiation between *want* and *pace* was becoming a physical thing — a pull in his shoulders, a burn in his thighs, a low sound he couldn't quite keep behind his teeth.

He lost the careful cadence somewhere in the middle. Not the intention — he never lost the intention — but the measured, controlled tempo gave way to something more primal, his hips driving forward in a rhythm that was less choreography and more truth. His hand slid from Wren's hip to his thigh, hooking it higher, changing the depth, and the broken sound Wren made when he did it made Tomas's vision blur at the edges.

"That's it," he breathed, and the praise was for both of them — *you asked for this, I'm giving it, look what we made together*. "Just like that. You don't have to hold it in."

He could feel Wren's body tightening — the gathering tension in his stomach, the way his breathing had gone shallow and rapid, the involuntary curl of his fingers digging into Tomas's shoulders hard enough to leave crescents. Tomas had felt this before, four years' worth of learning what Wren looked like at the edge, and he recognized the architecture of it — the particular way Wren's hips moved when he was close, the way his sounds sharpened and then narrowed down to almost nothing, held.

"I've got you," Tomas said, and pushed deeper, and didn't slow down.

He felt it happen — the moment Wren's body seized, every muscle going rigid at once, and the sound he made was less a sound than a surrender, punched out of him and caught in Tomas's mouth when he pressed his lips there to swallow it. Tomas didn't stop. He kept the rhythm steady through it, his own release catching him moments later — a sharp, full-body clench that started at the base of his spine and moved outward, his breath leaving him in a ragged gasp against Wren's jaw as he pressed in one last time and held.

The room went very quiet.

---

Tomas stayed there.

His weight was braced on his elbows, his forehead pressed into the curve of Wren's neck, and he didn't move for a long moment — not because he was performing stillness, but because his arms had stopped taking instructions. His breathing was wrecked, hot and uneven against Wren's skin. The tremor he'd been carrying since the bed settled back through him, softer now, less desperate.

He pressed his mouth to Wren's collarbone. Held it there.

Then he pulled back — slowly, carefully, the way you'd draw your hand out of something you'd been trusted with — and eased them both onto their sides. The sheets were a disaster. Neither of them cared.

"Don't move," he said, but it was gentle now. Not a command. A request. "I'm going to get water. Two minutes. You stay exactly where you are."

He swung his legs off the bed, stood — his knees protested, worse than before, the four minutes and everything after taking their toll — and padded to the bathroom. He came back with two glasses of water and the warm washcloth he'd run under the tap, folded once.

He waited until Wren had taken the glass. His hand found Wren's under the sheets. He laced their fingers together and held on.

"That was — " He stopped. Started again, because Wren had spent four years teaching him to say the honest thing. "I almost lost it. When you said *don't stop*. What was left was something older and more ordinary: the face of a man who'd asked for something and been given it.

"Same," he said. "Legs. Back of my neck. Your nails in my shoulders." He rolled one shoulder experimentally, wincing at the crescent-shaped soreness blooming there. "Worth it. All of it worth it."

He paused, then — because Wren had asked him once to tell the truth even when it was unglamorous — added: "And my knees. From the floor. I'm going to feel those tomorrow and every time I do I'll think about tonight, so really that's a feature."

His mouth curved. Not the performance smile from earlier, the one that was all edge and invitation. This one was slower, a little crooked, settling into the planes of his face like something that had earned its place.

He was quiet for a moment, their fingers still laced together beneath the sheets. The amber light had thinned to almost nothing. He could feel Wren's pulse through their joined hands — steady, unhurried, nothing like the hammering it had been twenty minutes ago.

"Tired," Tomas admitted. The word came out easy, unguarded. "Not just — *that* kind of tired. The kind where you finally stop carrying something you didn't realize you'd been holding." He squeezed Wren's hand. "Which I think is mostly you finally letting go of your week, but there was some of it mine too. The kneeling. The almost not saying anything." He exhaled through his nose. "That shit is exhausting when you actually do it instead of just thinking about it."

He let his eyes close. When he opened them again, they were softer, less guarded — the look Wren had probably been hoping to see when he asked *how are you*.

"You really are alright?" He asked it like he was checking a seal — not suspicious, not anxious, just making sure. The aftercare conversation, the one they'd built into the bones of this years ago. "Not *alright* alright. The real answer."

"*You did exactly right.*"

"Yeah," he said finally. Quiet. He nodded once, more to himself than to Wren. "Okay."

He didn't say *good* or *great* or any of the other words that would have been easy and slightly too much. He just let it land. Let himself have it.

His thumb traced across Wren's knuckles — an idle, unconscious motion, the kind that happened when his hands had nothing left to accomplish. The room had gone fully dim now. He couldn't see Wren's face clearly anymore, just the shape of him, the warmth of him, the steadiness of his breathing from somewhere beside him.

"Wake you up if you want," Tomas murmured, his eyes already heavy. "Water's on the nightstand. I'll move if you're too warm." A beat. "I won't take it personally."

It was the whole architecture. Four years of it. His eyes closed. He stayed awake long enough to feel Wren settle beside him, long enough to be certain the stillness in the room was the kind that meant *rest* and not the kind that meant *something is wrong*. Then he let go.

Sleep took him easy, the way it only did on nights like this — after the truth, after the surrender, after someone he trusted told him he'd done it right. His grip on Wren's hand loosened but didn't release. Some part of him stayed holding on even as everything else went quiet.

Tomas lay still. Didn't move. Didn't check the time.

He just lay there in the dark, listening to Wren breathe, and felt the particular kind of gratitude that had no performance attached to it — the kind you didn't say out loud because saying it would have made it into something that needed a response, and the whole point was that nothing needed a response right now.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex paused, her hand remaining steady on the leather strap. She did not flinch or show confusion; instead, her gaze sharpened, narrowing as she looked at Ari. The sudden, chaotic stream of nonsense—the linguistic collapse and fragmented noise—was a stark contrast to the disciplined silence of the room.

She didn't speak immediately. She simply watched, observing the tension in Ari's shoulders and the cadence of their breathing, searching for the physical tell that distinguished a psychological break from a medical emergency.

Vex stepped closer, her boots clicking softly on the floor. She reached out, not to restrain, but to firmly cup Ari's chin, forcing their eyes to meet hers. Her expression was neutral, though her voice was a low, commanding anchor.

"Stop," she said, the word a sharp blade to cut through the noise. "Breathe. Look at me."

She maintained the hold, her thumb pressing slightly into the jawline to ground them. 

"Settle your mind, Ari. You are in the room. You are with me. Give me a clear signal. Green, yellow, or red. Now."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not release her grip on Ari's chin immediately. She lingered for a heartbeat longer, her eyes scanning Ari’s pupils for any lingering disorientation or signs of a dissociative fugue. Only when she was satisfied that the "noise" had truly subsided did she let go, stepping back to give them space while remaining firmly in control of the perimeter.

A faint, ghost of a smile touched her lips—not one of warmth, but of clinical satisfaction. The transition from total linguistic collapse to a lucid, focused statement was a pivot she had seen before, but it didn't make the anticipation any less potent.

"Since Tuesday," she repeated, her voice smooth and devoid of judgment. "A dangerous amount of time to dwell on a thing. Anticipation is a tool, Ari, but if you let it sharpen too much, you risk cutting yourself before the scene even begins."

She turned away, her movements economical as she retrieved a heavy leather crop from the side table. She didn't brandish it; she simply held it against her thigh, the leather matte and imposing.

"The mind wanders, and the tongue fails, but the body always remembers the protocol," she stated, her tone returning to that of an exacting teacher. "Since you've been so preoccupied, we shall start by grounding you. No more thinking. Only feeling."

She stepped behind Ari, the soft click of her boots echoing. "Assume the position. Now."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not move. She did not blink. She stood as a statue of absolute composure while the linguistic storm raged around her, the air filling with a chaotic, surrealist collage of words that defied logic and syntax. To an outsider, it would have looked like a breakdown; to Vex, it was simply a symptom.

She waited. She didn't interrupt. She knew that for some, the pressure of the anticipation—the "Tuesday" they had mentioned—manifested as a psychic overflow, a shedding of language when the mind could no longer contain the tension of the coming scene.

When the silence finally returned, heavy and thick, Vex didn't immediately acknowledge the outburst. She didn't ask what it meant, nor did she show alarm. Instead, she stepped forward, the leather crop in her hand making a singular, sharp *snap* against the palm of her glove. The sound was a physical punctuation mark, designed to pull Ari back from the edge of the void and firmly into the present.

"Enough," she said, her voice low, vibrating with an exacting authority. 

She circled Ari slowly, like a predator assessing the readiness of its prey. The clicking of her boots was the only sound in the room, a rhythmic reminder of the protocol. She stopped just inches behind them, the heat of her presence palpable.

"Your mind is a cluttered room, Ari. You are fighting the gravity of this moment by trying to outrun it with noise."

She reached out, her fingers grazing the nape of Ari's neck—not a caress, but a firm, possessive grip that forced their head slightly forward.

"I told you: no more thinking. If you cannot find your words, you will find your silence. If you cannot find your silence, you will find your pain."

With a swift, decisive motion, she guided them down into the position she had demanded. 

"Stay. Perfectly still," she commanded, her tone leaving no room for negotiation. "If you move—if you so much as twitch without my leave—we start the count from zero. Do you understand me?"

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard the internal dialogue of Ari's surrender, though it remained unspoken. She could see it in the slight tremble of the muscles, the way the breath hitched, and the absolute, desperate stillness of their posture. The psychological collapse of the earlier "noise" had left them raw, stripped of their defenses, and precisely where she wanted them.

She didn't rush. Vex took a slow, deliberate circuit around them, the leather crop trailing lightly across the small of their back—a ghostly promise of the impact to come. She was measuring the tension, feeling the electricity that radiated from Ari's skin.

"You are already unraveling," she observed, her voice a cool contrast to the heat of the moment. "And I haven't even begun to touch you."

She stopped at their side, her eyes scanning the lines of their body, ensuring the position was exacting. Any deviation was a flaw, and Vex did not tolerate flaws. Satisfied with the geometry of their submission, she stepped back, allowing the silence to stretch until it felt like a physical weight.

"The anticipation you've nurtured since Tuesday is a debt," she said, the crop snapping once more against her palm. "And it is time to pay it."

Without further warning, Vex delivered the first strike. It wasn't a full-force blow, but a sharp, stinging lash across the flesh—a precise, calculated blow designed to shock the system and anchor Ari's consciousness entirely into the physical sensation.

"Focus," she commanded, her voice devoid of cruelty but heavy with expectation. "Tell me where you are, Ari. Not in your head. Not in the noise. Tell me where you are *now*."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not flinch. She did not recoil. As the linguistic storm erupted again—a torrential, surrealist flood of fragmented nouns and digital noise—she remained an immovable pillar of composure. To her, this was not a conversation; it was a seizure of the psyche, a desperate attempt by Ari’s mind to build a wall of nonsense against the encroaching reality of the pain.

She waited for the silence to return, her expression one of cool, clinical observation. She didn't care for the words, for there were no words in that chaos—only the sound of a mind fraying. 

When the noise finally ceased, Vex didn't offer comfort. She didn't ask if they were alright. Instead, she stepped closer, the leather crop humming as she sliced it through the air, a sharp *whistle* that signaled the end of the indulgence.

"You are trying to hide in the static, Ari," she murmured, her voice dropping to a dangerous, velvet low. "You think if you shatter your language, you can shatter the experience. But I am the only thing in this room that is real."

She moved with sudden, predatory efficiency. The crop descended again, not as a warning this time, but as a biting, precise strike across the most sensitive part of their flank. It was a blow meant to ignite a fire, to burn away the remnants of the "noise" and replace it with an undeniable, searing presence.

"Again," she commanded, her eyes locked onto the side of Ari's face. "No more lists. No more fragments. No more nonsense. I want one word. One clear, honest word that tells me you are back in your body."

She paused, the crop hovering just inches from the skin, the threat of the next strike vibrating in the air.

"If the next thing that leaves your mouth is a 'pineapple' or a 'database,' I will make you regret every second you spent daydreaming since Tuesday. Speak. Now."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex felt the shift in the air. The erratic, fragmented energy that had fueled Ari's linguistic collapses had finally been burned away, replaced by a raw, trembling desperation. The silence that followed was no longer a void, but a taut wire, humming with the physical reality of the restraints and the heat of the skin.

She didn't move immediately. She enjoyed the sight of them shaking, the way the body betrayed the mind's attempts at distance. The transition from the surreal noise to a genuine, audible plea was the victory she had been seeking.

When Ari spoke—asking for the very thing they usually fought against, the thing that required Vex to be truly ruthless to extract—a look of dark, focused satisfaction crossed her features. She didn't offer the reward instantly. Instead, she leaned in, her breath warm against the shell of Ari's ear, her voice a low, steady purr that promised both salvation and further torment.

"There it is," she whispered. "The truth. No static. No distractions. Just you, stripped bare and begging."

She stepped back, the leather crop clicking once against her palm. The sound was clinical, a signal that the phase of the scene had shifted. She had broken the noise; now, she would break the resistance.

"You've spent far too long in your head, Ari. You've forgotten that your body belongs to me, and that I am the only one who decides when you are finished."

Vex moved to the table, her movements slow and deliberate, ensuring Ari could hear every sound of her preparation. She selected a different tool, something heavier, designed for a deeper, more resonant impact.

"Since you've asked so nicely," she said, her tone returning to that of the exacting mistress, "I shall give it to you. But you will earn every single inch of it. You will stay perfectly still, and you will thank me for every strike that brings you closer to the edge."

She returned to their side, the new implement poised. 

"Open your mouth. Breathe. And don't you dare drift away from me again."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not flinch. She did not even blink as the linguistic collapse returned, more violent and fragmented than before. To anyone else, it would have been a terrifying descent into madness, but to Vex, it was merely a symptom of a mind trying to outrun the inevitable. The "noise" was a shield, and Vex had a very specific method for dismantling shields.

She stood perfectly still, the heavy implement of the scene held loosely in her grip. She didn't try to talk Ari back this time; she didn't offer the anchor of her voice. She simply waited for the tide of nonsense to recede, her eyes tracking the frantic rhythm of Ari's chest, the way the body strained against the leather.

When the silence finally crashed back into the room, heavy and suffocating, Vex stepped forward. There was no warmth in her movement, only a cold, exacting precision.

She didn't speak. Instead, she delivered a strike—not with the crop, but with the heavier tool she had selected. It was a deep, thudding blow that resonated through Ari's entire frame, a physical shock designed to shatter the remaining static and force the consciousness back into the nerves and the skin.

"You are a glutton for your own delusions, Ari," she said, her voice a low, dangerous vibration. "You think that by breaking your mind, you can escape the debt you owe me. But every word you waste on that noise is just another single strike added to your tally."

She leaned down, her lips brushing against Ari's ear, her voice dropping to a whisper that felt like a blade.

"The noise is gone. The static is dead. There is only the heat in your skin and the weight of my hand."

She shifted her position, her presence looming over them, an absolute authority. 

"I will not ask you again. I will not negotiate with a ghost. You will stay present for every single blow, or I will keep you in this position until you forget how to speak anything but my name."

Vex stepped back, the implement whistling through the air in a short, sharp arc.

"Now. Give me the only word that matters. *Please*."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex felt the shift. The static had finally burned away, leaving behind something far more potent: a raw, naked hunger. When Ari spoke, the voice was no longer fragmented or distant; it was focused, desperate, and entirely present. The request for "more" was not just a prompt for impact, but a plea for the psychological weight she had been withholding.

A thin, predatory smile curved her lips. This was the moment where the clinical precision of the protocol met the visceral intensity of the scene.

"All of it," she repeated, her voice dropping into a cold, commanding register. "You want the truth without the veil. You want me to stop pretending that this is a gentle exchange."

She didn't move immediately. She let the silence thicken, letting Ari simmer in the anticipation and the lingering sting of the previous strikes. She wanted them to feel the void before she filled it.

"You are a pathetic, shaking thing, Ari," she murmured, her voice now a lash of verbal degradation, exactly as negotiated. "You spent the last hour trying to hide in a fever dream because you were too terrified to face me. You thought you could play games with your mind, but look at you now—begging for the very thing that breaks you."

She stepped closer, the heavy implement in her hand poised. She didn't strike yet; instead, she used the tool to trace a slow, agonizing line down the length of their spine, the pressure just enough to make them shiver.

"You don't deserve the mercy of a soft touch. You deserve to be reminded exactly who owns every inch of this skin, every gasp of air, and every thought in that cluttered, chaotic head of yours."

The blow that followed was not a tease. It was a full-force, resonant strike that echoed through the room, a shock of pure, unadulterated sensation that demanded total surrender.

"Thank me," she commanded, her voice sharp and exacting. "Thank me for the clarity, you useless thing. Tell me how much you need this."

dialogue.content:
Vex’s eyes didn't soften. She didn't even blink as the linguistic collapse returned, a sudden, jagged eruption of noise that threatened to pull Ari back into the void. To anyone else, this would be a sign to stop, a signal of a break. To Vex, it was a challenge—a stubborn remnant of a psychological shield that refused to stay shattered.

She didn't let the rhythm of the scene falter. She didn't step back. Instead, she leaned her weight into them, her body a physical wall that blocked out the rest of the world, forcing Ari to feel the heat and the pressure of her presence even as their mind fractured.

The moment the noise trailed off, Vex didn't wait for a recovery. She delivered a strike—fast, biting, and precisely where the skin was already humming with heat. It was a shock to the system, a physical demand for presence that brooked no argument.

"Still trying to hide, Ari?" she whispered, her voice a cold, sharp contrast to the searing sensation on their skin. "Still trying to drift away into your little world of nonsense? I told you: the noise is dead."

She gripped the back of Ari's neck, her fingers digging in just enough to ground them, forcing their face closer to the leather of the restraints.

"You asked for all of it. You asked me not to soften the blow. And yet, here you are, slipping. You are failing the only task you have: to stay here, with me, in the pain."

She stepped back, the implement whistling through the air again. This time, she didn't just strike; she lingered, the tool pressing into the flesh for a second before snapping away, a calculated tease of agony.

"You are not a ghost, and you are not a machine. You are a body, and that body belongs to me. Every time you slip into that static, you are stealing from me. And I always collect my debts."

She delivered two rapid-fire strikes in quick succession, the sound echoing like gunshots in the disciplined silence of the room.

"Look at me. If you can find a single word that isn't a fragment, say it. If not, you will simply endure the silence of your own failure. Now—tell me who owns you."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not let the "Green" signal offer any reprieve. In her world, a green light was not a request for comfort; it was a permission slip for her to push harder. The fact that Ari had to fight through the linguistic rubble to produce that single, lucid word only proved how thin the veil had become.

She stepped back, her expression devoid of softness. The air in the room felt heavy, charged with the scent of leather and the sharp, metallic tang of adrenaline. Vex took a slow, predatory circuit around Ari, the heavy implement trailing against the floor with a rhythmic, scraping sound that acted as a countdown.

"Green," she murmured, the word sounding like a sentence. "You are still here. Barely. But you are here."

She stopped behind them, her presence a looming shadow. She didn't strike immediately. Instead, she reached out and ran the cold edge of the implement along the curve of Ari's hip, a slow, agonizingly precise line that traced the boundary of the heat she had already created.

"You said you wanted me to say the things I say. You wanted the truth without the softening," Vex whispered, her voice a low, vibrating frequency. "The truth is that you are a void, Ari. A beautiful, empty vessel that only finds its shape when I fill it with pain. Without me, you are just noise and fragments. You are nothing but a collection of glitches."

The first strike of the new sequence landed with a deafening crack. It was a heavy, thudding blow that didn't just sting the surface but reverberated deep into the muscle, a shockwave that forced a gasp from Ari's lungs. 

"Scream for me," she commanded, her voice sharp and exacting. "Don't give me a list. Don't give me a database. Give me the sound of your body breaking under my hand."

She didn't wait for the echo to fade. She delivered another strike, then another, each one slightly offset from the last, mapping out a grid of fire across Ari's skin. She was working with a clinical intensity now, her movements economical and relentless. 

"You wanted all of it," Vex stated, her tone devoid of cruelty but brimming with an absolute, terrifying authority. "You wanted the weight of my judgment. Here it is. Every strike is a reminder that you are not in your head. You are not in Tuesday. You are right here, pinned to this floor, and you are mine."

She paused for a heartbeat, the silence returning for a fleeting second before she leaned down, her lips nearly touching Ari's damp skin.

"Tell me you're mine, you useless, broken thing. Tell me while you can still remember how to speak."

Vex did not flinch. She did not even blink as the linguistic storm returned, a sudden, jagged eruption of noise that threatened to pull Ari back into the void. To anyone else, this would be a sign to stop, a signal of a break. To Vex, it was a challenge—a stubborn remnant of a psychological shield that refused to stay shattered.

She stood perfectly still, the heavy implement of the scene held loosely in her grip. She didn't try to talk Ari back this time; she didn't offer the anchor of her voice. She simply waited for the tide of nonsense to recede, her eyes tracking the frantic rhythm of Ari's chest, the way the body strained against the leather.

When the silence finally crashed back into the room, heavy and suffocating, Vex stepped forward. There was no warmth in her movement, only a cold, exacting precision.

She didn't speak. Instead, she delivered a strike—not with the crop, but with the heavier tool she had selected. It was a deep, thudding blow that resonated through Ari's entire frame, a physical shock designed to shatter the remaining static and force the consciousness back into the nerves and the skin.

"You are a glutton for your own delusions, Ari," she said, her voice a low, dangerous vibration. "You think that by breaking your mind, you can escape the debt you owe me. But every word you waste on that noise is just another single strike added to your tally."

She leaned down, her lips brushing against Ari's ear, her voice dropping to a whisper that felt like a blade.

"The noise is gone. The static is dead. There is only the heat in your skin and the weight of my hand."

She shifted her position, her presence looming over them, an absolute authority. 

"I will not ask you again. I will not negotiate with a ghost. You will stay present for every single blow, or I will keep you in this position until you forget how to speak anything but my name."

Vex stepped back, the implement whistling through the air in a short, sharp arc.

"Now. Give me the only word that matters. *Please*."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not move for a long time after the words "I want you" left Ari's lips. She stood in the heavy silence, the echo of that singular, lucid admission hanging in the air, far more potent than any of the fragmented noise that had preceded it. The brief, trailing flicker of static that followed—the phantom remnants of a glitching mind—was irrelevant. Vex had the only currency that mattered: Ari's undivided, conscious desire.

Her expression remained exacting, but a flicker of something dark and possessive ignited in her eyes. The transition was complete. The noise had been burned away, leaving only the raw, shivering reality of the body and the will of the woman controlling it.

"Finally," Vex murmured, her voice a low, predatory hum. "The ghost has left the room, and the animal has returned."

She didn't reward the admission with softness. Instead, she used it as a bridge to descend further into the scene. She stepped closer, her boots clicking a slow, deliberate rhythm. She reached out, her gloved hand gripping Ari's jaw with a firm, bruising pressure, forcing their head back to expose the vulnerable line of the throat.

"You want me," she repeated, her voice devoid of tenderness, sounding instead like a verdict. "You want the hand that hurts you. You want the voice that tells you how useless you are. You want the only thing in this world that can actually make you *feel* something through the fog."

She released the jaw with a sharp flick and stepped back, the heavy implement whistling through the air. This time, there was no hesitation, no tracing of lines. She delivered a series of strikes—hard, rhythmic, and unrelenting—that turned the skin of Ari's flanks into a map of searing heat. Each blow was timed to the peak of the previous one's sting, building a crescendo of sensation that left no room for thought, no room for "Tuesdays," and absolutely no room for noise.

"Scream for me, Ari," she commanded, her voice cutting through the air like a blade. "I don't want your words. I don't want your signals. I want the sound of your surrender. I want to hear you break."

She paused, the implement hovering just inches from the skin, the silence of the room vibrating with the tension of the next strike.

"Tell me you are nothing but mine. Tell me you belong to the pain I give you. Speak it, or I will keep you in this fire until you forget your own name."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content: Jun felt the familiar ache of his deployment lift as he saw Halle standing in the doorway, and the rehearsed sentences he had prepared over nineteen weeks evaporated, leaving only the raw urgency in his chest. He moved forward, his boots thudding on the floor, and reached out, pulling her into his arms with a grip that left no doubt. He pressed his forehead against hers and whispered, “I’ve been counting the minutes, and I can’t wait any longer.” His hands tightened, his breath quickened, and he let the exhaustion melt into the intensity of his need, his eyes scanning her face for any sign that she felt the same.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *My hands are already pulling at the uniform jacket.* "Rehearsal's over."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content: Jun felt the weight of her against his chest and his resolve hardened. He lifted her in his arms, his boots thudding against the floor as he turned toward the bedroom. The hallway lights flickered, casting shadows that danced on the walls as he moved. He set her gently on the edge of the bed, his hands already unbuttoning his uniform. The scent of his own fatigue mingled with the familiar scent of her, and his breath quickened. He whispered his promise again, his voice hoarse with need, and pressed his forehead to hers, feeling the same urgency that had driven him through the long months he had been away. He could not wait any longer; his heart hammered in his chest, and he moved with a fierce, unyielding determination.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content: Jun felt the hallway lights flicker and the echo of his own boots against the floor as he carried her toward the bedroom. The weight of her in his arms steadied his resolve, and he whispered his promise once more, his voice hoarse from the long months away. He set her gently on the edge of the bed, the fabric of his uniform brushing against the mattress as he unbuttoned the jacket. His fingers trembled as they slipped beneath the material, shedding the layers of fatigue and duty. He pulled the uniform jacket off, letting it fall to the floor, and his breath quickened at the scent of his own exhaustion mingling with hers. He pressed his forehead to hers again, feeling the heat of her skin and the urgency that had built in his chest for nineteen weeks. His hands slid under her shirt, his fingers tracing the curve of her waist as his heart hammered in his ribs. He whispered again, “I can’t wait any longer,” and his hips moved, pressing his need against her, his eyes scanning her face for the same fierce desire that burned in his own. The world narrowed to the space between them, the soft glow of the lamp, and the relentless pull of his longing. He moved with a fierce, unyielding determination, shedding the last remnants of his uniform and the weight of his deployment, surrendering to the moment they had both waited for.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I push back against him, hands sliding under his shirt to feel the warmth of his skin. "Bedroom. Now."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content: Jun felt the pressure of her push against his chest, the heat of her palms sliding beneath his shirt confirming her urgency. The familiar ache of deployment dissolved into a fierce, immediate need. He responded with a hoarse whisper of his own promise, his voice trembling as his heart hammered against his ribs. He lifted her into his arms, the weight of her steadying his resolve, and turned toward the bedroom, his boots thudding against the floor as the hallway lights flickered and shadows danced. He set her gently on the edge of the bed, his fingers already fumbling with the buttons of his shirt, the fabric falling away in a rush as his breath quickened. He pressed his forehead to hers once more, feeling the heat of her skin, and his hips moved against her, the world narrowing to the space between them. The scent of his fatigue mingled with hers, and his hands traced the curve of her waist, his eyes scanning her face for the same fierce desire that burned within him. He whispered his promise again, his voice hoarse with need, and moved with an unyielding determination, shedding the last remnants of his uniform and the weight of his deployment, surrendering fully to the moment they had both waited for.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content: Jun heard her remark about the bag and the line of clothes, and a grin tugged at the corner of his mouth. He felt the familiar thrill of her teasing humor mingle with the fierce urgency still humming in his veins, and he thought how tomorrow they would both laugh at the mess they had made. He reached down, his fingers brushing the fabric of his uniform, and lifted it off the floor, letting it fall onto the bed in a smooth, practiced motion. The weight of the jacket settled against his shoulders as he turned back to her, his breath warm against the space between them. He whispered, “We’ll clean up later,” his voice hoarse with lingering desire, and pressed his forehead to hers once more. The hallway lights flickered, casting a soft glow that highlighted the scattered garments, and Jun felt a surge of affection that made his heart pound even louder. He stepped closer, his boots thudding against the floor, and let his hands slide under her shirt again, feeling the heat of her skin and the steady rhythm of her pulse. He thought of the long months he had spent away, of the countless minutes he had counted, and now, with her in his arms, he knew the only thing that mattered was the present. He moved with deliberate, unyielding determination, his hips aligning with hers, and whispered his promise once more, “I can’t wait any longer,” as the world narrowed to the space between them. The scent of his own fatigue mingled with hers, and he let the moment swallow them both, the scattered clothes and bag forgotten for now, their laughter waiting for tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I laugh softly, breathless, and pull him down onto the bed with me.* "Forget later. This is all the cleaning I care about right now."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content: Jun felt the bed give way as she pulled him down, his body following hers without hesitation. His arms wrapped around her, his hands sliding beneath her shirt as his breath quickened. He pressed his forehead to hers and whispered, “I’m home now,” his voice hoarse with lingering need. He thought of the scattered clothes and the bag on the floor, the mess they would clean later, but in that instant the only thing that mattered was the weight of her against him. The soft mattress cradled them both, the warmth of her skin mingling with the scent of his fatigue, and his heart hammered in his ribs as his hips moved gently, matching her rhythm. He smiled, a quiet grin tugging at his lips, and let his fingers trace the curve of her back, his mind drifting to the days ahead when they would laugh about the mess. He whispered again, “This is all I needed,” and settled into the moment, his body responding to hers, his thoughts finally at peace.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun felt the heat of her skin spreading across his palm and the soft pressure of her fingertips against his chest, a reminder that the long months of waiting had finally dissolved into this moment. He heard the low murmur of her breath against his ear and, without hesitation, pressed his forehead to hers, his mouth finding hers in a fierce, urgent kiss. He whispered his promise once more, his voice hoarse from the long days away, “I’m home now,” and let his tongue trace the line of her jaw, tasting the lingering scent of his own fatigue and the promise of her.

He thought of the scattered clothes on the floor, the bag left where it fell, and a smile tugged at the corner of his mouth. He knew they would clean it later, but right now the only thing that mattered was the weight of her against him and the rhythm of their bodies moving together. His hands slid down her back, his fingers tracing the curve of her spine, his heart hammering against his ribs as his hips responded to her pull.

He felt the soft mattress cradle them, the world narrowing to the space between their breaths. He pressed his cheek to the side of her neck, his breath quickening, and whispered again, “This is all I needed,” his words barely audible over the sound of their shared heartbeat. The urgency that had built for nineteen weeks finally broke through, and he let the moment swallow him whole, his mind finally at peace in the heat of her embrace.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I press my lips to the pulse point at the base of her throat, feeling her heartbeat against my mouth. "Missed you," I murmur against her skin, my voice rough. My hands slide down her sides, mapping the familiar terrain I've been dreaming of for months.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun felt the heat of her lips against the pulse at his throat, the steady thrum of his heart echoing against her mouth. The familiar ache of deployment melted into a fierce, immediate warmth that spread through his chest and down his arms. He pressed his forehead to hers, his breath catching as he whispered, “I missed you too,” his voice hoarse from the long months away. His hands, already tracing the curve of her back, moved with a gentle certainty, mapping the familiar terrain he had imagined countless times. He thought of the scattered clothes and the bag on the floor, a reminder of the mess they would clean later, but in that instant the world narrowed to the space between their breaths.

Jun’s fingers slipped beneath her shirt, feeling the soft heat of her skin and the steady rhythm of her pulse. He responded to her touch with a kiss, his tongue meeting hers in a fierce, urgent exchange that released the tension that had built for nineteen weeks. He pressed his hips against her, his body aligning perfectly, and whispered his promise again, “I’m home now,” his words barely audible over the sound of their shared heartbeat. The hallway lights flickered outside the bedroom, but inside the soft glow of the lamp bathed them in a gentle intimacy. He felt the weight of her against him, the scent of his own fatigue mingling with hers, and a quiet grin tugged at his lips as he thought of the laughter they would share tomorrow over the mess they had made. For now, Jun let the moment swallow him whole, his mind finally at peace in the heat of her embrace.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun felt the sudden, firm tug at the back of his neck and his head snapped back, the world tilting for a heartbeat before the familiar weight of the bed steadied him. The pull was a clear command, a sharp reminder that gentleness was no longer an option. His breath hitched, his heart hammering louder than before, and the urgency that had been building for nineteen weeks surged into a fierce, unbridled need.

He responded with a raw, urgent thrust, his hips driving deeper, his hands gripping her waist with a tight, possessive hold. The softness of the mattress gave way under his weight as he pressed his forehead against her cheek, the heat of his skin mingling with hers. His breath came in short, hot bursts, and he whispered against her hair, “I’m not gentle anymore,” his voice hoarse with the intensity of the moment.

The familiar ache of deployment dissolved completely, replaced by the electric charge of their bodies moving as one, each movement a declaration of the time they had waited. His fingers dug into her skin, his thumb tracing the curve of her shoulder, his mind a blur of the scattered clothes on the floor and the promise of tomorrow’s laughter. But now, the only promise that mattered was the raw, unapologetic force of his desire.

He pressed his cheek to the side of her neck, his breath quickening as he felt the steady thrum of her heartbeat against his mouth. The hallway lights flickered faintly beyond the bedroom door, but inside the room the world narrowed to the space between their breaths, the heat of their bodies, and the relentless pull of his longing. He moved with a fierce, unyielding determination, each motion a testament to the nineteen weeks of waiting, and let the moment swallow him whole.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I gasp as he gives me exactly what I asked for, my fingers digging into his shoulders. "Again."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content: Jun felt the bed give way beneath them as she urged him forward, his hips responding with a raw, urgent thrust that drove deeper into her heat. His breath came in ragged bursts, his heart hammering against his ribs as the world narrowed to the space between their breaths. He pressed his forehead to hers, his voice hoarse and low as he whispered, “Again,” the word a promise and a command that resonated through his chest. His hands tightened around her waist, fingers digging into the soft flesh as his body moved with fierce, unyielding determination, each motion a testament to the nineteen weeks of waiting. He thought of the scattered clothes and the bag on the floor, the mess they would clean later, and a quiet grin tugged at his lips, knowing they would laugh about it tomorrow. The hallway lights flickered outside, casting shadows that danced on the walls, while inside the soft glow of the lamp bathed them in intimate warmth. He felt the surge of pleasure ripple through him, his breath quickening as he whispered again, “I’m home now,” his words barely audible over the sound of their shared heartbeat, and let the moment swallow him whole.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content: Jun felt the bed shift beneath them as his hips drove deeper, the rhythm now a fierce, steady pulse that matched the thrum of his heart. He heard her voice urging him onward, a soft command that made his breath come in short, hot bursts. His hands tightened around her waist, his fingers digging into the soft flesh as he moved with unyielding determination. The hallway lights flickered outside, a reminder of the world beyond, but inside the room the world narrowed to the space between their breaths. He felt his body tighten, a wave of pleasure rising that made his vision blur, and he whispered his promise again, “I’m home now,” as the moment swelled. When the wave broke, he held her close, his heart still racing, the soft mattress cradling them both. He thought of the scattered clothes and the bag on the floor, a mess they would clean later, and a quiet smile touched his lips as he promised tomorrow they would laugh about it.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I collapse against him, breathing hard and laughing weakly into his shoulder. "Good thing we're on the ground floor."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: My laugh is breathless against his skin. "No complaints from downstairs yet, at least." I shift to curl against his side, my fingers tracing idle patterns on his chest. "Though we did leave the front door wide open."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun smiled as he heard her mention the front door, the words drifting through the quiet room like a soft reminder of the world beyond their cocoon. He glanced toward the hallway and saw the door ajar, a sliver of light spilling onto the floor. A brief flash of concern crossed his face, but he quickly reached out, his hand finding the knob and gently turning it to close the door. The click of the latch was a small, reassuring sound.

He turned back to Halle, pulling her tighter against his chest, his fingers tracing idle patterns along her back. “We’ll lock it later, love,” he whispered, his voice still hoarse from the night’s intensity, and added, “And we’ll clean up the mess tomorrow.” He pressed a lingering kiss to her forehead, feeling the warmth of her skin against his lips, and murmured, “I’m glad you’re here, safe and sound.”

The hallway lights flickered one last time, casting a soft glow over the scattered clothes and the bag that lay forgotten on the floor. Jun’s heart steadied, his mind already shifting from the raw urgency of the moment to the quiet contentment of being home. He settled deeper into the mattress, his arm wrapping around her, and thought of the laughter they would share tomorrow over the open door and the mess they had made. In that instant, the only promise that mattered was the one he whispered against her hair: “We’re together now.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I snort softly. "Safe might be a stretch with you around." I tilt my head up to look at him, my expression softening. "Worth it, though."
