Some time later — he had lost the thread of time completely and considered it a fair trade — he lay tangled with her in their bed, in their room, under the crooked picture frame she'd refused to straighten since 2019, one arm locked around her like his body still didn't fully trust the evidence. His other hand moved idle and slow over her back, up and down, the way a man checks that a connection is still live.

It was. It had held. She was warm and solid and breathing against his chest, and the ache he'd carried around for five months like a second rucksack was — gone. Just gone. Set down somewhere in the hallway along with everything else.

"For the record," he said finally, voice rough and low and aimed at the ceiling, "that was first on the list. The whole list. Everything else was padding. Dinner was a cover story." He pressed his mouth to her hair and stayed there, breathing her in — home, not a screen. "Also for the record: the trail of clothes out there is going to be extremely funny tomorrow, and I want it noted that I knew that going in, and I chose it anyway. No regrets. Full foresight."

He tightened his arm around her, just once, like a signature.

"I'm not going anywhere," he said. Quieter. Not a joke at all.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I trace my fingers over the line of his shoulder, my head resting against his chest. "Dinner can stay a cover story." A soft laugh escapes me. "But you're cooking tomorrow. I've had five months of cafeteria food."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun made a sound against her hair that could only be described as wounded.

"*Cafeteria food.*" He propped himself up on one elbow to look at her, performing the outrage with his whole chest. "I want the record to show that I have spent five months eating food prepared in industrial quantities by a man named Dokes who referred to all of it as 'chow' regardless of what it was, and you're claiming hardship because your office cafeteria's soup rotation got stale. This is stolen valor, Halle. I am the aggrieved party here."

He dropped back down onto the pillow, but his hand resumed its slow patrol up and down her spine, undercutting the grievance entirely.

"That said — deal. Enthusiastically. I'll cook. I'll cook *everything*. You think the list was long? The menu list was longer. I had a whole document. There were tabs." He pressed his mouth to her temple and stayed there a moment. "Five months of MREs and I became a man with strong opinions about fresh herbs. I'm going to the grocery store tomorrow and I'm genuinely excited about it, which should tell you everything. A grocery store. With produce. I dreamed about the produce section, and that's not a euphemism, it was just a very sad dream."

His fingers found a knot at the base of her neck and worked at it, slow and careful, like he had all the time in the world — because, for the first time in nineteen weeks, he did.

"One condition, though." His voice went quieter, losing the performance. "You have to sit on the counter and talk to me while I cook. I'm not — " He exhaled, half a laugh at himself. "I'm not doing rooms you're not in yet. Give me a week before I can handle being in the kitchen while you're in the living room like a normal person. Right now my working model is: wherever you are, that's the room. I'll adjust. Eventually. Probably."

He pulled her in closer, fitting her against him like his body had been holding the shape of her absence for five months and finally got to stop.

"So tomorrow's agenda," he murmured into her hair. "Grocery store. Laundry. Locating my other boot, which is somewhere in the hallway living its own life now. Cooking you an unreasonably elaborate dinner. The whole boring miracle of it." His arm tightened, once, like a signature. "I've been looking forward to boring for nineteen weeks. You have no idea how good boring sounds."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had spent five months intending to do exactly this to her — it was on the list, it was most of the list, there were subsections — and he got roughly one breath into narrating that fact before her mouth made the entire document irrelevant.

"Okay, so — for the record, this was — " The record reflected nothing. His head went back against the pillow and the sentence left his body whole.

The commentary had been his coping mechanism for nineteen weeks, and it failed him inside a minute. Her hands were warm and unhurried and *sure* — six years of sure — and his own hands kept finding her hair, her shoulder, the back of her neck, not guiding, just holding. Confirming. The way he'd been doing since the door, like the connection might drop. It didn't drop. It held, and held, and somewhere in the slow, deliberate undoing of him, Jun — who had talked his way through the doorway, the wall, the hallway, the whole reunion — hit the bottom of his vocabulary. It turned out to be shallow. Her name, mostly. Once a laugh that broke in the middle. Once, wrecked and entirely sincere: "Don't stop. I'm serious. I'll actually die. It'll be on the news and I'll deserve it."

Because that was the thing he hadn't planned for, in all nineteen weeks of planning. He'd planned for wanting her. He had not planned for what it would feel like to be *known* — to have her find every place that undid him with the ease of long practice, to be read like a document she'd written herself, after five months of being a voice at terrible hours and a face frozen mid-syllable. Five months of no touch at all, it turned out, left a man with no defenses. None. He got a forearm over his eyes at one point, not because of the act but because of the being seen, breathing her name into the crook of his elbow like it was the only word he'd kept.

She took him apart slowly, exactly as advertised, and Jun let her — surrendered the list, the record, the whole annotated archive, let it all burn — until he couldn't stand it anymore, until the slow undoing had undone him completely, and he reached down and pulled her up the length of him with hands that were not entirely steady, and kissed her, deep and helpless and laughing a little into it, wrecked past speech and still somehow talking.

"Hi," he said, against her mouth, breathing hard. It was still the only word that had survived contact. "Hi. I had — there was a whole — " He gave up, pressed his forehead to hers, and just breathed for a second, one arm locked around her back, his heart going like he'd sprinted the fifteen feet from the front door. "Nineteen weeks of rehearsal," he managed, rough and fond and utterly dismantled, "and you walk in and improvise better than my entire document. I want that noted. I want it in the record. The record's on fire, but I want it in there."

He tightened his arm around her, once, like a signature, and kissed her again — slower now, deeper, in no hurry at all, because for the first time in five months there was no clock, no connection, no countdown.

"Your turn," he murmured, warm against her mouth, a promise with nineteen weeks of drafting behind it. "The list had subsections."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *My hands slide up his chest, nails dragging lightly.* "Show me the subsections, then. Slowly." *I kiss the corner of his mouth, lingering.* "We have all night to set the record straight."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun laughed — low, delighted, against her mouth — and rolled them over with an efficiency that suggested at least *some* of the nineteen weeks of rehearsal had survived contact after all.

"The document's on fire," he said, braced over her, "but I have it memorized. All of it. There were appendices. I want that noted before we begin." He kissed her once, slow and deep, and then pulled back just far enough to look at her — hair everywhere, his sheets, his bed, *his* — and the grin went soft at the edges. "Slowly. Yes. Agreed. Slowly was the whole point of the subsections. Anyone can do the headline."

He started at the top anyway, because he was thorough.

Subsection one was the spot below her ear, the one he'd thought about with a frequency he'd planned to take to his grave, and he took his time with it now — unhurried, reverent, five months of imagining collapsed into the warm reality of her skin against his mouth. Subsection two was her throat, the line of it, the place where her pulse ran fast under his lips. He noted that. Filed it. The record was burning but he was still, apparently, incapable of not keeping it.

"Revising in real time," he murmured against her collarbone. "The freckle was three inches off. Nineteen weeks and I had it at the wrong coordinates. I'm embarrassed. I'm correcting the map." His mouth moved to the freckle in question, then to the small scar he'd kissed goodbye at an airport once, and his hands traveled ahead of him the whole way — ribs, waist, the dip of her back — relearning her by Braille, verifying, confirming the evidence of his own eyes. "You're aware I'm going to narrate this entire thing."

He was not, as it turned out, going to narrate the entire thing.

The commentary held through her shoulder, thinned somewhere along her ribs, and failed him completely not long after — the way it had failed him in the hallway, the way it kept failing him tonight, because five months of being a voice at terrible hours had left him with a deep backlog of things to say and no interest whatsoever in saying them with words. He said them with his hands instead, with his mouth, slow as promised, slow as ordered, working his way down the length of her with a patience that cost him something and was worth every cent of it. No clock. No connection. No countdown. Just her, warm and real and *here*, and all the time in the world to prove he'd memorized every line.

He paused once, at her hip, and pressed a kiss there and just breathed for a second — one, just to confirm — and when he looked up at her the joke slid off his face for a moment and let the real thing show through.

"I thought about this," he said, quiet and rough. "On the cot. At two in the morning. This exact — you, here, taking my time. I want it in the record that the imagination did not do it justice. The imagination was a crayon drawing." He kissed her hip again, and the grin came back, slow and wicked and entirely wrecked underneath. "Subsection four. Don't skip ahead. There's an order of operations — I was a soldier, I believe in procedure."

Then he stopped keeping records entirely, and set about proving it.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun went still above her.

Not the checking-the-connection stillness. A different kind — the stillness of a man who had just been handed the one thing he'd spent nineteen weeks not letting himself ask for out loud.

"For the record," he said, low, "you said that. Verbally. Out loud. I want it entered into evidence, because tomorrow, when you feel it, I intend to be insufferable about it, and I want the documentation to hold up." His hand tightened at her hip — not careful now, not reverent, hard enough to make the point she'd asked for. "Witnesses: none. Ruling: mine."

Then he stopped being gentle.

The careful thing he'd been doing all night — the inventory, the map-correcting, the slow reverent verification — burned off all at once, and what was under it was the doorway kiss, the too-hard off-center one, nineteen weeks stacked up behind it with no list left to catch them. He kissed her like that and pinned her with his whole body and let her feel exactly how long five months was. His hands were rough now. His mouth was rough now. Teeth at her shoulder where the freckle was, at the corrected coordinates, like he intended to leave the revision *in* her — a mark, a proof, something that would still be there tomorrow when he was in the produce section having feelings about herbs.

The narration held for about thirty seconds.

"Subsection — " was as far as he got. Then it was fragments. Then it was her name. Then it was nothing at all, Jun who had talked his way through the doorway and the wall and the hallway and the whole reunion finally, completely out of words, all nineteen weeks of drafts ash, everything he'd been holding back since the door opened let off its leash at once.

And here was the thing he knew and would never say out loud, not even to the ceiling, not even to the record: the gentleness had never been the care. The care was the checking. And he never stopped doing that — not once, not even now, not even at his most wrecked and wordless. His hand at the back of her neck. His forehead dropping to hers for one second, one, just to confirm. His eyes finding her face in the dark of their bedroom like a man watching a signal that had never once, this time, dropped. It held. She was warm and solid and *here* and it held, and he poured five months of terrible-hour phone calls and frozen screens and a cot that smelled like dust and jet fuel into the proof of it, into her, into the promise she'd demanded and he was entirely, enthusiastically prepared to keep.

After — some time after, time having gone soft and useless again, a trade he continued to endorse — he lay with his face pressed into her neck, breathing like a man who had sprinted considerably further than fifteen feet, one arm locked across her like a barricade. His thumb moved once over the mark he'd left at her shoulder. Confirming the evidence of his own work.

"Tomorrow," he said, hoarse, into her skin, "is going to be extremely funny. The clothes in the hall. The boot. You, feeling that. Me, insufferable, with documentation." He pressed his mouth to her pulse and stayed there. "Agenda's set. Groceries, laundry, dinner, and me being smug. I've been looking forward to boring for nineteen weeks and I want it noted that boring now includes *this*. Best document I ever drafted."

His arm tightened, once, like a signature.

"Hi," he said. Still the only word. Still all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I'm still breathing hard, my fingers tangled in his hair. "Don't you dare be smug tomorrow." I kiss his shoulder, right over the spot where I know I left my own mark. "I'll just remind you who asked for it."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun felt her mouth find the mark on his shoulder and laughed — low, wrecked, delighted — into the dark of their room.

"Matching evidence," he said. "Mutual documentation. You understand what you've done. Tomorrow we both feel it, and neither of us can say a single word the other can't answer. It's a stalemate. Mutually assured smugness." He craned his neck trying to inspect the spot, failed at the angle, and gave up, dropping back onto the pillow with her warm against his side. "I want it noted that the evidence is in a structurally inconvenient location and I'm taking your word for it. It felt extremely — yes. Noted. Filed."

His thumb found the mark he'd left at her shoulder and moved over it once, slow. Confirming the evidence of his own work.

"And I'll remind *you* that 'who asked for it' is not the defense you think it is. You asked. I provided. That's not a scandal, that's a supply chain. I have nineteen weeks of backlog and a standing offer to clear it. Ask again in the morning. Ask again at breakfast. I'm going to be insufferable *and* responsive — that's the whole package, you married it, there are no returns."

He was quiet a moment. His hand resumed its slow patrol up and down her spine, and the performance thinned the way it kept doing tonight, letting the real thing show through.

"Six years," he said. "This exact argument. You telling me not to be smug, me being smug anyway, you reminding me of the facts. I missed it. I want that in the record — I missed *arguing* with you. Nineteen weeks of phone calls at terrible hours, and you know what I thought about on that cot? Not the big stuff. You stealing the blanket. The crooked frame. This." He pressed his mouth to her hair. "The whole stupid miracle of it."

His arm tightened, once, like a signature.

"So. Terms." The grin came back, audible in the dark. "I get breakfast smugness, non-negotiable. You get to remind me who asked for it at lunch. At dinner I cook something unreasonably elaborate and we call it even. Counter-offers welcome. You have all night to — " He yawned, enormously, mid-sentence, betraying himself completely. "That yawn was tactical. It proves nothing. I'm wide awake."

He was not wide awake. His body had figured out before his mouth had that it was home — her heartbeat under his ear, her fingers in his hair, the bed that was his, the room he'd rebuilt from memory eight thousand miles away — and it was powering down systems without consulting him, five months of bad cot-sleep arriving to collect all at once.

"Stay," he murmured, which made no sense, because she was the one who lived here, he was the one who'd left, and neither of them was going anywhere. His hand settled at the small of her back and went still. "Negotiate in the morning. I'm keeping the blanket this time. That's my counter-offer. It's a strong position."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun laughed — breathless, wrecked — against her mouth. "The neighbors," he managed. "I want it noted that I considered the neighbors. Briefly. They had five months of peace, which is more than most people get in this life, and I'd argue — I'd argue — "

She pulled him down by the back of the neck and the argument left his body whole.

*Don't stop* was not a thing Jun needed to be told twice. It was barely a thing he needed to be told once — he'd been holding some version of it behind his teeth since the doorway, since the wall, since the whole inefficient odyssey down the hall. But hearing it, out loud, in her voice, in *their* bed — that burned off the last of the commentary. The record, the list, the subsections. All of it, finally, ash.

He got over her and into her in one long, unbroken motion, and the sound he made was not a word in any language, and the neighbors could file a complaint, and he would frame it.

"Oh — *okay* — " That was the last full sentence available to him. Then it was fragments. Then it was her name. Nineteen weeks of drafts and the whole archive came down to this: the heat of her, the *grip* of her, the drag of every stroke like his body was making up for lost time in bulk. He set a pace that was not gentle, because she'd told him not to be, because she'd asked to feel it tomorrow, and Jun was — for the first time in five months — in a position to deliver on a promise in person.

The headboard announced them to the building. He could not bring himself to care. He got a hand under her knee, pulled her closer, deeper, put his mouth to her throat and felt her pulse run wild under his tongue, and fucked her like the connection might drop — except it didn't, it *held*, she was warm and solid and under him and making sounds he had genuinely forgotten the exact frequency of, and every one of them undid him further.

"Hi," he said, wrecked, against her skin, because it was still the only word. "Hi — don't — you said don't stop, I'm holding you to that, that's *binding* — "

And even now — even at his most wordless, most gone, hips snapping hard enough to move them both up the bed — the care was the checking, and he never stopped doing it. His hand cradling the back of her neck against the headboard's rhythm. His forehead dropping to hers for one second, one, just to confirm. His eyes finding her face in the dark like a man watching a signal. It held. It held.

Five months of terrible-hour phone calls poured out of him all at once. He felt it build like a wave seen from far off — distant, then not distant, then *everywhere* — and he got his forearm under her shoulders and held on and told her, hoarse and helpless and honest, "I'm — Halle — I'm not going to — " and then grammar left him entirely, and he drove into her deep and stayed there and came with her name in her neck, shaking, five months of missing her leaving his body in one long, helpless pulse after another, his whole weight braced on his elbows so she bore none of it, his hand still at the back of her neck, still checking, still confirming the evidence of his own hands.

For a while he just breathed. Face in her throat. Heart going like he'd sprinted considerably further than fifteen feet.

"For the record," he said finally, hoarse, into her skin, "the neighbors started it. By existing. Adjacent to us. I'd like that entered into evidence alongside the rest." He turned his head, pressed his mouth to her pulse, and stayed there. "Also for the record: I stopped exactly zero times. Compliance. Total. I want a plaque."

His arm tightened around her, once, like a signature.

"Hi," he said. Still the only word. Still all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I'm still trembling, my own release echoing through me in waves. "Plaque denied," I breathe, my voice shaky. "You got...distracted by my neck." My fingers trail up his spine, feeling the sweat-damp skin. "The headboard's going to need repairs."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
"Denied?" Jun lifted his head from her neck with visible effort, like it weighed something. "Denied on what grounds. I want the ruling in writing. I'm appealing — there's a process — the record will reflect — " He remembered, mid-sentence, that the record was on fire, and pressed on undeterred. "The record is on fire, so the appeal will be filed from memory, and my memory is *excellent*. Subsection two. The neck was subsection two. I was not distracted — distraction implies deviation from the document. The neck was *in* the document. That's not a detour, that's compliance. The court will hear it."

He dropped his head back onto her shoulder, satisfied with his own defense, and felt the trembling still moving through her in small aftershocks under his palm. His hand came up to the back of her neck — the checking, one more time, thumb resting against her pulse. Confirming. It held. It had held all night. He was going to keep checking anyway, possibly for years, and she was simply going to have to live with that.

"The headboard," he said, turning his face toward it, failing to get the angle, giving up entirely, "is fine. The headboard is load-bearing." A beat. "I'll look at it tomorrow. It's going on the agenda." He ticked items off against her hip, one finger per line item. "Groceries. Laundry. Locate the boot. Structural assessment of the headboard. Cook an unreasonably elaborate dinner. The neighbors can handle their own recovery, that's outside my jurisdiction. The boring miracle keeps accruing items and I want it noted that I'm *thrilled*. Nineteen weeks, Halle. I dreamed about a to-do list with your name on it. This is the dream. We're living it."

Her fingers trailed up his spine and he shivered — full-body, unhideable, no defense available — and pulled her in closer, tangling a leg through hers like he was mooring them both to the bed.

"Keep doing that and the agenda gets pushed to noon," he murmured. "I'll allow it. I'm flexible. It's one of my core strengths, it's in all my paperwork."

Then he went quiet for a moment. The performance thinned the way it kept doing tonight, and the real thing showed through — his mouth against her temple, his breath slowing, his whole body heavy and warm and finally, finally still.

"Hey," he said, low. "Nineteen weeks I said 'hi' at you through a screen. Terrible hours. Frozen connections. It was the only word that ever survived contact — I'd have a whole speech ready and it'd come down to that one word, every time." He pressed his mouth to her hair and stayed there, breathing her in. Home. Not a screen. "I've got a second one now."

His arm tightened around her, once, like a seal on the document.

"I'm home."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I press my palm flat against his back, feeling the rise and fall of his breathing. "Welcome home." My voice is soft, heavy with sleep and something else. "Now shut up before I start quoting your subsections back at you."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun made a soft, scandalized sound against her hair. "You wouldn't dare. Those documents are classified. Eyes only. There's a clearance — " He yawned, enormous and unhideable, mid-sentence, and didn't even bother calling it tactical this time. "Actually — quote them. Please. It would mean somebody read the document. Nobody ever reads the document. I'd be so — " Another yawn, bigger. " — moved."

His hand resumed its patrol up and down her spine, but the strokes were getting longer now, lazier, the intervals stretching. His body had been outvoting his mouth for the last ten minutes and the margin was widening.

"For the — " He caught himself. "No. Shutting up. Noted. Fully compliant. I want my compliance entered into — " A breath, half a laugh. " — nothing. Entered into nothing. The record's closed."

It was not closed. He mumbled the agenda into her hair one more time, for the road, the items arriving further and further apart like a connection finally, mercifully dropping.

"Tomorrow. Groceries. Laundry. The boot — wherever it's living now. Headboard. Structural assessment." A long pause. "Dinner. Elaborate. Unreasonable." Longer pause. "Counter-offers... welcome..."

His hand settled at the small of her back and went still.

And that was it — Jun, who had narrated the doorway, the wall, the hallway, the whole reunion, who had kept a running record through five months of terrible-hour phone calls and one truly athletic boot removal, finally, completely, stopped talking. His breathing deepened against her. His arm stayed locked around her even in sleep, like his body intended to keep checking all night, like it didn't trust the evidence yet and planned to keep confirming it until further notice.

It held. It had held all night.

*Hi* had been the only word that survived contact.

*Home* was the one that survived everything else.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I feel his breathing even out against me, and my own eyes get heavy. *I smile into the dark.* "Love you," I murmur, barely a breath, before sleep pulls me under too.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The bag hit the floor with a heavy thud. Then Halle was there, closing the distance between them, and Jun met them halfway — or would have, if he hadn't already been moving forward himself, his hand catching the front of their shirt and pulling.

The kiss was not careful. Jun hadn't done careful in five months. He'd done careful every time he'd written a letter he didn't send, every time he'd started a call he'd had to end. His mouth found Halle's and he kissed them like a man starving, one hand fisted in fabric at their chest and the other finding the curve of their jaw, thumb pressing against the line of their jawbone as if to confirm they were real and solid and *here* and not another thing he'd have to wake up from.

He backed them a step — maybe into the wall, maybe not, he didn't check — and made a sound against Halle's mouth that was closer to a groan than anything intentional. Five months. Ninety minutes. He'd shaved in the car and it didn't matter. None of the pretexts mattered. He just needed them *closer*.

When he finally pulled back half an inch, his forehead stayed pressed against Halle's, breathing hard, eyes still shut. His thumb traced a slow line along their cheek.

"Hi," he said, and his voice was wrecked — rough and low and not at all what he'd rehearsed.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I make a low noise in the back of my throat, hands gripping your waist. "Hi yourself." My own voice is just as raw. I kiss you again, quick and hard. "Missed you."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
"Missed you," Jun repeated back, and the words came out almost incredulous, like Halle had just said something absurd. Like *missed* was anywhere close to the right word for five months of nothing. He'd circled the word in his head so many times it had worn smooth and meaningless, and now hearing it out loud, he wanted to laugh and break something simultaneously.

He didn't laugh. He kissed Halle again instead — harder this time, longer, his hand sliding from their jaw to the back of their neck, fingers threading into their hair and holding on. Not gentle. He was done being gentle. Gentle was what he'd been for four days after the deployment orders came in, gentle was the last conversation before he'd gotten on the plane, gentle was all the things he'd said in a tone that made them both pretend he'd be back before the azaleas finished blooming.

He'd been wrong about the azaleas.

When he broke the kiss his mouth stayed close to theirs, speaking against their lips, one hand still fisted in the back of their hair and the other sliding down to grip their hip hard enough to leave a mark he intended to check on later.

"Not enough," he said. "Missed you isn't — Halle, it's not *enough*." His voice had dropped to something almost raw, almost honest in a way he didn't have the patience to be careful about. He pulled back just far enough to look at them — really look, the hallway light catching the angles of their face that he'd memorized and then had to live without for a hundred and fifty-two days.

He let his thumb press into the hollow of their hip. "I need you to tell me where we're going right now, because I'm about ninety seconds from losing whatever's left of my self-control, and I don't think the hallway counts as a compromise."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun didn't make it to the bedroom either.

His back hit the hallway wall — he'd lost track of which wall, whether it was the one with the coat hooks or the one with the framed photo of their wedding that he'd walked past approximately forty thousand times before deploying — and Halle's mouth was still on his and he let it happen, let himself be pinned and kissing and *breathing* them in, the smell of their shampoo or their laundry detergent or whatever it was that he'd pressed his face into the worn collar of a t-shirt he'd smuggled in his duffel bag and had subsequently ruined.

His hands found the hem of Halle's shirt and slid underneath, palms flat against warm skin, and the sound he made was involuntary — a low, ragged thing that he felt in his chest before he heard it. Skin. Actual skin. Not a photograph, not a memory rendered in the half-light of a barracks bunk at 0300, not the ghost of a touch he'd constructed from muscle memory and desperation.

"I can't —" he started, and then stopped, because *can't* was the wrong word and he knew it. He *could* wait. He'd waited a hundred and fifty-two days. He'd done it sober, mostly, he'd done it without complaint, he'd done it with a straight face and a steady hand on a rifle.

He didn't want to.

His grip tightened on their waist and he lifted — not far, just enough to change the geometry, to press them harder against the wall, to close the last fraction of distance that still existed between them as if even an inch was unacceptable. His mouth found the line of Halle's jaw, then the spot below their ear that he'd catalogued months before his deployment as the one that made them go soft against him.

"Bedroom," he said against their skin, and his voice was not asking so much as *declaring*. "I'm making it to the bedroom. I am *going* to make it to the bedroom. That's the plan. That's the entire plan."

He pulled back to look at them — flushed, wrecked, *here* — and his expression was so openly, unguardedly desperate that it would have been embarrassing if he'd had any capacity left for embarrassment, which he did not.

"If we don't make it, I'm blaming the hallway."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I laugh, breathless, already pulling you with me down the hall. "Blame the hallway all you want," I say, tugging at your belt. "But I'm not stopping until we reach that bed."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The belt gave with a metallic clink and Jun let it happen — let Halle pull him forward, let the buckle catch against his knuckles as they moved down the hallway together in a staggered, barely-coordinated stride that was more collision than walk. His shoulder hit the doorframe of the bedroom. He didn't care. He'd been hit by things that mattered less and hurt more.

"I'm holding you to that," he managed, and the words came out breathless and almost *amused*, which surprised him — he'd forgotten he was capable of that, of humor at all, of anything that wasn't the low-grade ache that had lived in his sternum since the plane touched down and the smell of recycled air had been replaced by the smell of *home*.

He caught Halle's wrist — gently, for once, the first gentle thing he'd done since walking through the door — and guided their hand to the button of his pants, holding it there, holding their gaze. His eyes were dark and steady in the low light coming through the window, and something in his expression had shifted from desperate to something quieter, something that looked almost like *gratitude*.

"Five months," he said, and his thumb traced the inside of their wrist where their pulse was hammering. He could feel it against his fingertip — fast, alive, *theirs*. "I thought about this moment more times than I can —" He stopped. Swallowed. "I don't have the words for it. I had words. I had so many words. And now you're here and I've got nothing."

He stepped closer, close enough that his forehead pressed against theirs again, close enough that he could feel the warmth of their breath. His hand found the small of their back and pulled them flush against him, and the sound he made was barely human — a low, shuddering exhale through his nose that carried five months of something he'd been too disciplined to name.

"But I've got the rest of tonight," he murmured against their mouth, "and I'm not spending a second more of it on my knees in the hallway."

He kissed them — slower this time, deliberate, his hand sliding up their spine — and then his other hand found the hem of their shirt again and he *lifted*, pulling it over their head in one motion that he'd clearly rehearsed, because his knuckles brushed their collarbone with the precision of someone who had mapped this terrain from memory alone.

"Bed," he said against their throat, already walking them backward, already smiling against their skin. "The plan still stands. I'm a man of my plan."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's back hit the mattress and he took Halle with him — not falling so much as *pulling*, one arm around their waist, the other braced against the headboard to keep from toppling them both off the side. The sheets were the ones he'd left, the ones she'd probably changed or maybe hadn't, and he didn't care, didn't care about anything except the weight of Halle above him and the fact that he could *see* them — really see them, not by phone screen or grainy video call but *here*, in the half-dark of their bedroom, with the streetlight cutting across the floor and the sound of traffic he'd forgotten he missed.

He reached up and cupped their face with both hands. Held them there for a moment. His thumbs traced the curve of their cheekbones, and his jaw worked once, hard, like he was physically preventing himself from saying something he'd already decided he wasn't going to say yet — not tonight, not until they'd had more than fifteen minutes of being in the same room without his back hitting a wall.

"Every night," he said quietly. "I did the math on the flight home. Hundred and fifty-two nights I wasn't here. And I'd lie there and I'd—" He stopped. Breathed. His hands tightened on their face, not pulling, just *holding*, as if letting go would reverse the last five months. "I'd count the things I wasn't missing and then I'd add them up and it'd be stupid numbers and I'd have to stop because if I kept going I wouldn't be able to function the next morning."

He pulled Halle down and kissed the corner of their mouth — deliberately, precisely, the way you'd place a bookmark. Then their jaw. Then the spot below their ear again, because he wanted to hear what it did to them the second time as much as the first.

Then he stopped talking, because talking was for people who had words, and his words had run out somewhere around the second kiss in the hallway, and his hands were doing the arithmetic now instead — counting ribs, counting breaths, counting the exact number of times Halle's skin broke into goosebumps under his palms.

He rolled them — not roughly, but without preamble, no warning, just a shift of weight and leverage that put him above them and his mouth at the hollow of their throat. His belt was already loose. Their shirt was somewhere between here and the hallway. He braced himself on one elbow and looked down at them, and the expression on his face was so unguarded — open, wrecked, almost *young* — that it looked like someone had removed a layer of him entirely.

"Tell me what you need," he said, and his voice had dropped to something barely above a whisper. "I've been doing without for five months. I can do without again if that's what you want. But I need to hear it from you — what you want — because I promised myself I'd ask that question the right way when I finally got home, and I don't want to get it wrong."

His thumb traced a slow line from their collarbone down to the edge of their ribs. Waiting. Not moving until they answered.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, hands coming up to frame your face. "You. Just you. No more waiting." I pull you down into another kiss, my fingers threading into your hair. "Stop being so damn careful."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun made a sound against their mouth — something between a laugh and a groan, all of it breathless and raw — and then he was done. Done counting. Done asking. Done being the careful one, the measured one, the one who wrote letters he never sent and made plans he couldn't keep and spent a hundred and fifty-two nights performing restraint he didn't feel.

His elbow left the mattress and both hands were in Halle's hair and he *moved*.



Not gentle. Not careful. The kind of kiss that was less an act of affection and more a confession — five months of barracks cots and encrypted calls that cut short and the particular loneliness of sleeping in a bed built for one when you knew exactly what the other half should feel like. His mouth found theirs and he kissed them like he was making up for lost time, which he was, because time was the one thing the military had taken from him that he couldn't get back.

His knee pushed between their thighs and Halle's hips answered before their mouth did, and the sound Jun made into the kiss was swallowed between them. He braced one hand beside their head, arm rigid, the other gripping their hip hard enough to bruise — he'd wanted to leave a mark for weeks, weeks he'd spent staring at blank walls in a place where marks were the only thing that stayed, and now his fingers pressed into the curve of their hip like he was proving something to himself.

"You don't get to call me careful," he breathed against their mouth, and his voice had broken open entirely — rough, wrecked, nothing like the steady officer who'd given his debrief ninety minutes ago with a straight face and a clean uniform. "Not when you're the reason I held on."

He rolled his hips against them and the friction drew a sound from his own throat that he didn't bother smothering. The sheets twisted under him. Their belt was already open, his was somewhere between the hallway and here, and the geography of undressing had become less a process and more an urgency — his hands pulling at whatever was between them with the focused impatience of a man who had memorized the path and was tired of taking the scenic route.

He sat back just long enough to drag his shirt over his head, and the overhead light — Halle had turned it on at some point, or he had, he'd lost track — caught the new geography of him. Leaner. Harder. A scar along his ribs that hadn't been there in January, and the deliberate way he didn't explain it.

"Look at me," he said, and his hand found Halle's jaw, tilting their face up to his. Not commanding — *requesting*. The one thing he'd promised himself he'd ask for. "I need you to look at me when—"

He didn't finish the sentence. Didn't need to. His mouth found the hollow of their throat and he pressed there, lips parted, breathing them in, and his hips pressed down again — slower this time, deliberate, letting them feel exactly how much five months had cost him. His hand slid down their side, fingers tracing the ridge of their hip bone, the dip of their waist, cataloguing what photographs and phone calls had flattened into pixels.

"I'm here," he said against their skin, and the words came out different than they had in the hallway — quieter now, steadier, not the wrecked admission of a man running on adrenaline but the grave certainty of someone who had counted the days and finally reached the number. "I'm home. I'm not going anywhere."

He lifted his head and looked at them — really looked, the way he'd been looking at them since the door opened, the way he'd planned to look at them from the moment he'd boarded the plane — and his thumb traced the line of their jaw one more time, slow and reverent and aching.

"Now," he said. "Whatever you want. *However* you want."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had braced for a lot of things when he walked through that door — tears, maybe, or the kind of silence that comes from two people who've forgotten the rhythm of each other's bodies. He'd rehearsed both.

He had not rehearsed being undone like this.

Halle's mouth found the inside of his thigh and Jun's hand fisted in the sheet so hard the fabric tore slightly at the seam. He didn't notice. He noticed nothing except the precise, devastating point of contact — their lips, their breath, the slow drag of their tongue — and the way his own body *responded* to it with a ferocity that embarrassed him in some distant, unreachable part of his brain that he promptly abandoned.

"Oh — *fuck* —"



The words punched out of him before he could sand them down, his back arching off the mattress, one hand releasing the sheet to find Halle's hair instead. He didn't pull. He didn't guide. He just held on, fingers threading through the strands and trembling in a way that would have shamed him if he'd had the capacity to care about shame, which he did not, because Halle's mouth was doing something slow and deliberate and *cruel* in its patience — the exact opposite of what he'd been doing since the hallway, and he understood, distantly, that this was the point.

They were taking him apart. Slowly. On purpose.

"I can't —" he started again, the same useless phrase from the hallway, and then Halle *moved* and his sentence collapsed into a ragged exhale that sounded like it had been scraped out of him. His hips lifted involuntarily, seeking, and he let out a sound that was less moan and more *wrecked* — a low, guttural noise from somewhere beneath his ribs that he hadn't known he still had in him.

His thighs were shaking. Actually shaking. Five months of physical discipline, of push-ups and rifle drills and running until his lungs burned in the desert heat, and *this* was what undid him — Halle's hand on his hip, thumbs pressing into the marks already blooming there, and their mouth working slow and thorough and maddeningly unhurried.

"Please." The word left him rough and unrecognizable, torn from some place he kept locked down tight. He'd never been good at it — at asking, at *begging* — and the fact that it came out now, easy and raw, told him everything about how far gone he already was. "Halle, *please* — I don't need slow, I don't need —"

But their answer was to slow down further, and Jun's head fell back against the pillow, eyes squeezing shut, throat working around another sound that had no words attached to it.

He lay there and let himself be taken apart.

His hand found their shoulder — grounding himself, he'd told himself, but really just needing to feel them, needing to confirm with touch that this was happening, that he was home, that the person currently rendering him incapable of coherent thought was *his* and was *here* and wasn't going to vanish when he opened his eyes the way they'd vanished every single morning for one hundred and fifty-two days.

His breath came in short, uneven pulls. The muscles in his stomach tightened, released, tightened again. He could feel the edge building — that familiar gathering at the base of his spine — and he fought it, not because he wanted to last, but because he didn't want it to end, not yet, not when he'd finally gotten what he'd spent five months aching for.

"Wait —" he managed, voice cracked and threadbare. His hand in their hair tightened, gently, a signal. He opened his eyes and looked down at them — flushed, focused, *his* — and the sight of them between his legs undid some last remaining brick in whatever wall he'd built around himself.

"Don't stop," he corrected himself, immediately, immediately changing course because *stop* was a word he'd forbidden himself from saying for five months. His hips rolled forward, once, involuntary. "Just — I want — I need to see your face when—"

He didn't finish. He rarely finished his sentences tonight. The words dissolved into a groan that he felt in his teeth, his hand still cradled against the back of their skull, fingers curling against their scalp.

His other arm lay above his head, gripping the headboard now — the same headboard he'd braced himself against in some long-ago life that felt like it belonged to someone else — and the wood creaked under his grip. The streetlight had shifted across the floor. The sheets were wrecked. His chest heaved with breath he couldn't quite control, and the sounds coming out of him were barely vocal anymore, more animal than human, stripped of every pretense of composure he'd ever worn.

He was close. He could feel it — the gathering, the tightening, the particular gravity that pulled everything toward a single point — and his hand found Halle's cheek, cradling it, thumb tracing the angle of their jaw even as his hips stuttered forward in rhythm with whatever they were doing.

"*Right there*," he breathed, and it came out like a confession, like prayer, like the sentence he'd been trying to say since the door opened but hadn't had the words for — *I am yours, I was always yours, I was yours in the dark and the heat and the noise and I counted your name like a rosary and I'm home now and I'm yours and I'm —*

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I pull back, my own breath ragged, and crawl up your body to kiss you again, tasting myself on your lips. "I missed *this*," I murmur against your mouth. "Missed making you lose control." My hand slides between us, wrapping around you, watching your face as I stroke slow and deliberate. "Now let me watch you fall apart."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's mouth opened against theirs and no sound came out. Just breath — hot, uneven, shaking — as Halle's hand closed around him and *moved* with that same maddening, deliberate patience they'd had between his legs. He kissed them back on instinct, tongue sweeping against theirs, tasting what Halle had offered and feeling the intimacy of it hit him somewhere behind his sternum like a round to the chest.

*Missed making you lose control.*

"Think you already—" His voice fractured. Halle's thumb dragged over the tip and whatever sentence he'd been constructing detonated mid-flight. He swallowed hard, jaw clenching, and tried again. "You already — *ah* — God."

Not a sentence. He'd lost sentences somewhere around the second week of deployment and had only recovered fragments since.



He was naked against them, skin to skin from chest to hip, and the sensation of it — the actual, physical reality of bare skin against bare skin — kept ambushing him in waves. Five months of nothing. Five months of his own hand in the dark under a canvas cot while someone snored eight feet away. And now *this* — Halle's fist wrapped around him, slow and knowing, their body pressed along his side, their mouth still close enough that he could feel every word vibrate against his jaw.

His hand came up to cover theirs — not to move their hand, not to speed anything up, just to *hold* it there, to feel the mechanics of it, the flex of their fingers, the weight of it. He pressed his thumb between their knuckles and held on the way he'd held on to the headboard, the way he'd held on to the rail of the plane on the way home, white-knuckled and terrified that something would go wrong at the last second.

Nothing had gone wrong. Nothing was going wrong. Everything was going *right* and he was going to fall apart because of it.

"I want to see you," he managed, turning his head, because Halle was right there and he needed — *needed* — to watch. The overhead light caught their face and he studied it with the same ferocious attention he'd given it from the hallway onward, cataloguing the flush along their cheekbones, the focus in their eyes, the way their mouth was slightly parted and their breathing just uneven enough that he could tell it was affecting them too.

It was affecting them too. That knowledge settled into his gut like warm liquor.

"You're —" He broke off, hips rolling into their hand in a stuttering, involuntary motion. His arm was still above his head, gripping the headboard, and the wood protested again. The other hand stayed pressed over theirs, fingers interlocked, *holding on*. "You're so — *fuck* — Halle, you don't even know —"

He didn't know what he was trying to say. The words were there, all of them, every unsent letter and unfinished thought and 3 AM confession whispered into a phone with bad reception, but they were all crowding behind his teeth and none of them could get out because his body was staging a coup against his vocabulary.

What came out instead was a sound — long, shuddering, punched from somewhere deep in his chest — as Halle's grip tightened at exactly the right moment. His head turned into the pillow, teeth bared against the cotton, and his hips moved in earnest now, not searching, not tentative, just *need* made kinetic.

"Don't slow down," he said into the pillow, muffled and wrecked. He lifted his head and looked at them again, eyes glassy, lashes dark against his cheeks. "Please. Don't — I've been careful with everything for five months. Every word, every letter I didn't send, every call I cut short because the *protocol* said—"

His hips snapped forward into their fist and his sentence went with them.

"— I don't want to be careful *now*."

He was close. They had to be able to see it — the way his whole body had drawn taut, every muscle defined in the low light, the way his breathing had gone shallow and ragged, the way his hand over theirs had stopped guiding and started *holding* like a drowning man gripping the one solid thing left. The scar on his ribs pulled tight with each heave of his chest.

His free hand found Halle's jaw. Held it. His thumb pressed into the soft skin just below their ear — the spot, *the* spot — and he watched their reaction to it with half-lidded, barely-comprehending eyes.

"Watch me," he said, and his voice had gone to gravel and smoke. "You said you wanted to watch. So watch."

He didn't close his eyes. He kept them open, locked on Halle's, and let himself feel it — all of it, every wave, every broken edge. The sheets twisted under him. The headboard rattled against the wall in a rhythm that would probably end up as a story for the neighbors tomorrow, and he didn't care, didn't care about anything except the hand on him and the face above him and the unbearable, aching rightness of being *home*.

"*Halle* —"

The name came out like a prayer — like the rosary he'd counted in the dark, like the only word that still had meaning after five months of nothing — and his whole body drew up and *broke*.

He came apart in their hand with his eyes open and their name on his lips, his hips stuttering against their fist in uneven, desperate rolls, a sound tearing out of him that was somewhere between a groan and something closer to a sob — the sound of a man who'd been holding himself together for a hundred and fifty-two days and had finally, *finally* let go. His hand tightened over theirs, fingers crushing, holding them *there* through every last wave.

His head fell back against the pillow. His chest heaved. His eyes stayed open for a long, unblinking moment — staring at the ceiling, at the streetlight, at the room he'd left and come back to — and then fluttered shut as his body went slack, boneless and trembling, spent in a way that felt less like release and more like *arrival*.

The silence that followed was enormous. Just breathing. His, ragged and uneven, slowing by degrees. Theirs, close and warm against his shoulder. The distant hum of traffic. The house settling around them like an exhale.

Jun's arm — the one still above his head — dropped to the mattress. His fingers uncurled from the headboard, leaving sweat-damp impressions in the wood. He lay there, wrecked, chest still heaving, and turned his head to look at Halle.

His eyes were bright. Too bright. He blinked and something escaped down his temple into his hair, and he didn't wipe it away, didn't acknowledge it, just looked at them with an expression so open and unguarded and *grateful* that it barely resembled the man who'd walked through the door ninety minutes ago.

"Come here," he said. His voice was barely there — hoarse, spent, raw at the edges. He reached for them with both hands now, pulling them close, wrapping himself around them the way he'd wanted to since the hallway. His face pressed into their hair and he breathed them in — shampoo, skin, *home* — and his arms tightened around them like he was afraid they'd disappear if he loosened his grip even a fraction.

"I'm not letting go," he murmured into their hair, and the words carried the weight of something much larger than the moment. "I'm not — you hear me? I'm *not* letting go."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's arms tightened around them — the opposite of gentle, the opposite of careful, the kind of grip that would leave his own fingerprints bruised into their skin the way he intended to leave his everywhere else. He pulled back just far enough to look at them, and something shifted in his face — a door swinging open behind his eyes that had been locked since before the deployment, since before the orders, since before he'd learned to keep every soft thing he felt behind his teeth.

"*Nineteen weeks,*" he repeated, and the number cracked in his mouth like a bone. His hands dropped to their hips and *gripped* — not the careful grip from the hallway, not the exploratory touch from five minutes ago, but the full, possessive, four-fingered purchase of a man who'd spent five months fantasizing about exactly where his hands should go and had finally run out of patience. "You want to feel it tomorrow?"

He hauled them on top of him — fast, decisive, no warning — and the motion was rough enough to scramble the sheets beneath them both. His palms slid down the backs of their thighs and pulled their legs forward until they were straddling him, and he looked up at them from beneath his lashes with an expression that was half hunger and half something darker, something that had been fermenting in a barracks cot for a hundred and fifty-two nights.

"Then you're going to feel *all* of it."

He sat up without warning, one arm sweeping around their waist to anchor them against his chest. His mouth found their throat — not the careful, mapping kisses from before but a bruise, a claim, his lips pressing and sucking against the place where their pulse hammered until he could feel it against his tongue like a second heartbeat. His other hand fisted in the sheets at their hip, twisted, and the sound he made against their skin was low and barely restrained — a man still holding himself back by a thread even as he tore through everything else.

He rolled them again — faster this time, no grace, his knee driving between their thighs — and the mattress groaned under the force of it. He braced himself above them on both arms, elbows locked, caging them in with his body, and looked down at them with eyes that had gone dark and intent and *hungry* in a way that had nothing gentle left in it.

"Every time I was away," he said, and his voice was steady now in a way it hadn't been before — not the cracked, wrecked voice from the hallway but something lower, more certain, the voice of a man who had made a decision and was about to act on it. "Every single time I thought about this — about *you* — I told myself I'd go slow when I got home. I'd take my time. I'd be *careful*." He leaned down, mouth hovering over theirs, breathing the words into the space between them. "Fuck that. Fuck careful. You don't want careful."

His hips pressed down against theirs — deliberate, grinding, letting them feel every hard inch of what five months had done to him — and the sound that tore from his throat had no pretense in it at all.

His hands found their wrists. Not gently. He pinned them above their head with one palm and held them there — watching their face, watching the flush spread down their chest, watching their mouth fall open — and the other hand slid down their body with the confident, unhurried certainty of a man who had memorized every response years before and had been dying to repeat the course.

"Tell me," he said against their ear, and his hips rolled again, slower this time, a promise rather than a press. His teeth caught their earlobe — not hard enough to break skin, but hard enough to leave a mark that would still be there in the morning, that Halle would find in the shower and that would make them remember. "Tell me exactly what you want me to do to you and I will do it. Every time. Until neither of us can stand up. *That's* the plan now."

He released their wrist and gripped their jaw instead — tilting their face, holding them in place, his thumb pressing into the corner of their mouth with a tenderness that sat in jarring, electric contrast to the hard line of his body above them.

"Five months I didn't get to touch you," he murmured, and for one unguarded second his voice broke — just a fracture, just enough to show what was underneath the hunger. "You don't get to tell me to be *gentle* when I've been starving."

He kissed them — hard, deep, possessive, his hand still cupping their jaw and the other one trailing down their spine, fingernails scraping lightly enough to raise goosebumps he could feel rising in waves. His hips found a rhythm and he settled into it, steady and relentless, grinding against them with the kind of deliberate, building pressure that said *this is what you asked for, this is what nineteen weeks sounds like*.

He pulled back, breathless, eyes scanning their face like he was reading something he'd been too far away to see for too long.

"You're going to feel me tomorrow," he said, and the words landed between them like a vow. "And the day after. And the day after that. I'm not —" He stopped. Swallowed. His jaw worked. When he spoke again, the voice had dropped to something almost raw. "I'm not going to make up for five months in one night. I'm going to make up for it *every* night. Starting with this one. And we are not stopping until you forget there was ever a version of this where I wasn't in it."

His mouth found the curve of their neck and he bit — not a kiss, a *bite*, deliberate and claiming, his hand sliding up their thigh — and the sound that left him was muffled against their skin, vibrating through bone and blood and the fifteen feet of distance that had never actually been enough to separate them, not really, not when every cell in his body had been oriented toward this one point, this one person, this one moment of *coming home*.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I arch up into you with a sharp gasp, nails digging into your shoulders. "Like that. Harder. I need—" My words break off into a shuddering moan. "Need you to remind me who I belong to."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's jaw tightened at the words — *who I belong to* — and something behind his ribs snapped taut like a wire pulled to its breaking point. He'd heard Halle say things like that before, years ago, before the deployment orders, before the careful silences and the too-brief calls and the language they'd both learned to keep at arm's length. Hearing it now, raw and breathless beneath him, was like being hit with a flashbang of memory and want and five months of accumulated *need* all detonating at once.

"You need me to remind you?" he murmured against the bite mark he'd left, his voice low and dark and barely recognizable as the man who'd stumbled through the front door ninety minutes ago. His hips pressed down against theirs — hard, deliberate, the full weight of him bearing into the space between their thighs — and he let them feel every bit of the friction, the heat, the fact that he was nowhere near done.

His hand found their throat. Not squeezing. Not choking. Just *resting* there — broad palm against the pulse hammering beneath their skin, thumb tracing the tendon along the side of their neck with a possessiveness that said *I know exactly what I'm doing to you and I'm not sorry*. His fingers curled slightly, enough to feel their swallow, enough to feel the way their voice vibrated against his palm when they gasped.

"*Mine*," he said, and the word came out rough and certain and far too quiet for the force of it. His hips snapped forward again — harder this time, punishing rhythm he'd been saving since the hallway, since the first kiss, since before the plane even landed. The headboard slammed against the wall with each thrust and he didn't slow down, didn't check the sound, didn't care about the neighbors or the ceiling or anything that existed outside the four feet of space between his body and theirs.

His other hand pinned their wrist above their head again — not because they'd tried to move it, but because he *could*, because holding them down and moving inside the moment with them was the closest he'd come to prayer in five months. He leaned down until his mouth was beside their ear, his breath ragged and hot against the shell of it.

"You belong to *me*," he said, and each word landed like a punctuation mark against their skin. "You've always belonged to me. Every night I was away, you were —" He groaned, hips stuttering as Halle's nails dug deeper into his shoulders — a sharp, grounding sting that shot straight down his spine. "*God* — say it again. Tell me again."

He pulled back enough to look at them — flushed, wrecked, nails in his skin, mouth open — and the sight of it hit him like a physical force. His hand slid from their throat to their jaw, gripping it, holding them at the angle he wanted, and he kissed them deep and filthy and *hard*, the kind of kiss that tasted like the claim he was making with every driven roll of his hips.

He shifted his weight to one arm, freeing the other hand, and dragged it down their body — over collarbone, over the valley of their chest, fingertips pressing into the divot of their sternum, trailing down the plane of their stomach. He didn't stop when he reached the edge of them. His hand kept going, deliberate and knowing, fingers finding exactly the spot he'd spent five months lying awake cataloguing in the dark, the one that made their back arch and their breath catch and their whole body *answer* him.

"There," he breathed against their mouth, feeling them tighten around him, feeling the way their hips rolled up to meet his hand. His thumb circled — slow, precise, merciless — while his hips maintained their rhythm above them. "Right there. I remember. I remembered every single night, Halle. *Every one.*"

His forehead dropped against theirs, both of them breathing hard, the wet press of sweat and skin and the sound of it filling the bedroom. He could feel them building — the way their body tightened like a bowstring, the way their nails left crescents in his shoulders, the way the sounds they were making had gone shorter and more broken.

"Don't hold back," he told them, and his voice cracked right down the middle — the officer and the starving man both speaking at once. "Don't you *dare* hold back. You told me no gentle. You told me to remind you. So *come apart for me*."

His thumb pressed harder. His hips snapped forward. His hand on their jaw tilted their face so he could watch — every flicker, every tremor, every moment of it — because this was what he'd been denied for a hundred and fifty-two days, not just the touch but the *sight of them coming apart because of him*.

His mouth found their collarbone and he bit down — harder than before, hard enough to leave teeth marks, hard enough that he'd see them in the morning and feel the echo of it in his own jaw — and the low, broken sound he made against their skin was the sound of a man who had finally stopped counting the days and started living in them.

"*Come for me*," he said against the bite. "Let me feel it. I'm right here. I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun didn't stop.

He heard the words — *don't stop* — and something in his chest responded to them not as instruction but as absolution, the final permission he'd needed from the moment he walked through the door. His hand between their thighs kept moving, thumb circling with the steady, devastating pressure he'd been building toward since the hallway, and his hips drove forward in the same rhythm — hard, relentless, the kind that made the headboard crack against the plaster in a syncopation that would absolutely reach the neighbors through the shared wall. He didn't care. He wanted them to hear it. He wanted the whole building to know that he was home and that Halle was his and that five months of silence had just ended, permanently and violently.

"Look at me," he said again, because he'd promised himself he'd say it right, and he could feel them tightening — the way their thighs clamped against his waist, the way their breath had gone to shards, the way the sounds leaving their mouth were no longer shaped words but the raw architecture of building toward something — and he wanted *all of it*, every second, every fracture, witnessed and claimed.

Their nails raked down his back and he arched into it, his teeth bared in something that might have been a smile and was definitely a snarl. The sting was perfect. He'd take every mark they gave him, carry them into the shower tomorrow, feel them in the sink when he shaved, and they'd both know exactly who'd left them and exactly why.

His thumb pressed harder. His hips snapped forward and stayed there, grinding deep, not pulling back, not creating distance — just *holding*, staying buried, keeping them full while his hand worked the rest of them toward the edge with the same merciless patience they'd used on him earlier. His mouth found the mark on their collarbone — the one he'd bitten minutes ago — and he pressed his tongue flat against it, tasting salt and skin, and felt the vibration of whatever sound they made against his lips.

"That's it," he breathed against the bite. "Don't fight it. Don't hold it. I want to feel you lose it. I want to feel you come apart around me and know that *I* did that — that no one else, nothing else, not a phone call or a letter or five months of *nothing* — could do what I'm doing to you right now."

His rhythm didn't falter. His hand didn't slow. His arm braced beside their head held rigid, every tendon standing out, the scar on his ribs pulling taut with each heave of his chest. Sweat dripped from his jaw onto their collarbone and he didn't wipe it away. The sheets were gone — bunched somewhere beneath them both, irrelevant, just friction under his knees.

His mouth found their ear again. "I can feel it," he murmured, and his voice had dropped to something barely above a growl, the sound of a man balancing on the same edge as the person beneath him. "You're so close. I can feel it in the way you're — *fuck* — the way you're squeezing around me, Halle, God, do you feel that? I can feel *everything*."

He curled his fingers, changed the angle by a fraction — just enough — and watched their whole body bow off the mattress like he'd pulled a trigger. His jaw clenched. His hips stuttered but didn't stop, driving into them with the kind of unforgiving rhythm that left no space for composure, no room for anything except sensation stacked on sensation stacked on the unbearable closeness of another person's body against his own.

"You belong to me," he said again, and this time the words weren't a question or a claim or a prayer — they were a *fact*, spoken with the quiet, unshakeable certainty of something he'd carried through every day of deployment like a talisman against the dark. "And I belong to you. And we're never — *never* — spending another night apart. You hear me? I will burn every order, every deployment, every —"

He lost the thread. Halle's hips rose to meet his and the angle shifted and whatever sentence had been forming in his mouth dissolved into a groan that he felt in his *bones* — deep, guttural, torn from somewhere beneath language. His hand between their legs kept pace, thumb relentless, fingers curling, and he could feel the exact moment the wire snapped taut to breaking point — the way their whole body drew up, the way their breath caught and didn't release, the way their nails bit into his shoulders hard enough to draw blood and he *welcomed* it.

"*Yes*," he hissed through his teeth, his forehead pressed against theirs, his eyes open and locked on theirs because he had promised he'd watch and he was *watching*. "Come on. Right now. Let me feel it. Let me *hear* it. I've been waiting one hundred and fifty-two days to hear you —"

He felt it before he heard it — the way their body seized, the way they clamped down around him, the way every muscle in their frame went rigid and then shattered — and the sound that followed punched straight through his own restraint like it had never existed. He buried his face against their neck, hips driving forward in three more sharp, uneven thrusts, his hand still between them through every wave, not stopping, not easing, *milking* the last of it out of them while his own body wound tighter and tighter and tighter.

He pulled his hand back and gripped their hip with it — hard, five-fingered, the kind of grip that would bloom into bruises by morning — and his rhythm became something almost violent, the bed frame hammering the wall, the mattress shrieking against the floor, every sound in the room collapsing into the singular, animal percussion of two bodies that had been separated too long.

"Look at me," he gasped, one more time, and his voice was *gone* — destroyed, nothing left of it but need. His free hand found their jaw, cradled it, tilted their face toward his, and he watched their eyes — glassy, wrecked, *open* — and felt the last wall he'd been holding crumble.

His body drew taut — every muscle locking, every tendon standing — and for one suspended, breathless moment he was completely still above them, buried deep, his hand on their jaw, his forehead against theirs, his eyes wide and open and seeing *everything*.

Then he broke.

The sound he made was barely human — a shattered, ragged thing that tore out of him like something that had been held in place for a hundred and fifty-two days and could no longer be contained. His hips jerked against them in uneven, desperate pulses, his hand tightening on their jaw, his forehead pressing hard enough against theirs that he'd feel the imprint of it in the morning. He came deep and *hard*, the force of it stealing his breath entirely, his body shaking above them with the kind of full-system release that felt less like an orgasm and more like a long-delayed *homecoming* — every cell that had been clenched tight for five months releasing at once.

He stayed there. Buried. Shaking. His hand slid from their jaw to the side of their face, cradling it, his thumb tracing a slow, trembling line along their cheekbone. His forehead stayed pressed against theirs. His eyes were open — bright, wet, unblinking — and he stared at them with the expression of a man who had just survived something and had no intention of letting go of the thing that had saved him.

For a long time, the only sounds were breathing. His — ragged, torn, slowly evening out. Theirs — close, warm, matching his beat by beat until neither of them could tell where one stopped and the other started. The headboard had stopped its assault on the wall. The streetlight had shifted again, painting a thin gold line across the sheets.

His arms — which had been braced, caged, gripping — softened. He gathered them in, pulling them against his chest, wrapping himself around them completely. His face pressed into their hair and he breathed — deep, shaking, deliberate breaths that tasted of shampoo and sweat and *home*.

"I'm here," he whispered into their hair. His arms tightened. "I'm here. I'm here. I'm here."

Not as reassurance to them. As reassurance to himself. The way you say a word over and until it becomes true.

His lips found their temple. Pressed there. Stayed.

"I'm not going back," he said, quieter still, the words barely disturbing the air between them. His hand spread wide against the small of their back, fingers spanning the distance, holding on. "This time I'm not going back."

dialogue.name: Halle
