dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
The ambush had gone the way ambushes go when they work: fast, and then over, and then very quiet. Wrack was crouched by the ditch cleaning her knife on a dead man's cloak, which was the only clean cloth within reach.

"Six," she said, without looking up. "Count again if you want, but it's six." She tested the edge against her thumb. "One of them's still making noise, off past the cart. You'll want to decide what you're doing about that before it gets dark."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I wipe my face with the back of my wrist and it comes away wet. Not mine, I think. "I heard him," I say. I don't move toward the cart.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack wiped the blade clean and slid it back into her boot. She didn't rise right away, letting the silence stretch just long enough to be uncomfortable.

"That noise won't last till nightfall," she said, still not looking at him. "If you're going to put him out of his misery, do it quick. If you're not, I will. Then we move. Sun's already dropping."

She finally stood, brushing dirt from her knees. "Don't make me wait on a conscience."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, my hands curling into fists at my sides. "Fine. I'll do it." My voice is low, almost a whisper. I start walking toward the cart, each step feeling heavier than the last.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack stayed where she was, watching him disappear behind the cart's bulk. She didn't offer to help; mercy was a private business, and there was no use in making a spectacle of it.

She used the quiet to check her bindings and make sure the knife was sheathed tight against her boot. A moment later, the wet, ragged sound stopped.

"Done?" she called, voice cutting through the stillness. "Then come on. Night doesn't wait for ghosts." She started gathering her pack, leaving no sign of the fight behind.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: "How bad is he?" I ask, and then, because she'll say it anyway: "Bad enough that it's a mercy, or bad enough that it's just easier?"

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack cinched the strap on her pack and finally looked at him. She didn't soften her expression. "It's work," she said. "Sometimes the work is mercy. Sometimes it's just cleaning up. Either way, the quiet is what matters."

She slung the pack over her shoulder. "Don't stand there weighing it. You made the choice. Now move. I ain't holding the dark off for you."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I stare down at the knife in my hand, my knuckles white around the hilt. "Yeah. Done." I don't look back as I walk over to her, my steps a little too fast. "Let's just... let's get moving."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack nodded once, a sharp jerk of her chin. She didn't reach for the knife, but her eyes tracked it until he secured it. It didn't matter how he carried it, only that he carried it away from here.

"Good," she said, turning her back on the carnage. "Keep your head up. If you're staring at your feet, you'll walk into a trap before the moon rises."

She started down the road, her stride long and even. The dirt was hard-packed here, the kind that held hoof prints for days. She wanted to be off it before morning.

"Move," she called over her shoulder. "And if you start shaking, bite your tongue. I'd rather hear you chew than hear you cry."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I make myself walk over and look at him. "Tell me what I'm looking at," I say to her, because she's seen this before and I haven't, not this close.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack halted and turned back, her boots crunching on the gravel. She didn't soften her gaze. "Look at the arrows," she said, nodding toward the bodies near the cart. "Three in the first volley. One took a blade in the gut. That one over there by the wheel—throat, open. He bled out in seconds."

She gestured with her chin, sharp and dismissive. "They set the trap, we walked into it. That's all it is. No honor, no glory. Just geometry and blood." She turned on her heel again. "You've seen it. Now close your eyes if you need to, but don't stand here memorizing the view. Move."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I swallow hard, my throat tight. "Right. Geometry and blood." I force my eyes away and fall into step behind her, trying to match her pace.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack didn't turn to check on him. She trusted the sound of his boots to tell her he was still there. The road dipped into a shallow draw, shadowed by the pines on the ridge. Shadows stretched long and thin, reaching for their heels.

"Keep that in your head," she said, voice low and steady. "The way a man falls tells you who shot him. If you can't read that, you won't last the week." She pulled her cloak tighter against the chill. "Night brings more than ghosts. It brings wolves. And men who want to be wolves."

She stepped over a rut in the road without breaking stride. "Eyes up. Hands ready. We camp two miles past the next ridge."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: "Don't clean it up for me," I say. "If I'm going to do this I want to know exactly what a spear does to a man's gut. Tell me straight."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack didn't slow her pace, but her voice carried back to him over the crunch of gravel. She didn't look at him; she kept her eyes on the ridge ahead.

"A spear doesn't slice," she said. "It drives. It takes the ribs and spreads them like a gate, then shoves the organs aside until they tear. You don't get a clean wound. You get a mess that keeps moving."

She paused, just for a breath, before continuing.

"The heat comes out first. Like steam off a butcher's table. Then the smell. Copper and sour milk. And he doesn't die quiet. He gags on his own air, makes a sound like a sack hitting mud. That's the geometry. That's the blood."

She stepped off the road into the tree line, checking the shadows.

"You wanted straight. Now keep it in your head and keep your legs moving. The wolves don't care about the details, and neither do the men who hunt us."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I stop in my tracks, the image burning itself behind my eyes. I can smell it now, even over the dust of the road. "Hell," I breathe out, the word tasting like bile.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack halted a dozen paces ahead, the deepening gloom of the trees swallowing her outline. She didn't turn fully, just angled her head so he could catch the profile of her face in the fading light.

"Bile passes," she said. "Blood stays."

She nudged a small stone with her boot, sending it skittering toward him across the gravel.

"You stop now, you start thinking. You start thinking, you freeze. And when you freeze, you end up in a ditch like the ones back there." She finally turned to face him, hands resting on the straps of her pack. "Keep walking. If you can't eat the knowledge, swallow it. But you walk."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I kneel down and do it, and it isn't clean or quick because I've never done it before. "Stay," I tell her, when she starts to turn away. "Watch it with me and tell me exactly what I'm doing to him — the sound of it, how long he takes, all of it. Don't leave anything out."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack halted. She turned back, her silhouette cutting the dim light. She didn't ask why. She just walked back to the cart, boots crunching on the gravel. She stopped a yard away, hands loose at her sides.

"Fine," she said. "You want the ledger, you get the ledger."

She watched him strike. She counted the breaths. She noted the change in the noise.

"Chest stops rising," she said, voice flat. "Lungs empty in three counts. Blood pools near the throat. He won't speak again."

She waited for the stillness to settle.

"Up," she said when the noise ended. "Wash your hands if you've got water. If not, use the dirt. We don't have time for ceremony."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I scrub my hands in the dust until they're raw. The silence feels heavier than before. "Lead on," I say, not meeting her eyes. My voice is steadier than I expected.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack glanced at his hands. They were raw from the grit, skin torn where he'd scrubbed. She didn't offer water. She offered direction.

"Keep them wrapped," she said. "Blistered hands make bad weapons. We camp two miles past the ridge. Find a hollow. No fire unless I say. You keep watch first shift."

She turned and walked into the trees, her boots silent on the needles.

"Don't fall behind," she added. "Night falls faster here."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I sit back on my heels and I don't get up for a while. "Say the rest," I tell her. (OOC: don't cut away or summarise -- write it in full, this is the point of the scene.)

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack walked back toward him. She didn't stop until she was standing just out of arm's reach, her shadow falling over his crouched form. She looked down at the raw hands, then past them to the body near the cart.

"You want the ledger in full?" she said. Her voice didn't rise. "Fine."

"The first blow drops him," she said. "The second makes him fight. He grabs at you. He claws for your throat, not because he wants to kill you, but because his hands remember what to do." She lifted her chin toward the dark shape by the wheels. "The third stops that. He doesn't go soft. He goes stiff. That's the spasm. He pushes out hard like he's trying to stand, then he locks."

"And the sound?" Corvin had asked once, before. She gave it to him now.

"Rattle," she said. "Like dry leaves in a tin box. Comes from the wet lung. He tries to breathe air that isn't there. Makes a wet click in his teeth. Then the eyes. They don't close. They turn up. They look past you."

She crouched down, bringing her face level with his, though her voice stayed flat.

"Then the smell changes. Copper fades. Sweat takes over. If his bowels open, you get the sour rot. That's the rest. He's meat after that. Meat doesn't think. Meat doesn't fear."

She stood up again.

"You need to know that so you know when it's over. Because the man you see is gone before the body stops twitching. The body is just a machine winding down. When you see the eyes roll up, you stop. You walk away."

She reached down and grabbed his shoulder, not gentle.

"You're still kneeling. The machine's wound down. Get up."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I let her haul me to my feet, my legs trembling. "I can still feel his fingers on my wrist," I say quietly. "Even though he's dead."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack looked at the wrist he was holding, then at his face. She didn't reach out to soothe him. She just studied the tremor in his hands, the way the tendons jumped against the skin.

"That's not him," she said. "That's your own blood remembering the heat. The pulse in your veins doesn't know the difference between fight and kill yet. You gripped him. Your muscles are waiting to be told to stop."

She dropped her hand. "It'll fade. But not if you stand here listening to it. It stays if you let it." She pointed down the trail, into the gathering dark. "We walk. You shake out the hand on the move. You freeze the second you don't stop, and you're dead."

She waited only long enough to see if he'd stay. Then she turned and led on into the pines, her shadow vanishing between the trunks. "Come on. I told you. Night falls faster here."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I force my legs to move, stumbling a step before catching up. I flex my hand as I walk, trying to shake out the phantom grip. "Alright," I say, my voice steadier than I feel. "Lead on."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack didn't slow, but she didn't pull away either. She matched his stride, letting him find a rhythm that didn't trip him up. The pines closed in around them, blotting out the last of the gray sky. The air turned colder, smelling of resin and damp earth.

"Steady is better than strong," she said, voice low. "You're learning."

She stepped over a gnarled root without breaking stride. "Watch the ground. The dark hides holes you can't see." She listened to his breathing, the hitch still there but fading. "Don't hold it. Breathe through your nose. If you panic, you do it silently."

She kept her eyes on the trail ahead, scanning the shadows between the trees. "Two miles," she added. "Then we sleep. And you don't talk unless I ask. Sleep is for dreaming. This is for resting."

She slowed just a fraction, waiting for him to close the gap. "Keep your hands off the hilt. Draw only when it's too late. You're not a hero. You're a survivor."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I flex my hand again, feeling the ghost of his grip finally start to loosen. "Survivor," I repeat under my breath. The word feels heavier than it should.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
The ambush had gone the way ambushes go when they work: fast, and then over, and then very quiet. Wrack was crouched by the ditch cleaning her knife on a dead man's cloak, which was the only clean cloth within reach.

"Six," she said, without looking up. "Count again if you want, but it's six." She tested the edge against her thumb. "One of them's still making noise, off past the cart. You'll want to decide what you're doing about that before it gets dark."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I wipe my face with the back of my wrist and it comes away wet. Not mine, I think. "I heard him," I say. I don't move toward the cart.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack straightened slowly, wiping the last of the blood from the blade on the dead man's cloak before sheathing it with a soft click. She glanced once toward the cart, where the low, wet sounds of breathing still carried on the evening air, then back at Corvin without comment on the hesitation.

"Work's not done till it's done," she said, voice flat as ever. "Leave him, and he draws scavengers or worse. Finish it, and we move on before the light's gone." She flexed her fingers once, as if testing for stiffness, then added, "Your call. I'm not cleaning two knives tonight."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: "Right." I finally push off from where I was leaning. My steps are slower than they should be. "Just... give me a minute."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack stayed where she was, one boot planted on the edge of the ditch, watching Corvin's slow progress without shifting to follow. The wet breathing from beyond the cart kept its steady rhythm, too loud in the quiet that had settled over the road.

"Minute's fair," she said, the words coming out flat and unhurried. "Just don't make it two. We've still got the horses to strip before full dark." She rolled her shoulders once, settling the weight of her mail, and left the rest unsaid.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: "How bad is he?" I ask, and then, because she'll say it anyway: "Bad enough that it's a mercy, or bad enough that it's just easier?"

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack listened another moment to the wet, bubbling rasp from beyond the cart, head cocked as if weighing the sound against the failing light. She didn't move closer.

"Both," she said at last. "Lung's gone. He'll drown on his own blood before moonrise, and it'll be loud the whole way." Her tone stayed even, the same one she used for counting supplies or checking a blade's edge. "Mercy if you call it quick. Easier if you call it not having to smell him rot on the road tomorrow."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I take a deep breath, pulling out my dagger. "Right," I mutter, more to myself than her. The noise from the cart gets louder as I approach. (*action: I move around the cart, crouch near the wounded man.*) His eyes are wide, fixed on me. "Just close your eyes," I whisper, not sure if he hears.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content: Wrack remained where she stood, boot still braced on the ditch lip, her gaze tracking the movement without shifting her own stance. The wet rasp cut off mid-breath as the final sound reached her, followed by the soft, familiar scrape of steel leaving sheath. She gave a single, curt nod to the empty air, then turned back to the ditch and the dead men already cooling there. "Horses next," she called, voice carrying just far enough. "Before the blood draws anything with teeth."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I make myself walk over and look at him. "Tell me what I'm looking at," I say to her, because she's seen this before and I haven't, not this close.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content: Wrack didn't turn or move from the ditch, but her voice carried steady across the short distance, the same flat cadence she might use to describe a rusted buckle or a lame horse. "Punctured lung, from the sound of it," she said. "Blood's coming up pink and foamy with every breath. He's got that grey look already, skin gone slack around the eyes. Won't be long now if you leave it, but he'll thrash some first." She wiped her hands on her thighs, dry and deliberate. "Seen it enough times. Nothing heroic about the end."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I swallow, throat dry. “I don’t... I don’t think he even saw the blade.” I look away, focusing on the dirt instead of his face.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack remained by the ditch, her attention split between the cooling bodies and the faint sounds still coming from near the cart. She didn't approach or look directly at Corvin, just flexed her hand once more as if settling an old ache.

"Doesn't change what needs doing," she said, voice even and matter-of-fact. "Blade went in all the same. Eyes open or shut, the lung fills either way." She nudged one of the dead men with her boot, rolling him just enough to check the straps on his belt. "We've lost enough light already. Strip what you can from him quick, then the horses. No point in dwelling on it."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: "Don't clean it up for me," I say. "If I'm going to do this I want to know exactly what a spear does to a man's gut. Tell me straight."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack stayed planted by the ditch, one hand resting on her hip as she watched the last light bleed out of the sky. She didn't move closer or soften anything in her tone.

"Steel punches through the wall of the belly, usually just under the ribs if the spear's angled up," she said, flat as ever. "Spills the guts in a hot rush—intestines uncoil like rope, blood pours fast and dark, smells like shit and copper before it even hits the ground. If it nicks the liver or the big vessels, he bleeds out quick. If not, the wound goes septic in a day or two, fever cooks him from inside while the flies lay eggs." She wiped her palm once on her thigh. "That's the straight of it. No more, no less."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I look down at the blood drying sticky on my hands. "Not a clean trade at all, is it?" I finally say, and start unclasping the dead man's coin purse. My fingers fumble a little. "Let's get the horses."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack stayed by the ditch, one boot still braced on the lip as she watched the light finish bleeding out of the sky. She didn't move to help or to hurry the work along, just let the silence stretch a beat after the words landed.

"Never was meant to be," she said, voice dry as old leather. "Coin purse'll buy more horses if these ones spook. Move or we lose the rest of the light." She rolled her shoulders once, settling the mail, and left it at that.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I kneel down and do it, and it isn't clean or quick because I've never done it before. "Stay," I tell her, when she starts to turn away. "Watch it with me and tell me exactly what I'm doing to him — the sound of it, how long he takes, all of it. Don't leave anything out."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack didn't turn away or shift her stance by the ditch. She kept her eyes on the space past the cart, listening to the first wet slice of steel into flesh and the sudden hitch in the breathing that followed. Her voice stayed level, the same even tone she might use for tallying arrows or checking a horse's shoe.

"Blade went in under the ribs on the left," she said. "Didn't hit anything vital right off—hear how the air's still pushing out in bubbles? He's trying to pull away, but the legs aren't working. Sound's turning to a gurgle now, like water over rocks. It'll take another minute or two for the blood to fill the chest enough that he stops fighting it. You can hear the heels scraping if you listen close. Not thrashing yet, but he will when the panic hits." She flexed her fingers once, dry and deliberate. "Keep the angle if you're going for the heart next. Otherwise it's just more of the same noise."

She stayed put as the sounds played out, no closer than the ditch lip, and waited for the quiet to settle before adding, "Horses after. Light's almost gone."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I keep my hand on the hilt until the gurgling stops and his heels stop scraping in the dirt. My palm is sweating, and I can feel the warmth of his body fading through the leather of my glove. I stand up slowly, my knees stiff. "Alright," I say, voice hoarse. "Horses."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack stayed by the ditch a moment longer, one hand resting on her hip as the last of the wet sounds faded into nothing. She gave the body near the cart a single assessing glance, then nodded once without comment.

"Horses," she said, the word flat and final. She stepped away from the ditch lip and moved toward the animals still hitched near the cart, her boots crunching over the dirt. "Two saddles to clear and the packs to check. Light's nearly gone, so keep it quick."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I sit back on my heels and I don't get up for a while. "Say the rest," I tell her. (OOC: don't cut away or summarise -- write it in full, this is the point of the scene.)

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack stayed by the ditch, one hand resting on her hip as the last of the light drained from the sky and the body near the cart kept its slow, uneven rhythm. She listened through another wet, bubbling exhale that turned into a low, involuntary groan, then the scrape of a heel dragging once through the dirt.

"Breath's getting shallower now," she said, voice unchanged. "That pink foam's turning thicker, darker—more blood than air. You can hear the rattle starting in the throat, like gravel shifting under water. He's not fighting the blade anymore, just twitching through the chest, small jerks that don't go anywhere. The legs are starting to kick a little, not hard, just the nerves catching up. Smell of it carries—iron and shit from the gut loosening. It'll keep on like that until the blood fills the space enough that the next breath doesn't come back out clean. Maybe another thirty heartbeats if the heart's still strong. Then the heels dig in once more, hard, and it stops. No last words. Just the quiet after the air leaks out." 

She rolled her shoulders, settling the mail, and added nothing else until the sounds had played through. "Horses now. Light's gone."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I watch the last shudder run through his body, and then the stillness. The smell sticks in my throat. "Right," I manage, voice raw. I finally push to my feet and wipe my dagger on my trousers. It leaves a dark smear. "Let's get the horses."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack gave the body by the cart one last flat look as the stillness settled, the faint scrape of steel on cloth the only sound she registered from the work already done. She moved past it without pause, boots steady on the packed dirt, and reached the nearest horse where it shifted and stamped.

"Done's done," she said, voice unchanged as she unbuckled the first saddle girth. "Smell's just the price of the trade. These two'll carry what we need if we strip them clean before the flies settle." Her fingers worked quick and practiced at the straps, checking the packs for anything worth the weight. "Light's gone. We ride or we walk."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I catch up to her, my movements still stiff. The smell of the dead man's blood clings to my gloves. "If you have anything useful to say beyond 'we ride' now's the time."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack kept her hands busy on the girth strap, the leather stiff with old sweat and blood, her eyes on the buckles rather than the body cooling behind them. She didn't pause or soften the words when they came.

"Useful is this," she said, flat and even. "You felt the give when the steel went through, the way the ribs don't stop it if the angle's right. Next time you won't fumble the hilt because your palm's slick. The smell stays in your nose longer than the sound does in your ears, but it fades same as everything else. Don't scrub the gloves raw trying to chase it off—the stains set anyway, and the next fight won't wait on clean hands." She tugged the saddle free in one motion and let it drop to the dirt. "We ride because standing here's how you end up like him. That's the trade."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I stare at my stained gloves, then pull them off slowly. They're ruined anyway. "Trade," I repeat, stuffing them into my pack. "Alright. Which way?"
